*The Survival of Sarah Rose is an epic fantasy game. Production on TSSR is still ongoing.*
*What you are about to play is a work-in-progress.*
*If you enjoy the work and wish to support us, please consider joining us on patreon.com/HappyDaedalus.*
*TSSR takes place in a dark fantasy setting.*
*The events and stories depicted within, while fictional, may be triggering to some audiences.*
*Castle Reinmeer*
*The great castle rests at the heart of the nation of Rosanna.*
*For centuries, it has been the home of the Rose family.*
*Ruling with both wisdom and strength, the Rose family ensured centuries of prosperity for the nation of Rosanna.*
*But nothing lasts forever and rumors of new dangers have begun to spread.*
*An ambitious warlord to the east threatens war.*
*Something has begun to stir the hearts of all creatures wicked.*
*But perhaps most dangerous of all, enemies are rising from within Rosanna.*
*Some wear their threats on their sleeves, whilst others hide their intentions behind smiling faces.*
*The Rose family can feel it in the air...*
*Danger.*
*Amidst these many dangers, Sarah Rose, eldest daughter of the Rose clan, must walk her path.*
*She will need to learn who she can trust, who would seek to betray her, how to keep her nation safe, but above all...*
*She must survive.*
*King Orwell has returned from his travels through the provinces of Rosanna.*
*He enters the great hall of Castle Reinmeer, the snow of an early winter drifting in behind him.*
King Orwell Rose: "Finally, home again."
*King Orwell pluts his travel bag down.*
Sarah: "FATHER!"
*Sarah leaps into her father's arms.*
King Orwell Rose: "Ooh, Sarah, my back! Please daugher, I'm not as young as I was, and you've grown much too big to just be jumping on me."
Sarah: "You were gone for almost five months! If you thought I wasn't going to hug you, you don't know me at all."
King Orwell Rose: "You've grown older but I don't think you've grown up yet."
Sarah: "So mean!"
King Orwell Rose: "Speaking of growing up, have you seen..."
Thomas: "DAD!"
*Thomas Rose, Sarah's younger brother, and heir to the throne, embraces his father.*
Thomas: "I've missed you so much dad!"
*King Orwell grabs his son by the shoulders and holds him at a distance.*
King Orwell Rose: "I missed you too son, but remember: composure. It's not befitting for a future king to be running around like a wild child."
King Orwell Rose: "That goes for both of you."
*King Orwell looks sternly at his daughter.*
Sarah and Thomas in unison: *Yes Father.*
King Orwell Rose: "Good. Now, where is the royal assistant? I need begin drafting letters immediately."
Sarah: "I think I saw him in the library, Father. I'll walk with you."
King Orwell Rose: "Fine, fine. Thomas, find a servant to carry this luggage to my room. And don't let me catch you doing it yourself again."
Thomas: "Yes, Father."
*King Orwell and Sarah are walking through an empty hallway towards the library. Their steps softly echo.*
King Orwell Rose: "I hope your brother has been keeping to his studies while I was away."
Sarah: "He did...in a way."
King Orwell Rose: "What does that that mean, exactly?"
Sarah: "He's been doing a lot of reading, just, maybe not those books you gave him."
*King Orwell stops walking and lets out a deep sigh.*
King Orwell Rose: "Then what did he study?"
Sarah: "Master Thyme's books on nature."
*King Orwell stares out onto the courtyard, a stern look on his face. Snow is slowly drifting down.*
King Orwell Rose: "I'm going to have to talk with your brother."
Sarah: "Try to go easy on him Father. I read some of those books on military strategy you gave him. They're very boring."
King Orwell Rose: "Of course they are. I didn't give them to him for his enjoyment."
King Orwell Rose: "Your brother will be king one day, and when that day comes he needs to be ready."
*King Orwell's voice grows louder.*
King Orwell Rose: "Nobody ever came to our castle asking me for advice on rare types of birds from the eastern desert!"
*Sarah puts her hands on her father's shoulder.*
Sarah: "Dad, please, calm down. Thomas knows this, but you also need to accept that he isn't you."
Sarah: "All this military stuff, it doesn't come as naturally to him as it did to you."
Sarah: "Besides, it's a new age. Maybe waging wars isn't all a king is good for. Maybe he'll be a wise king instead."
*King Orwell shrugs.*
King Orwell Rose: "Anyone can be a king in the easy times. It's the bad times that a king needs to be ready for. And your brother isn't ready."
*For a moment, both are quiet.*
Sarah: "Father...did something happen on your trip?"
King Orwell Rose: "A lot...too much to talk about. You can ask me tomorrow, okay?"
*Choose*
*Pressure him.*:
Sarah: "Father, I can see that something is worrying you. Please, tell me now. You'll sleep better having shared."
King Orwell Rose: "Perceptive as always, daughter."
*King Orwell takes a moment to think about his answer.*
King Orwell Rose: "You know that every year I visit a different part of the kingdom, and this year, I went to see the eastern provinces."
King Orwell Rose: "I expected the usual: complaints about road repairs, demands for more money from the city holders, maybe someone trying to ask for your hand in marriage."
*King Orwell winks at his daughter.*
Sarah: "Very funny..."
King Orwell Rose: "But it wasn't like that at all. Everywhere I went, it was the same thing. People talking about a man called Hassar."
Sarah: "Hassar? I've never heard a name like that before."
King Orwell Rose: "It's Eastern, from beyond even the furthest provinces of our kingdom, across the vast eastern desert."
King Orwell Rose: "It didn't matter who I talked to: rich, poor, soldier, farmer. They all kept talking about this Hassar."
Sarah: "Were we attacked?"
King Orwell Rose: "No, nothing so serious. But there are rumors. Rumors that tell of him breaking the tribes of the desert, unifying them."
Sarah: "Should we be worried?"
King Orwell Rose: "It's too soon to say. I won't send an army into the desert on a rumor, but I also know that you can feel a war coming before it does."
*Let it be.*:
Sarah: "Ok father, tomorrow we'll talk."
King Orwell Rose: "I've kept you long enough, Sarah. I'll walk the rest of the way to the library myself."
King Orwell Rose: "I need to be alone with my thoughts for a bit."
*Sarah embraces her father, hugging him more tightly than she herself had even expected, holding him.*
Sarah: "We see how hard you work for us, for everyone, Father. Just remember to also think about yourself sometimes."
King Orwell Rose: "I'll look after myself, if you look after that brother of yours for me, promise?"
Sarah: "Promise!"
*Sarah had returned to her bedroom late that night.*
*Outside, the snow picked up. The snowstorm made the castle feel cut off from the rest of world. Isolated.*
*Sarah's eyes drift towards the thick tome, sitting on the edge of her desk.*
*The title reads: A historical account of cavalry flanking manoeuvres in the 8th and 9th century.*
Sarah: "Thomas wasn't wrong. These books are very dry."
*When her father had given Thomas the books, she knew Thomas would get distracted, as he usually did.*
*She had hoped to read the books on his behalf and give Thomas a summary so he could at least learn something.*
*But Thomas was difficult. It wasn't that he was stupid, or even that he was lazy. If he was, Sarah thought, that would almost be easier.*
*No, her brother Thomas was one of those unique people whose interests continually drifted from one topic to another.*
*His interests could stay fixed for months, only to completely shift in less than a day.*
*Once he had spend an entire week learning everything there was to learn about how glass was made.*
*Once Thomas was interested in a thing, it seemed to completely envelop his every waking moment, and he rarely stopped until he understood the object of his obsession.*
*Had Thomas been obsessed with war, he could have been a general unlike any other, but out of his many interests, war never seemed to be one of them.*
*Sarah had often wondered why. For most boys his age, war seemed to be the only thing they cared for. Soldiers, battle, glory.*
*Perhaps, Sarah speculated, it was simply his nature. Too kind to hurt anything, and so too soft for war, even the theory of war.*
Thomas: "Is this all you do all day? so boring."
Sarah: "AAAH!"
*Sarah lets out a high-pitched scream and spins around.*
*Standing in the corner of her room is her brother, Thomas.*
Sarah: "What are you doing creeping around my room? You should be in bed by now."
Thomas: "I know, I know. I tried, but I was staring at the ceiling and I just couldn't get to sleep."
Thomas: "So I figured, obviously, my dear sister must be suffering the same fate as me, so why not share the misery?"
Sarah: "I sleep just fine, for your information."
Thomas: "Pleeeeease don't send me back, ok? I really can't fall asleep."
*Sarah sighs.*
Sarah: "Ok, you can stay, but only for a bit. We're going to have the banquet tomorrow for Dad's return. If you don't get any rest, you're going to fall asleep in your soup like last time."
Thomas: "I didn't fall asleep in the soup!"
*Sarah laughs.*
Sarah: "Sure, slipped into it, whatever."
*Thomas walks over to Sarah's desk and picks up the book.*
Thomas: "Are you seriously reading this garbage?"
Sarah: "It's not as bad as you make it out to be. Also, you should try maybe doing what dad asks for a change."
*Thomas rolls his eyes.*
Thomas: "We can't all be perfect like you."
*Sarah smiles at her brother.*
Sarah: "True."
Thomas: "Show off."
*Sarah laughs.*
Sarah: "But seriously, Thomas, you should listen to Dad at least some of the time. He's only trying to do what is best for us."
*Thomas casually drops the tome back on the desk.*
Thomas: "Yeah, I know, but sometimes it just gets a bit much. Read this, train that, study such. Like, no matter how much I try, I just can't be like him, Sarah."
Thomas: "All this, ruling a kingdom, it just comes easy for him."
*Sarah looks at her brother, his eyes fixed to the floor.*
*She gets up and puts her arms around him.*
Sarah: "That's not true. He told me how difficult it was, growing up under his father. How nothing he ever did was good enough."
Sarah: "Grandfather used to beat him, mercilessly."
*Thomas sudenly looks up, a shocked expression on his face.*
Thomas: "I didn't know that."
*Sarah keeps hugging her brother.*
Sarah: "He's tried to give us more freedom than he ever had. But you know, he's also preparing us for the real world."
Sarah: "Not everything is going to stay like things are now, Thomas. One day you will be king, and when that day comes, you need to be ready."
Thomas: "Yeah...I guess I could try to be better."
Sarah: "Just show some effort, even if you hate it. Pretending is half of what it takes to be a king."
*Thomas looks at the bed.*
Thomas: "Could I sleep here tonight?"
Sarah: "Thomas..."
Thomas: "Please, like we used to."
Sarah: "Yeah, when we were six. We're not kids anymore, it's not appropriate."
Thomas: "Pleeeeeease."
*Choose*
*Okay, just this once.*:
*Sarah and Thomas climb into the bed together.*
*Her brother hugs her, and she hugs him back.*
*They stay, locked in an embrace. It doesn't take long for Thomas to fall asleep.*
*Sarah stares at the ornate ceiling. Her brother soundly asleep next to her.*
*Nothing stays the same forever, but she wishes, some things could.*
*Grow up, little brother.*:
Thomas: "Whatever."
*Thomas storms off, angrily muttering to himself.*
*Sarah wakes to the first beams of light breaking through her curtains.*
*Her brother is still asleep, next to her.*
*It all feels peaceful. She likes to bully him sometimes, but truthfully, she loves her brother.*
*She gently nudges him, knowing the banquet will start soon.*
Sarah: "Hey, time to wake up."
*Thomas grunts, acknowledging he's awake but hoping to be spared the day's official events.*
Sarah: "Seriously, Thomas, you need to go to your room and get dressed before Dad comes and drags you to the banquet."
*Thomas drags himself from the bed.*
Thomas: "I'm going!"
*Thomas turns around before leaving.*
Thomas: "See you at the banquet."
*Sarah waves to her brother.*
*Sarah gets out of the bed and begins to get dressed for the banquet.*
*She watches herself in the mirror as she tries out a series of different dresses.*
*Sarah feels the spectre of her mother, advising her with every choice.*
*"Ooh no, not this one. Try that one*, she would say when Sarah was still young.*
*Her mother loved to dote on her, and Sarah had loved her doing it.*
*Sarah felt herself tear up at the memories.*
*It was different for her, because she could still vaguely remember her mother. Thomas had been too small before she passed.*
*She wondered if it was worse to feel this sadness, or to have no memory at all. Each seemed a different kind of cruelty.*
*After her mother had passed, it has just been Sarah, Thomas and her father.*
*Most kings would have remarried, but their father never had. When he lost their mother, she took part of his joy with her to the grave.*
*Her father had once told her that when their mother died, he had lost so much of himself, that he couldn't risk loving someone like that ever again.*
*Sarah shakes her head and pushes away the memory. Composure. Just as Father always said.*
*The tears could come later.*
*Sarah wakes to the first beams of light breaking through her curtains.*
*Save for herself, her bed is empty. She hopes Thomas won't be too upset that she had send him away.*
*Still, he should have known they were too old for that.*
*Sarah gets out of the bed and begins to get dressed for the banquet.*
*She watches herself in the mirror as she tries out a series of different dresses.*
*Sarah feels the spectre of her mother, advising her with every choice.*
*"Ooh no, not this one, try that one* she would say when Sarah was still small.*
*Her mother loved to dote on her, and Sarah had loved her doing it.*
*Sarah felt herself tear up at the memories.*
*It was different for her, because she could still vaguely remember her mother. Thomas had been too small before she passed.*
*She wondered if it was worse to feel this sadness, or to have no memory at all. Each seemed a different kind of cruelty.*
*After her mother had passed, it has just been Sarah, Thomas and her father.*
*Most kings would have remarried, but their father never had. When he lost their mother, she took part of his joy with her to the grave.*
*Her father had once told her that when their mother died, he had lost so much of himself, that he couldn't risk loving someone like that ever again.*
*Sarah shakes her head and pushes away the memory. Composure. Just as father always said.*
*The tears could come later.*
*Sarah arrived in the great hall.*
*Settled in the center was a large oak table, long enough to house dozens of people on each side.*
*Throughout the hall, servants ran up and down, placing plates, putting down silverware; some were ironing the sheet covering the oak table.*
*She enjoyed seeing the castle like this: alive, vibrant.*
*Some servants passed by, lowering their heads, mumbling their respects to their princess. Sarah acknowledged them and their efforts with a small nod.*
Thomas: "So busy."
*Thomas strolled into the great hall, stopping next to his sister.*
Sarah: "At least you managed to get here in time."
Thomas: "Yes, a certain someone gave me some advice. Said I should put in more of an effort."
Sarah: "Sounds like a smart person."
Thomas: "She likes to think she is."
*Thomas winks at his sister.*
*Sarah rolls her eyes.*
*At least he's trying, she thinks to herself.*
*Sarah watches the people slowly fill into the great hall.*
*The court nobles were amongst the first. Always priding themselves on their own importance, each representing an important family.*
*They had crowded around a young man with a thin frame and long, flowing blonde hair, reaching to his shoulders.*
*Sarah knew him and wasn't surprised to see him, Marion Achillea, from the Achillea family.*
*The Achillea family was one of the oldest and most prestigious families of Rosanna. They had fought with Sarah's ancestors in establishing the Rose dynasty. For their efforts, they were well rewarded.*
*Ever since, the Achillea family had thrived. Some old families fell, others faded away into irrelevance, but the Achillea family had withstood every challenge.*
*And Marion was their scion, first amongst all his peers. He walked around the room with a confidence that could only be the result of years of cultivation.*
*Marion was one of those nobles who knew exactly what station he belonged to, because he had been told so repeatedly from birth, and had his beliefs reaffirmed all his life.*
*Marion crossed the room to meet them.*
Marion: "Prince Thomas, Princess Sarah."
*Marion gave a quick bow.*
*Sarah and Thomas gave a brief bow in acknowledgement.*
Sarah: "Good to see you, Marion. I hope your travels went well."
*Marion shrugs.*
Marion: "As well as was to be expected. I'm just glad to be back here in the capital. Travelling with your father to the Eastern districts has been exhausting."
Sarah: "How so?"
Marion: "Every day, the same endless stream of meetings. Everyone wanting something. Just one dull face after the other. It makes you feel like a bookkeeper."
Marion: "Not to mention, after months of being on the road, you begin to miss the luxuries of the capital. You wouldn't serve up their idea of fine dining to a dog. But, we manage."
*Sarah politely smiled as she listened to Marion complain. From Marion, even a little could be too much.*
*A man waved at Marion from across the room, and Marion waved back.*
Marion: "Excuse me, Prince, Princess. Duty calls."
*Marion turns around to walk over to the man.*
Thomas: "Ugh, I can't stand the guy."
*Sarah nods.*
Sarah: "He can be a bit much, but his family is important, so that makes him important."
Sarah: "You should remember to keep him as a friend."
Thomas: "When I'm king, shouldn't he want to be my friend?"
Sarah: "You'll only be king when enough people like him agree that you are. A king sits atop a mountain. Only when the base holds, does the peak."
*Thomas rolls his eyes.*
Thomas: "You sound like Father."
Sarah: "That doesn't mean I'm not right."
Sarah: "Besides, have you seen Father yet?"
*Thomas had stopped listening, distracted by a plate of food being carried past him.*
*Suddenly, the door to the great hall is slammed open.*
*A servant runs into the room, half stumbling, drenched in sweat.*
*He tries to simultaneously catch his breath and struggle to get the words out.*
*Everyone in the great hall has gone silent, all staring at the man.*
Servant: *The king! The king is dead!*
*As the words hit Sarah, everything around her is drowned out.*
*She sees the nobles react: some in anger, some turned white.*
*She sees her brother, looking at her, confused, as if he can't understand the words.*
*She sees Marion, usually so composed, with a hint of fear in his eyes.*
*Sarah wanders out of the great hall in a haze, ignoring everything around her.*
*She needs to find her father.*
*Sarah storms into the bedchamber of her father. Servants try to stop her, but she brushes past them.*
*She is brought to a pause by the sight.*
*Her father is lying in his bed, his skin white as paper, eyes wide open.*
*The sheets are drenched in dark blood. So dark it has nearly turned black.*
*Lodged in his chest, a dagger, buried so deep she can only see the handle.*
Sarah: "Father..."
*Sarah tries to call out to her father, but her voice is weak and soft.*
*How could this have happened? Just yesterday, he had returned home. They had spoken as if they had all the time in the world between them.*
*And now he was dead.*
*Sarah kneels by the edge of the bed and reaches out to hold her father's hand.*
*His hand feels cold to the touch, and stiff. These are her father's hands, but not as she remembers them. His hands don't hold hers back.*
Sarah: "Wake up Father, please."
*Sarah knows her prayers won't be heard, but makes them all the same.*
*Behind her, she hears her brother enter the room, and scream.*
*She listens as the servants drag him away, kicking and screaming until he is too far to hear.*
*Sarah stays with her father, holding his hand.*
*She stays with him until nightfall. Until the servants are forced to carry her away.*
*The day of King Orwell's funeral has arrived.*
*A week has passed since his body was found.*
*In attendance are all the great houses and families of Rosanna, come to pay their final respects.*
*Beloved in life and beloved in death, a nation mourns the passing of their king.*
*Sarah looks out over the crowd of people that have fitted themselves into the great hall.*
Thomas: "Sarah..."
*Thomas embraces his sister.*
Thomas: "Who would have wanted to hurt Dad?"
*Sarah can't find the will to hug him back.*
Sarah: "It's okay Thomas, we just need to get through today. Let those questions rest for another day."
Thomas: "Then what?"
*Thomas sounded exasperated.*
Sarah: "Then another day. Coronation. Another day. On and on, Thomas. We just need to keep moving forward. Dad might not be here anymore, but he's watching over us."
*Sarah turns to her brother, looking deep into his eyes. His eyes are bloodshot from the crying that he hides from her.*
Sarah: "We need to make him proud now. Remember: composure."
*Thomas turns away from her, staring off into the distance, trying to look at nothing at all.*
*Sarah tries to remember the week since her father's death.*
*She had to do so much, in a way, it spared her from dealing with her grief.*
*Invitations, decorations, preparations. An endless amount of work for her to lose herself in.*
*Thomas, on the other hand, had turned inwards. He had grown more somber, and she had found him on some nights, walking through the dark unlit castle halls.*
*Sarah made a mental note, she needed to talk to her brother. It pained her to admit it, but he wasn't strong. He needed to know he could lean on her.*
*The events of the day proceeded. Priests read out the last rites. Some spoke words of comfort.*
*Not before long, Sarah and Thomas found themselves in the middle of the great hall, walking in linked arms, floating from one group of nobles to the next.*
Nobleman: *Our condolences.*
Noblewoman: *He was a great man.*
Ambassador: *He will be missed.*
*Sarah didn't want to sound cynical, she was sure that many of them truly meant what they said. It just seemed like words, not just these words but all words, seemed so empty right now.*
*Soon, she found herself subjected to a torrent of sympathies. It all became too much.*
Sarah: "Thomas, I need to take a moment, please carry on without me."
*Sarah unlinked her arm from her brother and quickly walked away.*
*Fresh air, that's what she needed.*
*Sarah was slowly walking across the battlements of Castle Reinmeer.*
*From a distance, she could still hear the sounds of the funeral. The endless kind words she couldn't stand right now.*
*Ever since her father had returned home, the cold had grown harsher with each day.*
*Sarah loved the summer, but today, she was happy for the stinging cold and the few snowflakes drifting in the wind. Dark clouds in the sky.*
*Seems right, Sarah thought to herself, that the world looks this bleak without your father. Nature itself mourns your passing.*
*Looking out out over the edge of the battlements, Sarah saw the many lights of the city, cutting through the dark. Beyond that, the great forests where she used to play as a child.*
*Would she have another day as free of care as she did back then? As she did even only a week ago?*
*So consumed in busy work, Sarah had not paid much attention to the questions that still needed to be answered.*
*Her brother would soon become king, and she knew that he would need her help. But what did either of them know of ruling a nation?*
*Already, in the days before the funeral, people had begun to approach her. Servants of all ranks, trying to procure favor with her.*
*She could keep them away, on account of her grief, but she knew that soon, the burdens of rule would truly fall on them.*
*And none of that even began to deal questions, such as who was responsible for her father's death.*
Sarah: "Dad...do you think we're ready?"
*The howling winds were her only answer.*
Varga: "Excuse me, but can I offer you my cloak?"
*Sarah turned, surprised by the voice. She sees a tall man standing on the battlements next to her.*
Varga: "It's too cold for you to be out here in nothing more than a dress."
*The man holds out a thick black cloak, large enough to envelop her completely, fashioned out of a wolf skin.*
Sarah: "It's okay, I don't mind the cold. I like it."
Varga: "I understand, but it's colder than you think. Hypothermia can sneak up on you."
*The man pushes his cloak into Sarah's hands.*
*Sarah, if only to not embarrass the man, accepts and puts on the cloak.*
Sarah: "Thank you, kind sir."
Varga: "No problem at all, uhm, my lady. My liege? Princess?"
*The man stumbles, trying to find the words.*
*Sarah laughs.*
Sarah: "It's ok, kind sir, don't mind the formalities. My name is Sarah Rose."
Varga: "I know who you are."
*A short pause.*
Sarah: "And...you are?"
*The man seems flustered.*
Varga: "I'm so sorry, of course, my name is Varga. Varga Northwood."
*Sarah observes the man.*
*He's tall, black hair, kept short and kempt, the way a soldier would.*
*A large scar runs across the side of his cheek, blemishing what would otherwise be a very handsome face.*
Sarah: "Sir Northwood...I can't say I'm familiar with that family name. What part of Rosanna do you hail from?"
*The man looks away, seemingly embarassed.*
Varga: "Well...the woods up north, actually. Mine is what you could call a more recent addition to the noble families."
*Sarah suddenly understands. That explains. Newly promoted nobility, equal in title but lacking the years of experience in protocol.*
Varga: "I'm sorry if I'm messing this up, it's my first time at such a formal event."
Sarah: "It's alright."
*Sarah gently puts her hand on the man's arm.*
Sarah: "Forget all those silly rules. Even I mess them up sometimes, and I've lived with them all my life."
*The man softly laughs, seemingly put at ease by Sarah's more informal tone.*
Sarah: "Tell me, how did your family earn their title?"
Varga: "Do you remember the insurrection at North Chapel?"
*Sarah did. It had been only a few years ago, but she rememberd that it had troubled her father greatly.*
*A group of farmers had burned the bridges leading to one of the northern provinces, out of protest over land rights, preventing Rosanna's standing army from moving there without taking a month long detour.*
*After burning the bridges, the farmers had begun looting the provincial capital, and even attempted to lay siege to the ancestral home of the Taylee family.*
*Overnight, the problem had been resolved when a small local group of loyalists seemingly appeared out of nowhere and killed most of the farmers.*
Sarah: "Yes, I believe I do remember."
Varga: "Well, I was the commander that broke the insurrectionist army."
*Varga had said it very matter-of-factly.*
*Sarah looked at him, stunned for a moment.*
Sarah: "Are you being honest with me?"
*Varga looked surprised.*
Varga: "Why would I lie?"
Sarah: "It's just, you seem so young...and that insurrection was years ago, you would have been..."
Varga: "Sixteen"
*Varga swiftly responded.*
Varga: "Yeah, I was pretty young when I did it, I suppose."
*Varga shrugged.*
Varga: "They call me a military prodigy, but I don't know about all that."
*Sarah observed the man again. She was surprised by how wrong her initial impression of him proved to be.*
Sarah: "Well, Sir Varga..."
*Sarah made a small curtsy.*
Sarah: "It has been a pleasure to make your acquaintance."
Varga: "Aah, uhm, yes and yours as well, Princess."
*Varga tried to imitate her curtsy, nearly tumbling off the battlements in his attempt.*
*Sarah laughed and tried handing him back his cloak.*
*Varga shook his head.*
Varga: "Please, Princess, keep it. I insist. I'll come back for it later."
Sarah: "Thank you, really. It's been nice to talk to someone for a while and not have it be about...well, you know."
*Sarah turned and took her leave.*
*Sarah slowly walked through the castle's garden. A thin blanket of snow covered most of the plants.*
*She sat down on one of the benches, drawing Varga's cloak tighter around herself.*
*Sarah offered to give the cloak back, but now, sitting in the snow-covered garden, she was happy he had been too polite to accept.*
*She wondered what to make of him. Accomplished beyond his years, and still, seemingly embarassed for his lowborn origins.*
*Sarah had met enough nobility to know that titles were a poor replacement for a good heart.*
*A twig snaps behind her.*
*Sarah spun around towards the source of the sounds.*
*Standing a little distance off is a woman with long black hair, and soft white skin as if she could fade into the snow.*
*Something about her seems...familiar.*
Kate: "Hey Sarah, been a while."
*Sarah stares at the woman, trying to figure out how she knows her.*
*Then, it dawns on her.*
Sarah: "Kate!!"
*Sarah jumps off the bench and runs towards the woman, leaping into an embrace.*
Kate: "I was starting to worry you didn't remember me!"
*Kate laughs.*
Sarah: "Wow, I just...I can't believe this. It's really you."
*Sarah takes a step back, still holding onto Kate. She eyes her up and down, almost as if afraid she isn't real.*
Sarah: "You've changed so much..."
*Kate had been Sarah's closest friend in childhood.*
*Unlike Sarah, Kate had been born to a servant family, working in the castle, but when they were children, matters of class weren't important.*
*They had explored every corner of the castle together, for years, they had been inseparable.*
*Then, one day, Kate and her family were just gone.*
*Sarah had been devastated. She asked her father to find her friend, but after months had gone by with no news, she had to move on.*
*Her father had tried to comfort her, telling her that this was not unusual for servants, to simply leave for work elsewhere, but Sarah had always kept wondering where her friend went.*

Kate: "I didn't just come here because your father had passed."
*Sarah could feel her heart beat in her throat. Whatever it was that Kate tried to tell her, it was something big.*
Kate: "Several months ago, I was contacted...by your father."
*Sarah sat listening, stunned.*
Kate: "He reached out to me in Lethram, across the sea, where I was stationed. He told me that there were dangerous forces out there, seeking to harm you."
Kate: "He said that he couldn't tell me much more than that, but he asked me, as your old friend, to come back to the castle, should anything happen to him..."
*Kate paused.*
Kate: "And he asked me to take you to safety...across the sea, to Lethram."
*Sarah found it hard to process what she was hearing. Her friend had kept this secret from her, but so had her father. Did her father know that he had been in danger all this time?*
Kate: "He paid the mercenary company I work for a small fortune, if we vowed to keep you safe in Lethram."
Kate: "When we heard of your father's death, we knew that we had to come and save you. That's why I'm here, to honor what I promised your father."
*Another pause.*
Kate: "Sarah, you need to come with me, to Lethram. It's the only place where we can keep you safe. But, we need to leave tonight, right now. There is a ship waiting for us in the harbor."
*Sarah's mind was spinning. The mystery of her father's death only grew, now Kate revealed herself to be her father's secret agent...and now she had to leave in the dead of night.*
*Sarah's eyes had become used to the dark, and she could see her friend's eyes, glittering with tears.*
Kate: "Sarah, please, come with me."
*Kate reaches out her hand.*
*Choose*
*Reach out and grab Kate's hand.*:
*No, I can't leave Thomas. This is crazy.*:
*Sarah, instinctively, pulls herself physically away from Kate.*
*She looks at her old friend. Her brown eyes seem almost black in the dark. Within them, she sees something break.*
Kate: "Sarah...please..."
*Sarah shakes her head.*
Sarah: "It doesn't matter if I'm in danger here, Kate. Thomas needs me, he always did, but now more than ever."
Sarah: "If you think that I'm going to leave him alone...then you don't really know me at all."
Sarah: "I will stay here, even if it means risking my life."
*Kate climbs off the bed.*
Kate: "Then you're an idiot. You don't know anything about the dangers of this world."
Kate: "There will be a day when you wish you took my hand, and when that day comes, remember that I offered, and it was you who declined."
*Sarah steels herself and looks at Kate.*
Sarah: "I've said my part. Get out before I have you dragged out by the guards."
*Kate shakes her head in disbelief. She pauses for a moment, trying to find the words, but finds none.*
*Kate turns and walks towards the door in large strides.*
*As she opens the door, she stands in the opening and turns around, looking at Sarah one last time.*
*Sarah sees that, again, Kate has no words.*
*Kate slips out the door, closing it softly, and vanishes.*
*Sarah tries to get back to sleep, but her thoughts keep her awake.*
*She wonders if she will ever see her old friend again.*
*Eventually, exhaustion carries Sarah off to sleep.*
*Some days had passed and Sarah had spend them trying to forget about Kate's visit to her bedroom.*
*Her words of warning, her attempt to take her away from Castle Reinmeer, it had all been so very odd.*
*But Sarah had soon found that Kate had been too cryptic. Sarah couldn't afford to be distracted, speculating about what dangers might be out there.*
*There were plenty of real dangers all around her.*
*Having finished reviewing some of the weekly reports, Sarah found herself wandering the castle, ending up in the great hall.*
*Sitting atop the stairs near the dais, she found her brother Thomas.*
*She observed him as she approached, and noticed that he did not notice her.*
*He might be in this room, but in his head, he was very far away.*
*Already prone to overthinking, her brother had turned almost entirely inward following the coronation.*
Sarah: "Only cheerful thoughts, I hope?"
*Thomas looked up, startled.*
Thomas: "Huh?"
Sarah: "I said, I hope you're having cheerful thoughts."
Thomas: "Ooh...sorry, I wasn't paying attention."
*Sarah flattened her dress and set down next to her brother.*
*She poked him with her elbow.*
Sarah: "Come on Thomas, share with me. We promised we were going to get through this together. That means trusting me enough to let me into your head."
*Thomas nodded, but still seemed to stare into the distance.*
Thomas: "You're right..."
Thomas: "It's just, ever since the coronation, it's all gotten even worse."
Sarah: "What has?"
Thomas: "The expectations that people seem to have. They come up to me, asking me to weigh in on one problem after the other."
Thomas: "And it's not just that, but they're also...different with me..."
Sarah: "Different how?"
Thomas: "I used to know what people were about, you know? If they liked me, or didn't like me. But now, everyone is always smiling at me."
*Thomas paused for a moment.*
Thomas: "But, it's like, their smiles aren't real, and I can see it, you know?"
*Sarah understood what her brother was getting at.*
*Ever since their father had died, it was true that more and more people seemed to want to ingratiate themselves with them.*
*Where before they had just been the heirs to the throne, now Thomas was actually king, and it made all the difference.*
*Sarah put an arm around her brother.*
Sarah: "I know things are different, Thomas, and it will take some time to get used to it."
Sarah: "But we'll get through this, you and me. And whenever things get too much, remember that I'm here for you. Always."
*Thomas nodded, but the words didn't seem to affect him much.*
Thomas: "People come up to me and ask me to settle disputes between noble houses I've never even heard of, or make military decisions, as if I know anything about that stuff..."
Thomas: "It's all just too much, and I just keep thinking about Dad, and how he would do everything better..."
*Sarah pulled her brother closer.*
Sarah: "I miss him too, Thomas."
*The two siblings sat in silence for a while.*
*An idea came to Sarah.*
Sarah: "You know, Thomas, maybe the problem is that you're trying to do everything all at once. You're not giving yourself the time to learn how to be king."
Thomas: "What do you mean?"
Sarah: "Well, you're comparing yourself to father, but he was king for more than thirty years. Of course you can't be as good as him overnight."
*Thomas nodded, understanding what his sister was getting at.*
Sarah: "Father often told me about his earliest days, how he struggled with the same things you're talking about."
Sarah: "And he said, a good king knows when to lead and when to listen. Maybe the problem is that you're taking on too much all at once."
*For the first time that day, Thomas looked directly at his sister.*
Thomas: "So what do I do? I can't just ignore these issues, can I?"
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "No, you can't, but we could add more people to the council. People who know about war, and know about the inner workings of the noble families."
Thomas: "Who?"
Sarah: "Lord Marion and Lord Varga."
*Sarah could see Thomas frown.*
Thomas: "Really? You want to add Marion to the council?"
Sarah: "I know you don't like him, but you're not looking for friends. You're looking for someone who is good at what they do."
Sarah: "And Marion's family is one of the oldest in Rosanna, and he knows just about everyone. He could be a real help to us."
Sarah: "And Varga, he's proven himself in battle, I've heard people say he's a genius at war. With him on the council, you can learn everything he knows."
Sarah: "Rely on them for their skills, not their personalities."
*Thomas looked away and contemplated his sister's advice. After some time, he responded.*
Thomas: "You're right. I don't have to like them, but if you say they're as good as they are, we can use all the help we can get."
*Sarah patted her brother on the back.*
Sarah: "I'll draft the letters to extend the invitation to both of them."
Thomas: "What if they say no?"
*Sarah shrugged.*
Sarah: "Then we'll just order their heads off."
*Sarah drew her hand across her throat, signalling decapitation. She added an exaggerated death sound for effect.*
*Thomas broke into laughter.*
*Sarah laughed along with her brother, but more than anything, she was happy to see him smile again.*
*It reminded her that the brother she knew, the easy-going quick-to-laugh brother, was still in there, despite the trauma.*
*Not long after, a messenger arrived for Thomas.*
*He opened the letter and read it. After, he sighed and stood up.*
Thomas: "The work never ends."
*Sarah held onto his hand and gave it a quick squeeze.*
*Thomas smiled, comforted by the gesture.*
*Sarah watched as her brother began to walk away, down one of the many hallways of Castle Reinmeer.*
*Though his shoulders still hung low, she hoped that his crown weighed a little less on him now.*
*It was a little over a week later when the first council meeting that included Marion and Varga began.*
*Sarah and Thomas had arrived early, preparing ahead of the meeting, and it was Varga who showed up first, slightly too early.*
Varga: "My king, my princess."
*Varga bowed as he entered, in that slightly fumbling way which only endeared him to Sarah.*
*It reminded her that there was a whole world outside of these walls, one where all the pomp and pretense of the court wasn't taken so seriously.*
*Varga took his seat at the table, placing down a large stack of papers in front of himself.*
Varga: "I was hoping I wouldn't be late..."
*Varga looks around the table.*
Varga: "But now I fear I might be too early."
*Sarah laughed politely.*
Sarah: "Don't worry Lord Varga, I wish all the nobles could be as timely as yourself."
*Varga smiled at Sarah. His shoulders relaxed as the compliment put him visibly at ease.*
Varga: "Your invitation, Princess, it was great honour. I only hope that I can live up to the trust you place in me."
Sarah: "My brother and I have no doubt that you will prove worthy of my trust."
*The three continued to exchange pleasantries until the door swung upon.*
*Marion entered, strutting across the room and performing a perfect bow before sitting down.*
Marion: "King Thomas, princess Sarah, thank you for the invitation."
*Marion's eyes went around the table, settling finally on Varga.*
Marion: "Glad to see you managed to find your way here as well, Varga."
Marion: "The castle can be a confusing maze for those unfamiliar with it."
*Sarah watched the two exchange glances.*
*She realized that whilst she had spoken to each of them, she had never seen the two men interact with one another.*
*There seemed to be a tension.*
*Marion was flashing that wide grin of his, but Varga only scowled back at him.*
Varga: "Good to see you as well, Marion."
*Whatever played between the two men, neither seemed to want to escalate here.*
*There wasn't much time for the two to clash, for not long after, the three advisors entered the room and took their place between the men.*
*General Barion, Spymaster Kravel and the Account Master Carolyn each greeted all the other attendants at the meeting.*
*After exchanging brief greetings, Thomas began the meeting by clearing his throat.*
Thomas: "Welcome, each of you, to today's council meeting."
Thomas: "As you might have noticed, we are joined by two new members to our council."
*Thomas waived his hand to one side.*
Thomas: "We have Lord Varga, hero of Northwood, the man who broke the farmer uprising. He will be advising us on matters concerning war."
*Thomas waived his hand to the other side.*
Thomas: "And we have Lord Marion Achillea, of house Achillea. The loyalty of his family to our country stretches back to its very founding."
Thomas: "He will be assisting us concerning the issues that have been brought up by the nobility."
*General Barion was the first to speak.*
Barion: "King Thomas, excuse me, but as High General, I believe that should you have any questions on matters of war, you should consult me."
*Thomas seemed uncomfortable at being so directly confronted. Sarah decided to intercede on her brother's behalf.*
Sarah: "General Barion, we understand your important contribution to our council, and we urge you to continue work on behalf of the royal army."
Sarah: "However, King Thomas believes that given the current threats from the East, that he needs someone who is able to also tutor him on matters of war."
Sarah: "We both understand that we are already asking a great deal of you, and so we did not wish to add onto your already great burden."
*General Barion stroked his great beard for a moment, but seemed pleased with the answer.*
Barion: "Yes, it is true, I have been quite busy. An assistant to carry some of the load would be very welcome."
*Sarah looked at Varga, but if being called an assistant had offended him, he didn't show it.*
Thomas: "Very well then, it's settled."
Thomas: "The first issue on the agenda..."
*Thomas shuffled through his papers for a while, trying to find what he was looking for.*
*This time it was Kravel who spoke up.*
Kravel: "It was concerning the tribes of the eastern desert."
Thomas: "Aah, yes...have we discovered anything new regarding that matter?"
*Kravel nodded.*
Kravel: "Following the last council meeting, I organized a few scout parties to go into the eastern desert."
Kravel: "I also reached out to my network of spies in the area, thin as it may be."
Kravel: "We received nothing definitive, but they say there are hints of a large troop movement."
*Sarah leaned in.*
Sarah: "Hints? What does that mean, exactly?"
Kravel: "They make mention of tracks, left on the outer steps, that could only be made by tens of thousands of horses."
Kravel: "There is a report that entire plots of grassland have turned arid."
Kravel: "As I said, nothing definitive, but it does appear there is an army on the move."
*Sarah turned to Thomas.*
Sarah: "We need to consider this seriously, Thomas. I think it's fair to say that it's more likely than not that an attack might come from the east."
*Thomas nodded as he kept transfixed on the table.*
*Kravel shook his head.*
Kravel: "No new reports or information. It's mostly been quiet on the frontier."
*Thomas looked at Sarah.*
Thomas: "See, sis, nothing to worry about. If there was an army out there, we'd have heard about it."
*Sarah nodded, but she was not entirely convinced.*
*It was Varga who now reared himself.*
Varga: "Given what I've just heard, I believe that we ought to excercise caution."
Varga: "We can't know for certain if there is an enemy waiting to strike, but we would do better to ready the army and prepare for the worst rather than hope for the best."
*Marion rolled his eyes.*
Marion: "That's a nice phrase, but it doesn't change reality."
Marion: "Rosanna does not have infinite resources to commit to every phantom that the peasantry imagine in the dark."
Marion: "If we waste resources here, that means sacrificing them somewhere else."
Marion: "I was out there, in the eastern district, with King Orwell. I saw no tribesmen, only farmers driving one another wild with conspiracy."
Marion: "A good ruler lets the facts guide him, not hysteria."
*Both Varga and Marion turn to Thomas, expecting him to settle the matter.*
*Thomas turns to Sarah.*
*Choose*
*We ready the army; best we be prepared.*:
*Sarah turned her attention towards both, but making it clear she spoke on her brother's behalf.*
Sarah: "Varga is right, if we prepare for nothing, then we lose nothing. But if the threat is real, we will be ready."
Sarah: "Lord Barion, make preparations to rally Rosanna's army."
*Barion saluted the command.*
Barion: "Yes, Princess!"
*We cannot afford to waste resources on fictions.*:
*Sarah turned her attention towards both, but making it clear she spoke on her brother's behalf.*
Sarah: "Marion is right."
Sarah: "Rallying the army means calling the soldiers from their homes and farms."
Sarah: "If the threat proves fake, the people will resent us."
Sarah: "Only if the threat proves real, should we rally the army."
*Lady Carolyn spoke up.*
Carolyn: "Is this how the king decides?"
*Thomas asserted himself again.*
Thomas: "Yes, we will act just as my sister said. It is the best option, given our circumstances."
*With Thomas having spoken up, the matter was considered settled by all.*
*After settling several smaller items, General Barion was the first to bring up another matter.*
Barion: "My king, I must inform you that recent reports have found the city's walls to be dangerously weakened in some critical areas."
*Thomas suddenly sat up.*
Thomas: "Weakened? How? Our city hasn't been attacked in...I don't even know how long."
*General Barion nodded.*
Barion: "This is correct, but in recent years the tide has been higher than ususal. This has favored our city's port, but it has had unexpected consequences."
Barion: "The engineering corp informs me that the higher water levels have eroded the foundation of the city's walls along our coastal flanks."
Barion: "Without urgent repairs, these defects could prove fatal should an enemy know how to exploit them."
*Marion threw up his arms.*
Marion: "Surely, we cannot be expected to fund every single pet project that the army comes up with?"
Marion: "As hard as it is to believe, the noble families while rich, are not infinitely so. Raising taxes so the engineering corp can play in the dirt, it's absurd."
*Barion scowled at Marion.*
*As the council members were distracted by the bickering, Thomas leaned in close to Sarah and whispered.*
Thomas: "What should we do?"
*Choose*
*Reinforce the walls; we can't let them collapse.*:
*Thomas nodded at Sarah and turned back to the council.*
Thomas: "I have made my decision."
Thomas: "We will reinforce the walls, the risks outweigh the costs."
*Marion shook his head but said nothing.*
*The walls have stood just fine for centuries; they'll stand for centuries more.*:
*Thomas nodded at Sarah and turned back to the council.*
Thomas: "I have made my decision."
Thomas: "The walls can wait, we must be wise on where we spend our money."
*With the matter settled, the council continued on, working through various other minute matters.*
*Sarah idly listened as three different petitions for district land reforms were brought up and discussed.*
*Ruling, she had come to learn, happened as much in the grand moments as it did in the small.*
*Several hours later, with the last of the issues discussed, settled or pushed back, the advisors took their leave.*
*As Sarah went to leave, she found Varga waiting for her.*
Varga: "Princess, uhm, Sarah, could I escort you?"
*Sarah smiled at Varga. She wondered if this man would ever get used to the trappings of nobility.*
*Perhaps, she thought, past a certain age you could simply never internalize all the endless protocols and nuances of the royal court.*
Sarah: "Of course, Lord Varga."
*She linked her arm through his.*
Sarah: "But where are you escorting me to?"
*Varga seemed flustered.*
Varga: "I...I don't know, I thought...wherever you needed to go."
*Sarah softly laughed.*
Sarah: "The library is fine, I like to write down my thoughts on these meetings while they're still fresh."
Varga: "Of course!"
*Together, Sarah and Varga walked through the hallways of Castle Reinmeer, towards the library.*
*Who's escorting whom? Sarah thought to herself, as she corrected Varga a few times on the route to the library.*
Varga: "The reason I wanted to escort you, Sarah, is that I wanted to thank you. In person, I mean."
Sarah: "Why is that?"
Varga: "Well, I know that the council is a prestigious position. And I know that there have not often been people of my...station, allowed to attend."
*Sarah could feel him grow more tense, the muscles in his arms flexing.*
*It was true what he said. Most everyone on the council hailed from nobility, Varga was the rare exception.*
*But to Sarah it had seemed only logical. A way to break through the same old way of ruling.*
*People like Varga made up most of the nation, it seemed absurd to Sarah that they should not have a voice at the table.*
Sarah: "I believe in merit, Varga. Your title, your birth, people here pretend like that's all that matters, but I'd rather have a hundred of you than some of these nobles."
*Sarah's words seemed to lift Varga's spirits.*
Varga: "It means a lot to hear you say that, Sarah."
*Varga paused for a moment.*
Varga: "So, how did I do? On the council meeting?"
*Sarah patted his arm to comfort him.*
Sarah: "You were great. I was afraid that you might have been intimidated by the setting and would say nothing, but I was glad that you spoke your mind about the army."
Sarah: "Your background gives you a unique perspective. Use it, never feel like your voice doesn't matter."
Sarah: "All the other stuff, the protocols and rules of the court, you'll catch on soon enough."
*Varga laughed, a little too loudly, at that.*
Varga: "It's weird. I commanded an army, led them to crush the rebellion, and watched thousands of men die in battle."
Varga: "And yet I've never felt the kind of uncertainty and unease on the battlefield as I do here at the court."
*Sarah listened as Varga entrusted his worries to her.*
Sarah: "We all have talents, things we're just naturally good at, and environments where we feel most comfortable."
Sarah: "But if we only did the things that come easy to us, we'd never grow or learn to challenge ourselves."
*She stopped walking and looked directly at Varga.*
Sarah: "This castle, this court, it can be what you make of it, Varga. You can see yourself as seperate from it, always feeling alienated, or you can become a part of it. Add to it."
*Varga was moved by Sarah's words. He nodded in affirmation.*
Varga: "You're right. I didn't mean to complain."
Varga: "You've given me a rare opportunity and I promise I will serve you and your brother as best I can."
Sarah: "I have no doubt that you will."
*Sarah felt Varga begin to move again, almost pulling her along.*
*Varga stopped, flustered, as he realized Sarah wasn't walking with him.*
Sarah: "Lord Varga..."
Varga: "Sorry, Princess, I...what did I do?"
*Sarah gestured at the large door behind her.*
Sarah: "We're at the library."
Varga: "I'm such an idiot...this place is like a maze, I honestly don't know how anyone finds anything."
*Varga caught himself.*
Varga: "Don't tell Marion I said that, please."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "I'll keep your secret."
Sarah: "Thank you for escorting me. I'll find my way in myself."
*Varga made a quick bow. He walked away, before turning around when Sarah called after him.*
Sarah: "Ooh, and Lord Varga...try not to get lost. It would be a shame for you to survive all those battles, only to lose your life wandering the halls of Castle Reinmeer."
*She saw him turn red as he spun around and walked away, picking up his pace.*
*Sarah sat down in the library and tried to focus her mind on her notes.*
*The winter's grace festival was under way, and all throughout Rosanna, people had begun to decorate their homes.*
*Castle Reinmeer was no exception, covered from floor to ceiling in extravagent gold and silver garlands.*
*Standing near the entrance to the great hall, Sarah greeted everyone who visited.*
*Inside the great hall, Thomas sat atop his throne in full regalia.*
*Sarah could see him slouched, waving disinterested at the crowd. And yet, even her brother seemed kingly when dressed up like this.*
Noble wife: *Aah, Princess, thank you for allowing us to attend, the castle looks incredible!*
*Sarah smiled and nodded.*
Sarah: "We're happy to host you."
*Smiles, compliments, condolences for her father, it was all an endless repetition, but Sarah shouldered it and never showed her exhaustion.*
*As the room filled up, Sarah could hear the buzz from inside grow louder.*
*There was the occasional hoot and cheer from the crowd as performers juggled or somersaulted through the aisles. Some performers managed both at the same time.*
*With most of the nobles now in attendance, Sarah signalled the servants to continue welcoming any stragglers, as she went inside.*
*As soon as she stepped into the great hall, she felt the heat press upon her skin.*
*The long tables were covered from end to end with different dishes. The many smells combining in the air, filling the great hall with a rare scent of festivity.*
*Sarah continued walking through the center of the hall, up to the dais to take her place next to Thomas.*
*She waved politely at faces she couldn't remember, and a few she could. Varga was there, as was Marion.*
*Sarah wished she had the time to speak to them.*
*Climing up the stairs, she sat down in a smaller, lower seat, besides Thomas. It was close enough to speak, but so far away from anyone else, she doubted they could hear them.*
Thomas: "Everyone here?"
*Sarah waved her hand as if to dismiss the question.*
Sarah: "Anyone who isn't here yet is probably not important enough to wait on."
Thomas: "Alright, shall I begin then?"
*Sarah nodded.*
*She wondered why she felt so distant today. She always loved the winter grace festival.*
*Perhaps, she thought, it's because this was the first major festival without her father. The day felt tainted, somehow.*
*Thomas rose up from his seat, and an attendant stomped hard on the floor three times, bringing the room to a silence.*
Thomas: "Let me begin by welcoming all of you to this year's winter grace festival."
Thomas: "I stand here, happy to see so many friendly faces, and to see this great hall sing with a joy that can only come from good friends and good food."
Thomas: "But there is also a pain in my heart. An absence that I feel, as surely as all of you."
Thomas: "My father presided over countless of these gatherings, but for me, this is a first."
Thomas: "Even now, I find myself instinctively looking at the door, waiting for him to walk through. A winter festival without him, almost seems, wrong."
*Sarah found herself surprised to see her brother echo her own feelings so closely.*
Thomas: "The winter grace festival is about togetherness, so how do we celebrate that, when we are still mourning a loss that has separated us?"
*Thomas paused for a moment.*
Thomas: "We used to celebrate it with my father, but I propose, that this year, we instead celebrate in honour of him."
Thomas: "Those of you who had the privilege of truly knowing my father, knew how much he enjoyed the winter grace festival."
Thomas: "The company, the decorations, the food...the beer."
*A roaring laugh erupted from the room.*
Thomas: "So let us honour my father, by keeping his memory alive and celebrating this year's winter grace festival in the way that he would have wanted us to."
*Thomas raised a chalice.*
Thomas: "To my father, a king without equal."
*All across the hall, others raised their cups and yelled out their toasts.*
*As Thomas fell back into his seat, the party truly took off.*
*Thomas looked at Sarah, he seemed utterly wracked and exhausted.*
Thomas: "How did I do?"
*Sarah looked at Thomas, stunned.*
Sarah: "You were incredible, Thomas."
Thomas: "You think so? I spend all night writing and memorizing it."
*She watched as her brother slouched back into his seat. He had been somewhat of a true king for a moment, but Sarah slowly realized it didn't come easy to him.*
*The night carried on, and Sarah and Thomas spend it eating, receiving gifts from the nobles and listening to their troubles.*
*It was only towards the end of the night, when the mood suddenly shifted.*
*The door to the main hall burst open, each frame slamming into the walls. The sound echoed through the hall and a gust of wind was carried in.*
*A dreadful silence came over the room as a everyone turned their heads to see the source of the disturbance.*
*Marching through the center of the hall, in great strides, was a man.*
*His skin was a soft oaken brown, darker than any other in the room by far. His dark hair was swept back, cut in a practical fashion. A military fashion.*
*His young face was contrasted by his old eyes.*
*Just as his appearance and his style, the clothes he wore were foreign as well. A soft swirling white, mixed with a deep purple and the occasional leather patches of armor.*
*Sarah had never seen a man dressed like this, but she didn't need to in order to know that this man hailed from the eastern desert.*
*He was too alien to belong to her world.*
*The man strode across the hall, ending up at the feet of the stairs that led up to the dais.*
*Off to the sides, the guards had drawn in closer, but Thomas had waved to hold them off, seemingly more intrigued than afraid.*
*The foreign man fell to one knee.*
Emissary: *King Thomas, I humbly greet you.*
*Thomas motioned for the man to stand up.*
Thomas: "Please rise, visitor."
*The man did as instructed. His eyes fell directly on Thomas, before switching towards Sarah.*
*He only stared at her for a moment, before returning to Thomas, but to Sarah it had seemed an eternity.*
*There was something in this man's eyes. A purpose. All the others in the castle looked at her for who she was, a princess, but this man had the eyes of a predator.*
Emissary: *I have travelled far, hailing from deep within what you call the eastern desert, and I have come to deliver a gift, from my master to you, king Thomas.*
*The man's accent was faint, he was clearly well educated to speak the language of Rosanna so effortlessly.*
*Thomas was now leaning in, wanting to know more.*
Thomas: "A gift?"
*The emissary nodded.*
Emissary: *My master, the great Khan Hassar, has tasked me to bring you a gift of peace.*
*The room was still silent as a crypt.*
Emissary: *Khan Hassar bears a great burden, placed upon him by the stars in heaven. He is to bring unity to this world, and bind all peoples together into a single tribe.*
Emissary: *In service of this great task, he has brought together the tribes of the desert, and brought low the far-eastern nations from beyond the desert.*
Emissary: *Great emperors of dynasties that have stood for millenia, have bowed their heads low to Khan Hassar.*
Emissary: *But others, sought to impede his great task. It is because of them that I must sadly bear an offer of peace in one hand, and a warning in the other.*
*The emissary reached into a bag and pulled something out.*
*A woman shrieked loudly, breaking through the silence. The room began to grow rowdy. Men began to shout obscenities.*
*Sarah felt herself grow weak, but forced herself to look on. Look at the decapitated head that the emissary was now holding up for all to see.*
