*Together, they walked through the camp, out towards the staging grounds.*
Kate: "I was wondering where you were."
Sarah: "Vaelen had called an early meeting, there's a change in plans."
*Kate looked at her surprised.*
Kate: "This late before the attack, he wants to change plans?"
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "We're going to be attacking the palace..."
*The words hung between them for a moment. Kate was the first to break the silence.*
Kate: "Fuck."
Kate: "I mean...if it's the plan, it's the plan, but that's going to put us right in the middle of the fight..."
*Sarah agreed. Their earlier plan saw them moving in the flanks, with the Mythran army taking the bulk of the punishment, but now they would be operating deep inside the enemy territory.*
*Kate grabbed Sarah's arm and made her stop marching.*
*She grabbed Sarah by her armor and pulled her in for a kiss.*
*Sarah didn't resist, and felt Kate's tongue pushing deep into her mouth. She welcomed it.*
Sarah: "What was that for?"
*Kate looked serious.*
Kate: "In case we don't survive this. So you know what you mean to me."
Sarah: "And if we do survive?"
*Kate smirked and leaned in close enough to whisper.*
Kate: "Then I'm going to fuck your brains out in the throne room."
*Sarah laughed at how crass Kate was being.*
Sarah: "Best we survive then."
*Sarah and Kate arrived at the staging ground together. Already, the soldiers were busy preparing for the assault, putting on their armor, sharpening their weapons a final time.*
*Standing among the crowd, fixing each other's armor, were Caleb and Ephraim.*
*Caleb waved at Sarah and Kate as they walked up to them, Ephraim saluted.*
Ephraim: "Commanders."
*Sarah waved one hand at Ephraim, dismissing his official attitude.*
Sarah: "I keep telling you, just treat me like you always did."
Ephraim: "Rank is rank, but, I'll do as you instruct me, Sarah."
*Sarah and Kate had both made commander rank, sharing the duties of leading the vanguard unit.*
*Caleb and Ephraim had each, in their turn, been promoted to officers, underneath Sarah and Kate, despite their longer experience.*
*Sarah suspected that even here, her noble birth had given her an advantage in her promotion.*
*Still, she had earned her experience in battle, and the truth was, she was far more suited towards command than either of the two men.*
*Caleb, while a great soldier, was illiterate, which limited his options for advancement.*
*Ephraim, who could read, while a good strategist, seemed uncomfortable taking actual command.*
*Sarah's royal upbringing had taught her reading and writing, but also taught her the subtleties of politics and leadership.*
*She had been raised to possibly one day lead a nation, so the idea of ordering commands was not so unnatural to her as it was to Ephraim.*
*Sarah imagined that Kate enjoyed many of the same advantages that she did, despite her lower class, she had been raised in the castle, becoming literate and familiar with hierarchy.*
*Still, Sarah knew she didn't have much time to worry about whether her promotions were entirely based on merit or not.*
*If she was to retake Rosanna one day, she needed to be in a position of strength. What did it matter whether it was entirely earned or not?*
Caleb: "So, Sarah, are we ready?"
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "Change of plans, I'm afraid."
*Sarah went over the change in strategy, explaining that they were now taking the palace's western wing, rather than staying in the flank.*
*If any of them had any reservations, they didn't show them.*
Ephraim: "It's dangerous, but, I think it's true that the palace is likely poorly guarded."
Ephraim: "If we move as fast as you say we do, we might catch them by surprise."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "The map shows that there is only one real entrance into the western wing."
Sarah: "If we manage to break through and take it, we can fortify the way in and out."
Sarah: "We can lock ourselves inside."
Sarah: "Once we take control of the entrance, we clear out whatever is left inside."
Sarah: "With only one narrow way in and out, their numbers won't make a difference, and we can hold off long enough for reinforcement."
*Kate nodded along.*
Kate: "And once we have it, nobody can force us out."
*Sarah agreed.*
Sarah: "The Mythrans will likely demand access, we'll deny them, they'll negotiate with Vaelen, drag it out, buy ourselves time."
Sarah: "When we eventually let them in, there won't be a single thing of value left."
*With the strategy clear, each of them took off towards their own respective group of soldiers.*
*All together, the unit was perhaps some 500 soldiers strong. Not a lot compared to a standing army, but each man or woman had seen combat before.*
*Sarah would rather take them into battle than five thousand new recruits.*
*Soon after, the battle horn rang out over the camp, instructing all the units to move to the front.*
*Trudging through the sand of the desert, Sarah was almost glad to know that she would soon be standing on top of the solid walls of Bagrad.*
*Gathered under their banner, her unit was the first to finish assembling.*
*By now, the walls of Bagrad loomed even larger.*
*The only thing they had prepared were siege ladders. They didn't offer much, but with so few guards atop the walls, they hoped they could take the walls before facing any real resistance.*
*On her left and her right, Sarah watched the soldiers begin to line up.*
*Between them and the walls, there was still a little over a mile that they would have to cover.*
*If their information had been wrong, and there was a unit of archers on the wall, it would turn into a bloodbath.*
*Sarah shook her head, as if to drive out the thought.*
*Enough things could go wrong, no need to imagine more problems than she already had.*
*By now, the entire mercenary company had finished positioning itself.*
*Off to the east, she could already hear the early sounds of battle. The Mythran host had engaged with Bagrad army.*
*An odd silence descended on the battle line. The moment right before the battle. Despite some three thousand soldiers, ready to charge, Sarah felt like she could hear a pin drop.*
*Ahead of her, she saw the air warp and dance from the heat.*
*Maybe the palace would be cooler, she hoped.*
*A loud battle horn rang out across the line.*
*As if as one, the front of the line began to move. Slowly at first, at a walking pace, but quickly building speed.*
*Sarah kept apace with the rest of the line and could feel her heart begin to beat faster.*
*She began to run faster, taking longer steps, stomping through the sand, careful not to fall.*
*She remembered how scared she had been the first time, but now, it gave her a rush.*
*Charging out slightly ahead of the line, she saw almost nobody on either side of her.*
*She almost imagined that she was single-handedly conquering the city.*
*If you could see me now, Atilla, Sarah dreamed.*
*Off to her sides, Sarah saw the ladder crews gaining on her, moving up.*
*They were close to the wall now. Sarah said a silent prayer that there had been no archers.*
*The first of the crews arrived at the base of the wall and began to pull up the ladder.*
*On each side, all along the mighty walls, Sarah saw the siege ladders begin to be pulled up.*
*One of the soldiers yelled out confirmation.*
Siege crew: *Ladder ready!*
*Sarah turned around to her soldiers.*
Sarah: "Up the ladder, now!"
*Hungry for battle, she saw the first of her soldiers begin scaling the ladder.*
*Not long after, Sarah felt her own urge overtake her, leaping onto the ladder and beginning to climb.*
*Don't look down, she thought to herself at the halfway point.*
*Eager for battle, but scared of heights, she joked to herself.*
*Suddenly an ear piercing scream rang out and Sarah saw a shadow shift past the ladder.*
*Looking down, against her own instincts, she saw that the first man up the ladder was now falling down, screaming as he did.*
*Smoke was rising from his face. But Sarah realized, there wasn't much of a face there, only a pitch black goo that bubbled.*
*Boiling oil, she realized. They were throwing burning oil down at them.*
*Hesitation now meant death.*
Sarah: "Up the ladder! Keep moving!"
*Sarah screamed and physically pushed her soldiers up the ladder.*
*Off to the sides, she saw more oil being poured down.*
*Her hands were frantically reaching for the next bar, and the next. Out here, on the ladder, she was too vulnerable.*
*Sarah felt herself run out of breath.*
*All around her, the kinds of screams only burning flesh produced, grew louder.*
*Suddenly, her hand touched the last bar.*
*As Sarah rose up further, she grabbed the top of the battlements, pulling her body over the edge and all but throwing herself onto the walls of Bagrad.*
*Solid ground beneath her feet.*
*All around her, she saw other soldiers scale unto the wall.*
*But Sarah could not look at them, for before her, was something that stunned Sarah's imagination.*
*From atop the wall, all of Bagrad could be seen. The city stretched out seemingly as far as the horizon, in each direction, fully occupying Sarah's field of view, no matter where she looked.*
*A city like this, there was none like it in all the world.*
*Sarah felt a sadness come over herself. Even in ruins, far past its prime, this city was a jewel like no other.*
*People had build this, and lived here. All across the city, wonders rose up, and in the center, the greatest of all, a palace that seemed to shame any other in existence.*
*Sarah imagined that the people of this city must laugh if they ever saw anyone call Castle Reinmeer a castle. Compared to this, her ancestral home was a hovel.*
*The city had fallen from its heights, centuries before Sarah was even born, but now she wished with all her heart that she could have seen what it was like back then.*
*Could you grieve for something that never was?*
*But then, Sarah felt her heart steel.*
*She was not a noble princess, visiting the wonders of the world.*
*She was a soldier, a mercenary, come to put the final stake in the heart of a dying empire.*
*There were those who build this marvel, Sarah realized, and there were those who would destroy it. She was the latter.*
*She had often prayed that her father might look down on her and be proud of who she had become, but now she prayed that he would look away from her. She could not bear the idea of him watching her do this.*
*Forgive me father.*
*Sarah unsheated her sword.*
*The battlements fell quickly as the rest of the vanguard's soldiers made their way up the ladder.*
*Only a handful had died ascending the ladders, and for those deaths the Bagrad soldiers atop the battlements were made to pay dearly.*
*Sarah watched their morale break nearly instantly as the first wave of soldiers made it onto the walls.*
*Some stayed, throwing their life away for a battle that seemed already lost. Most dropped their weapons and began to run.*
*She saw an arrow catch one of the soldiers in the back, collapsing to the ground. His comrades trampled over him.*
*They would keep running, throw away their armor, their weapons, run back to their homes and pretend to be citizens.*
*Better that than a violent death, Sarah thought.*
*She wasn't the young girl she'd been when she first fled her homeland. She had blood on her hand as much as any other in the mercenary company.*
*And yet, she had never managed to learn to love the carnage in the way that some could.*
*Each death still haunted her.*
*Despite this, she also knew she could not yield. Her heart had been steeled a long time ago when she first set upon this path.*
*She had known the killing that would come, and she had accepted that bargain long ago.*
Sarah: "Gather up!"
*Sarah declared as she stepped down from the final flights of the stairs that led down from the great walls into the streets of Bagrad.*
*A small cadre of soldiers followed in her footsteps.*
*Sarah had studied the maps of the city, but down at the street level, it was harder to make sense of where they were.*
*Still, she knew roughly where the palace stood, which was enough.*
Sarah: "Our only chance is if we keep our momentum!"
Sarah: "You straggle, you get left behind."
*The soldiers battered their swords against their shields, acknowledging her words.*
Sarah: "First one in the palace gets double their share of the loot!"
*To this, she received an approving cheer.*
*Leading her unit, Sarah started to jog at a moderate pace.*
*They had to make time, but Sarah also knew that the city and its many tall buildings offered countless chances of an ambush.*
*As she began making her way through the city, she could see the windows of the houses were battened down.*
*The make-shift barricades would prove no obstacle to the armies that would soon descend on the city, and still the citizens had put them up.*
*It offered them safety, if only the illusion of it.*
*Other than that, she found the city to be a ghastly place. It's size belied the fact that most of it was empty.*
*Some of it deserted in anticipation of their arrival, but much more of it deserted far before then.*
*This was what it felt like to walk the streets of a dead city. To walk streets and squares build to hosts tens-of-thousands, now emptied out.*
*It was after nearly half-an-hour of marching that they met any opposition at all.*
*Coming upon an open city square, dominated by a large fountain which had long run dry, Sarah spotted a small unit of Bagrad soldiers.*
*All in all, it couldn't have been more than a dozen soldiers, each in a state of unpreparedness, still putting on their armor and sharpening their blades.*
*Too late for that, Sarah thought.*
Sarah: "Charge!"
*Her command send her own unit of soldiers rushing forward.*
*Outnumbering them by a solid margin and already hyped by the start of battle, Sarah knew instantly that this was no real fight.*
*Some of them scurried, but most of them simply stood in stunned silence.*
*Rushing up to them, Sarah came in close to a soldier. In his face, she could see only confusion. The last feeling he'd ever have.*
*She drove the blade through his shirt, into his heart.*
*Absent his armor, Sarah's blade cut right through him.*
*She heard him gargle a sound, but only blood poured from his mouth.*
*He still looked confused as he stumbled back, Sarah's blade sliding out of his chest, now covered in a bright red.*
*All around her, she saw her soldiers rush up against the other Bagrad soldiers.*
*Next to her, she saw a young Bagrad soldier, perhaps not even a man yet, fumbling for his sword.*
*Too late for that too, Sarah thought as she watched one of her men cut the boy down, slicing his neck open with the blade of an axe.*
*As the last of the Bagrad soldiers fell around her, she saw three men running away.*
Soldier: *Commander, should we give chase?*
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "Let them go. They're running away from the palace, no use wasting time trying to hunt them down."
*Sarah raised up her blood-stained sword and pointed towards the palace.*
Sarah: "Press on!"
*Again, under her command, her soldiers advanced ever forward.*
*Marching in the middle of her men, Sarah could feel the static in the air. Her senses growing deeper, more aware.*
*It hadn't been the first time she'd felt it.*
*Something always grew in the hearts of men in the middle of a battle. A kind of bloodlust, or perhaps survival instinct.*
*The more they killed, the more they fought, the deeper they would sink into that primal version of themselves.*
*The version that never cared for anything else, other than kill or be killed.*
*Sarah held onto the feeling, but ever careful not to sink into it. She'd seen more than her share of brutality, carried out on whim.*
*You're still human. You're still a Rose.*
*Suddenly, the road before them opened up in all directions.*
*Above her, the sky opened up, its light finally able to reach through and drive away the shade cast by the tall buildings.*
*The palace square.*
*Vast and open in a city otherwise drowned in buildings, it added to the majesty of the palace.*
*The palace of Bagrad stood alone, surrounded by nothing, and reaching far up into the heavens, almost piercing the sky.*
*For a moment, Sarah stood in awe of the monument. Then, a voice called out to her.*
Kate: "Sarah!"
Kate: "Over here!"
*Sarah turned away from the great building towards Kate's voice.*
*She saw Kate running up to her, followed by another cadre of soldiers.*
Sarah: "Kate!"
*She yelled out to her friend.*
*They had been through a lot together, survived one battle after the other, and still Sarah worried the same each time for Kate.*
Sarah: "What's the situation?"
Kate: "We faced minimal resistance coming up on the palace. We arrived here just a bit before you."
Sarah: "What about the other units?"
Kate: "Some others are still making their way, but Sarah..."
*Kate was hesitant with her words.*
*Sarah didn't have patience.*
Sarah: "What is it Kate, tell me."
Kate: "The units lead by Caleb and Ephraim had arrived here first. They were waiting when we arrived and they...they've already one in."
*Sarah cursed under her breath.*
Sarah: "They knew they had to wait here, to gather up all our strength before pressing into the palace."
Kate: "I know. I told them as much, but they...they just didn't listen."
Sarah: "Idiots. If they think they're going to get credit for going in first, despite my instructions, they'll have another thing coming."
Kate: "So what do we do?"
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "If they went in by themselves, we should move up as well."
Sarah: "We have most of the soldiers here now, the rest can catch up later."
Sarah: "I'm more worried that they've gotten themselves into any trouble."
*Kate nodded.*
Kate: "Alright, you heard the commander! Rally up and get ready to move into the palace."
*Sarah watched as the soldiers fell into formation, taking this small moment of respite to prepare themselves for the next part.*
*Outside, Sarah could see no serious troop presence.*
*A few faces lingered atop the towers of the castle, but Sarah couldn't even be certain they were soldiers. Perhaps simply scared civillians.*
*Had Castle Reinmeer looked like this when the tribesmen pillaged her homeland?*
*Sarah raised her sword.*
Sarah: "Advance!"
*Moving as one, the soldiers began a slow yet steady march up towards the palace.*
*Their heavy plated armor clattered with each step, causing their march to give off a dreadful rhythm.*
*Rising up the steps to the palace, Sarah kept scanning the upper reaches. Waiting for an ambush that never came.*
*Finally, her troops arrived at the great central gate and advanced into the palace.*
*Entering the palace, Sarah could feel the air instantly cool, covered from the scorching desert sun outside.*
*In the distance, she saw a few people run. Servants, perhaps.*
Sarah: "Keep advancing down the hallway. The entrance to the western wing should be nearby."
*Suddenly, screams rang out.*
*The great halls of the palace converted the screams into nightmarish echoes.*
*Her troops? Sarah couldn't be sure.*
Sarah: "Move up!"
*The soldiers increased their pace, marching faster through the halls of the palace.*
*As they drew nearer, Sarah could hear the screams grow louder and louder.*
*A smell hit her nostrils, one sadly not unfamiliar to her.*
*Burning flesh.*
*Taking the lead, Sarah turned the corner and saw the source of the screams.*
*A small ways off in the distance, nearer to the entrance of the western wing, Sarah could her own soldiers, cowering behind pillars.*
*All around them, deep ink black traces of soot were drawn across the floor and walls of the palace.*
*A blinding light.*
*Another set of screams.*
*Then, her eyes were drawn towards the object that hung in the center of the air, dominating all space around itself.*
*Radiant, like a miniature sun, lashes of fire struck out and incinerated soldiers as though they were nothing.*
*No.*
*Not an object, Sarah realized.*
*A person.*
*In the midsts of the artifical sun, a man stood as if suspended in the air, defying any laws of nature.*
*His eyes burned like coals in a forge.*
*It was impossible, and her mind screamed at the unnatural sight.*
*It was impossible, except for one kind of person.*
*A mage.*
Sarah: "Mage!"
*Sarah screamed out the word and a bolt of panic ran through her soldiers.*
*Each of them was battle-hardened, had seen battles and bloodshed countless times over.*
*They would charge into battle with song and drink themselves into a stupor to celebrate after.*
*But this was nothing like that.*
*Mages weren't like the rest of them, and their power far exceeded anything that that a single soldier might bring.*
*Her men were ready to die on a battlefield face-to-face with the enemy, full of glory, but few among them could face something so unnatural.*
*Despite everything in her body telling her to retreat, Sarah knew there was only one way forward.*
Sarah: "Advance!"
*Gathering up their morale, Sarah felt her soldiers move forward again, but she could sense their hesitation.*
*Sarah saw Kate come up beside her.*
Kate: "Here, take this."
*Kate handed her a bow and arrow.*
Sarah: "Thanks."
*Against a mage, the only reliable strategy was to run away. Since that was not an option, a bow and arrow was the least worst alternative.*
*As they drew nearer, Sarah could see the mage still hanging in the air, bringing down lashes of flame on any soldier that he could reach.*
*With most of the soldiers hiding behind pillars, it meant his slaughter was a slow one, but it also meant there was no resistance left against him.*
*Sarah could see the mage slowly drifting through the air, hunting down all those that remained.*
*Whenever he reached out, the flames swirled down on the soldiers, their screams filling up the hall.*
*Those that tried to run were swiftly burned as well.*
*They were trapped.*
*As Sarah and her soldiers marched up closer, the sound of their stomping boots drew the mage's attention.*
*He wheeled around in the air as if attached to a string.*
*Whatever held him up, if anything, Sarah couldn't see.*
*His mouth opened, and a song drowned out all the other sound in the world.*
*He sang in a language that Sarah had never heard before, and whose every syllable struck her as if profoundly alien to anything she'd ever come across.*
*Sarah felt the heat of the fire hit her before she turned and saw the bursting inferno.*
*A few rows over, some of her soldiers lit up, screaming their final words, their armors quickly melting against their bodies, trapping them inside them.*
*Morale broke nearly instantly, their ranks scattering.*
*Formations. Training. Morale. All of it was useless against a foe that could turn you to cinders simply by willing it so.*
*Sarah closed her fist around the bow and arrow. It felt like a joke compared to what she was seeing.*
Sarah: "Keep advancing!"
*She screamed, hoping at least some would gain courage from her words.*
*Mages.*
*Sarah had received limited instruction on dealing with them. People knew they were dangerous, exceedingly so, but they were also rare.*
*She had spoken with seasoned soldiers who had never seen a mage in more than a decade of soldiering.*
*Herself, she had only ever met a mage once when she was still little, perhaps only seven years old.*
*Hiding behind her father, she had greeted the man who had a kindly smile and a strange confident grace about him.*
*Later, her father had told her that the man could have burned down their castle with ease, and that only a fool would ever mess with a mage.*
*Turns out I'm the fool, father.*
*Mages and their orders mostly kept to themselves, and so they rarely entered the field of battle, unless it served their interests.*
*Whatever his purpose here was, Sarah could hardly begin to speculate.*
*It also didn't matter.*
*He was an obstacle, between herself and her goal, and she'd deal with it like any other she had dealt with.*
*Sarah kept pressing forward, only a handful of other soldiers continued along with her.*
*From the corner of her eyes, she could see Kate was one of them. Kate, despite everything that had happened between them, was one of the few people she knew she could rely on.*
*Another soldier burst into flame, the heat exploding outward so violently, Sarah could feel it sear her face.*
*Suddenly, the mage turned in the air. Away from Sarah and her soldiers.*
*For a moment, she felt grateful.*
Caleb: "You wanna fucking take someone on? How about you try me!"
*Sarah watched as Caleb ran up from behind a pillar, aiming a crossbow up at the mage.*
*A loud thumping sound rang out as the crossbow released the bolt.*
*In less than a fraction of second, the bolt crossed the distance and lodged itself...*
*In mid air.*
*Stunned, Sarah looked at the scene.*
*It would have hit him, she thought. No, it should have hit him. The arc of the bolt was perfect, only to end up suspended in the air, inches from the mage's face.*
*The air itself shimmered around where the bolt was suspended, like ripples across the surface of water.*
*The mage twisted his wrist.*
*Flames rose up around Caleb's feet.*
Ephraim: "Caleb!!!"
*Sarah heard Ephraim's screams.*
*She watched as Ephraim lunged for Caleb, tackling him.*
*Together the two tumbled across the stone floor. Only a fraction later did the ground erupt into flame, missing them by a hair.*
*We have to do something, Sarah told herself, commanding herself to press on.*
*But how...how could she kill something like this? She knew how to kill a man or a woman, but this was something almost otherwordly.*
*More fire rained down, striking up against one of the pillars.*
*Sarah ran forward.*
*Raising up the bow, she drew back the string, aiming down the sight of the arrow up towards the mage.*
*An explosion roared next to her.*
*She felt her legs slide out from under her, crashing hard against the stone floor of the palace.*
*All around her, she could see soldiers crawling, trying to get away.*
*Had it not been for her armor, Sarah wasn't so sure she would have survived.*
*Looking up from down on the ground, Sarah watched as the mage descended down onto the ground, his feet softly touching down.*
*Fire continued to swirl around, hunting down one soldier after the other.*
*Sarah watched him draw nearer to her.*
*More screams.*
*She'd never get up in time.*
*She could never get away.*
*Her bow...where was it?*
*Sarah looked around franctically trying to find it.*
*Then she saw it, snapped in half by the blast.*
*This is how I die? Sarah could hardly bring her mind to conceive of it.*
*She should have died of old age...or perhaps died trying to reclaim her kingdom...but like this? In some city on the other side of the world in a hallway?*
*No...*
*Not like this, she begged.*
*The mage stood over her, less than a feet away.*
*And passed her.*
*She felt the heat swirl, but the flame went for another.*
*How...*
*Had he thought she was dead already?*
*No...she was sure she had moved. He must have known, and yet, the mage walked past her.*
*Sarah forced herself to her feet, gripping her sword.*
*In front of her, only a step and a thrust away, the mage stood with his back turned to her.*
*She leapt forward with all her might and drove her blade out before her, thrusting it with both hands.*
*Sarah felt her blade connect, piercing through the mage's chest.*
*So great was the force that she could feel him stumble, nearly losing his footing.*
*She could see the mage's eyes grow wide, stunned.*
Xanthippe: "I..."
*He inspected the fatal wound, blood pouring out from it.*
*His eyes drifted back towards Sarah.*
*And yet, Sarah could see in his eyes that he didn't see her. Instead, his eyes drifted around her, near her, but never seeming to find her.*
*Impotently, the mage waved his hands in front of himself, too far to touch her.*
Xanthippe: "Where...where did you come from?"
Xanthippe: "Is this..."
Xanthippe: "I don't...I don't understand..."
*His words slowly faded as his face grew paler from loss of blood.*
*Sarah stepped forward and swiped her blade horizontally across his neck. The blade went through clean, cutting off the mage's head.*
*His head rolled across the palace floor as his body collapsed down as though a string had been cut.*
*Then, an explosion of sound all around her.*
*Sarah turned and saw countless soldiers. Her soldiers. Rushing up to her, joyous screams!*
*Mage killer. Mage killer. Mage killer.*
*Again and again, they chanted the title at her.*
*She felt them grab onto her, patting her on the back, trying to lift her up.*
*She pushed them away.*
Sarah: "We celebrate after! Right now, I want every single one of you to continue on to the western wing!"
Sarah: "You want to honour me? Then honour me by bringing me my prize!"
*In unison, the soldiers stomped their feet and began to storm down the hallway, their rupturous screams filling the hall, striking fear into any possible enemy.*
*Sarah leaned against the wall, trying to regain her senses.*
*She saw Kate come up to her.*
Kate: "Sarah!"
Kate: "Are you alright?"
*Sarah checked her body for injuries but found none.*
Sarah: "Yeah, I think I am."
Kate: "That was...how did you do that?"
Sarah: "I don't know. It wasn't anything I did, he just...he seemed not to notice me and when I got up he had his back to me and..."
Kate: "It was incredible!"
Kate: "You killed a mage! You know how many people can say that?"
*Sarah wasn't sure she could be so happy.*
*Perhaps if she had known how she had done it, she could celebrate, but now the whole affair was only strange to her.*
*Had she killed him, or simply gotten lucky? Or perhaps there was something else.*
*How had he not seen her?*
*Sarah felt Kate hug her.*
Kate: "I was so scared. I really thought when he got that close to you that it was over..."
Sarah: "Yeah, me too."
*Sarah felt Kate press her lips up against hers.*
Kate: "I was afraid I'd lose you..."
*Sarah kissed her back.*
Sarah: "I'm not going anywhere."
Sarah: "Come on, you catch up to the rest of them, I'll be right behind."
*Sarah patted Kate on the back.*
Sarah: "Come on, you catch up to the rest of them, I'll be right behind."
*Sarah watched Kate run after the other soldiers.*
*She turned towards the center of the hallway.*
*Sitting down on the ground, she saw Ephraim, holding Caleb in his arms.*
*Sarah walked up to him. If he noticed her, he didn't show it.*
Sarah: "Ephraim..."
*She softly said his name, afraid she was intruding upon his quiet grief.*
Sarah: "Ephraim...I saw what happened."
Sarah: "Will Caleb be alright?"
*He slowly tilted his head and nodded.*
*She saw tears were flowing down his face.*
Ephraim: "The medics just took him away. They said he should be fine. Some light burn wounds and some head trauma."
*Ephraim laughed a pained laugh.*
Ephraim: "Maybe me tackling him is going to end up having done the most damage to him."
Sarah: "Eph...if you hadn't stepped in, Caleb would have been dead."
Ephraim: "He just...he saw that this fucking mage was coming for me and then he..."
*He wiped his face.*
Ephraim: "I was so scared...Sarah"
*Sarah knelt down beside him, putting one arm around him.*
Sarah: "He did what he did because...because he cared for you, Ephraim."
Sarah: "Caleb is the kind of guy that...he could never have lived with himself if he had stood by and watched someone he loved get hurt."
Sarah: "And he always acts before thinking."
*Sarah watched Ephraim chuckle through his pain.*
Ephraim: "Yeah...he really is like that."
Ephraim: "Why do I always have to love the foolish ones?"
*A heavy pause lingered.*
Ephraim: "He and I, we've been doing this work ever since we left out village. Always side by side."
*He turned his tear stained face towards her.*
Sarah: "I know, Ephraim."
Sarah: "I can't...I can't begin to think of what he means to you."
*She hugged him.*
*Through her armor, she could feel he hugged her back.*
Sarah: "Now Ephraim, look at me."
*Sarah seized his face between her hands.*
Sarah: "We're in the palace. This battle isn't over yet."
Sarah: "We need to keep going. You need to keep going."
Sarah: "Don't stay here by yourself. If you die, him risking his life will have been for nothing."
*She could feel him nod.*
Sarah: "So get up."
*Sarah stood up and stretched out her hand.*
*Ephraim took it, standing up to his feet.*
Sarah: "We're gonna teach these fuckers a lesson they won't soon forget."
*Raising his sword over his head, he screamed a terifying battle scream, and began to run.*
*As Ephraim took off, Sarah ran after him and the other soldiers.*
*When Sarah finally caught up to the core of her unit she found Kate waiting for her.*
*Kate was standing next to an arch that nearly rose up as high as the ceilings.*
*The entrance to the western wing of the palace, the only way in or out.*
*Next to the gate, three Bagrad guards were laying in a pool of blood. They didn't move, their faces a sickly grey colour.*
Kate: "Poor bastards were guarding the entrance."
Sarah: "Brave of them to stay at their post."
*Kate shrugged.*
Kate: "Brave or just stupid?"
Kate: "They threw their lives away, three of them trying hold off five-hundred of us. They didn't even hold us off for more than a second."
Kate: "And for what?"
Kate: "You think the asshole that owns this palace will even remember their names?"
*Sarah looked at their bodies.*
*Choose*
*Agree with Kate*:
*Sarah couldn't help but find herself agreeing with Kate.*
Sarah: "I guess you're right."
Sarah: "What a waste of a life, and whose going to remember them?"
Kate: "Not me."
*Kate spat on the ground near their bodies.*
Kate: "They would have killed me as gladly as I would have killed them."
Kate: "That's the real world. You're either killing or being killed. Life is just trying to stay on top for as long as you can."
*Sarah looked at Kate.*
Sarah: "What a grim way to live."
*Kate shrugged.*
Kate: "Grim, maybe. All I care about is true, and it's true."
*Disagree with Kate*:
*Sarah couldn't find herself agreeing with Kate. She was always too much of a cynic.*
Sarah: "These men made a vow and they kept it, even if it meant giving up their lives."
Sarah: "I think that's admirable."
*Kate spat on the ground near their bodies.*
Kate: "I think that's the old Sarah talking, the one that read too many books about knights and shit."
*Sarah turned to her.*
Sarah: "I'm still the the same Sarah."
*Kate laughed.*
Kate: "Maybe we can agree on that."
*Sarah turned back towards the gate that lead into the western wing.*
*Through the gate, she could see her men rushing frantically in ever direction.*
*This wasn't a battle anymore. They were looting, and each of them was feverishly trying to get the best piece for themself.*
*Sarah hoped they'd find more gold than women.*
Sarah: "Shouldn't you be out there with the rest of them?"
*Kate shook her head.*
Kate: "My men know they gotta kick back a share of what they find to me."
Kate: "They can do the grunt work of ripping open drawers, hoping to find a necklace. Gods know I did that shit long enough."
*Sarah saw entire chests being dragged out onto the hallway and turned over.*
*Mountains of clothes spewed forth.*
*A single golden ring flew out, scattering across the floor with a loud pinging noise.*
*As one, the soldiers leapt after it, trying to secure it for themself.*
*Sarah's eyes drifted back towards the mountain of clothes that had been thrown on the floor.*
*They dresses were made of a fine silk, a rich embroidery decorating from the waist down to the skirt line.*
*Did they know that a single one of those dresses was worth a month's wages? Probably not, she concluded.*
Sarah: "You see anything you like?"
*Sarah pointed towards the mountain of clothes.*
*Kate shrugged.*
Kate: "Not really my style I'm afraid."
Kate: "But I'd like to see you try them on."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Yeah, I bet you would like that."
*She turned towards Kate.*
Sarah: "Tell me, is it just gold so far or..."
*Sarah knew that Kate understood what she was asking.*
Kate: "Most of it, but there have been a few servants that were hiding."
Kate: "I told them to round up the children in the side room over there, keep them from seeing the worst of it."
Kate: "There are a few bodies in the rooms, male servants that were trying to hide."
Kate: "I think six or so female servants, they're...well off in that room."
*Kate pointed.*
*In the years she had worked with the mercenary company, Sarah had seen more than her share of brutality.*
*The simple truth was that, as much as she liked to call these people her brothers, they were overwhelmingly vile people.*
*Not to her, no they adored her, but to anyone outside of the company, they showed little mercy.*
*In her earlier days, Sarah had thought that she would put a stop to it, but the real world wasn't that simple.*
*The soldiers considered captured women a part of their reward, little different than the gold they looted.*
*It horrified Sarah, if only because she could see herself so easily in those women.*
*Had she not run away with Kate when she did, she would have been one of those women, captured and who knew what else by the tribesmen.*
*And yet she had also never been able to truly change anything.*
*If she tried to warn the soldiers, they'd do it in secret. If she spoke out publicy, they resented her.*
*In the end, she also simply could not be everywhere.*
*For every brutality she saw, there was a hundred more that happened outside of her view, outside of her command.*
*On a deeper level, Sarah also knew that she needed these men.*
*If she ever wanted any hope of reclaiming Rosanna, she would need these men. These monsters.*
*That meant bringing them over to her side. For some that was inspiring their hearts, but for many more it was simply filling their greed and urges.*
*Sarah felt a tear streak past her cheek.*
*What kind of a leader could she ever hope to be if he road back to power was paved by this horror?*
*Or was that how the real monsters of the world, like the tribesmen, stayed in power? By hoping that good people like herself were too kind-hearted to fight back?*
*Was she a good person?*
*Sarah felt her mind race, then forced herself to clear it.*
*The battle isn't over yet. Stay focussed.*
Sarah: "Kate, gather up some men and instruct them to gather up material to build a barricade."
Kate: "Yes, commander!"
*Kate saluted and began shouting at some of the soldiers nearby, yelling instructions.*
*Sarah looked up as she walked through the gateway. The ceiling on the other end rose up far higher, making the space feel even larger.*
*As she slowly explored the western wing, she tried to pay little attention to the chaos around her.*
*For most mercenaries, looting was an important part of survival, compensating for their otherwise limited wages.*
*A scream rang out from one of the rooms off to her side.*
*Sarah turned and watched a woman, dragged along by the hem of her shirt, a soldier pulling her violently.*
*Say something.*
*Why won't you say something?*
*Sarah turned away and continued to walk down the hall of the western wing, the screams of the woman slowly fading away behind her.*
*Was this world really as cold and indifferent as Kate believed?*
*Nearly every door in the hall was either already breached or was being chopped away at by soldiers with axes.*
*Splinters flew out, scattering across the floor.*
*This was how an empire died. Violently.*
*As she walked past the rooms, she could see inside of them.*
*Scattered across the floors of the rooms, all the things that soldiers couldn't be bothered to loot.*
*In some of the rooms, she saw the faces of the servants.*
*Their eyes hollow. Faces turned down to the floor. A broken people. A conquered people.*
*Sarah had seen it before, and it frightened her almost more than the blood did.*
*A kind of death of spirit. People too defeated to fight back, but too desperate for life to give up, caught in some nightmarish liminal space.*
*Sarah kept walking.*
*Each room was the same and yet different. Some degree of chaos. Some degree of sadness.*
*She was part of this. Her hands were stained as much as any that did the killing. Perhaps more, given her command.*
*Still, she walked the hall to bear witness to what she was a part to. It was the least she felt she could do.*
*Finally, she reached the end of the western wing.*
*Turning back around she could see the carnage behind her had only grown as more trinkets and jewels were hauled out. More people dragged away.*
*Near the far end, she could see the entrance.*
*An initial barrier made out of wood was partially constructed.*
*Soldiers buzzed up and away from it, slowly adding to the construct, slowly sealing up the only way in or out.*
*Sarah had done as Vaelen had asked of her, secured the western wing.*
*With the most immediate danger behind her, she couldn't help but go back to wondering what all this was about.*
*As far as Sarah could see, every room was richly filled, but none of it seemed particularly valuable, or at least not valuable enough to risk such a reckless attack.*
*Sarah sat down against one of the walls.*
*She pulled her blade from its sheath and laid it out across her lap.*
*As she continued to observe the hall and the soldiers ransacking every room, she drew a whetstone across the blade.*
*The soft grinding sound of her blade sharpening could faintly be heard amidsts the chaos.*
*Several hours passed.*
*With the western wing now fully secured and barricaded, no attack from Bagrad's forces ever manifested.*
*Perhaps they had dug in too deep, or perhaps the Bagrad army was stretched too thin trying to defend the city's main gate from falling.*
*As time progressed, occasional fragments of news slipped through.*
*First the city's main gate fell.*
*Then the slaughter took to the street.*
*By now, the Mythran army and Vaelen's auxillary forces were close enough to the palace that they could be heard.*
*Sarah simply sat and watched.*
*There was no reason to abandon her position.*
*It was such, sitting and waiting, that Sarah was finally approached by one of the soldiers that worked as a messenger.*
Soldier: *Commander!*
*He saluted her.*
Sarah: "Any news?"
Soldier: *Yes, commander Rose. Lord Vaelen has arrived at the barricade and has requested your presence.*
Sarah: "He's not a lord."
Soldier: *Excuse me?*
*Sarah waved her hand, dismissing the matter.*
Sarah: "Forget it. I'll go see him. Thank you for informing me."
*Sarah walked through the hallway up to the barricade.*
*The chaotic looting had slowed down now that most of the items of value had been found and collected.*
*Sarah climbed up the barricade and peered over the edge.*
Sarah: "Well, if it isn't our brave leader."
Sarah: "Hope you haven't come to take some of my glory?"
*He smiled at her in that confident, knowing way.*
Vaelen: "I wouldn't dream of it."
*He gestured at the barricade.*
Vaelen: "Seems like you've done alright for yourself."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "Captured and secured, just as you instructed."
Vaelen: "I knew I could count on you."
*Vaelen looked around, studying the construction.*
Vaelen: "What is this I heard about a mage?"
*Sarah shrugged.*
Sarah: "Ooh, I killed a mage. No big deal, really. You never killed a mage before?"
*Vaelen laughed.*
Vaelen: "No, Sarah, as a matter of fact I never have, and I think very few people in this world can say that they have."
*He paused for a moment.*
Vaelen: "I am happy that my faith in you has proven to be well placed."
Vaelen: "You did good work today. Not just with the mage, but also this."
*Sarah leapt down from the barricade and came up closer to Vaelen.*
Sarah: "Well, we lost a few men today, so it's a bit hard to celebrate."
*He looked at her intensely.*
Vaelen: "Good soldiers dying is always a tragedy."
Vaelen: "It's gruesome business, soldiering. But as much as we try to turn our hearts to stone, we still feel every loss."
Vaelen: "But maybe that's better. Reminds us that we're still human, despite everything."
*Sarah looked intently at Vaelen.*
Sarah: "I'm surprised."
Vaelen: "About what? That I have emotions?"
Sarah: "A little bit."
*Vaelen shrugged.*
Vaelen: "Look, Sarah, I don't wear mine on my sleeves, but it hurts me too."
Vaelen: "I have thousands of men under my command. Men that rely on my to keep them safe and employed."
Vaelen: "If I broke down at every death, I would never have been able to get to where I am today."
Vaelen: "But that doesn't mean I don't care about them."
*Sarah turned her eyes down towards the ground.*
Sarah: "Yeah, I know. I didn't mean anything by it."
Vaelen: "Of course, and I take no offense."
*He placed a hand on her shoulder.*
Vaelen: "Just know that I'm proud of you today. When the day is over and we celebrate those that survived, you will be honoured, trust me."
Sarah: "Thank you Vaelen."
*Sarah pointed towards the barricade behind her.*
Sarah: "What about this?"
Vaelen: "Keep it up."
Vaelen: "We want to keep the Mythrans out as much as the remnants of the Bagrad army."
Vaelen: "Unless I give you an explicit order, this stays up and nobody goes inside without my express permission, understand?"
*Sarah saluted him.*
Sarah: "Yes sir, not a soul."
*He smiled at her.*
Vaelen: "I wish all my commanders were as reliable as you."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Wouldn't be much work left for you if everyone did their jobs as well as I do mine, right?"
Vaelen: "I suppose that's true."
*She saw him turn around, looking down the far end of the hallway.*
Vaelen: "Anyway, Sarah, I didn't just come here to talk."
Vaelen: "I wanted to let you know that the last of the Bagrad forces have collapsed. We're now cleaning up small pockets of resistance, but the battle is over."
Vaelen: "The Mythran prince has entered the city and he's drawing closer to the palace."
Vaelen: "Once he gets here, he will demand the Shah surrender himself and his family."
Sarah: "They haven't done so yet?"
*Vaelen shook his head.*
Vaelen: "They're still barricaded up in the throne room, back in the royal quarters."
Vaelen: "I came here to ask you to join me."
Sarah: "Join you?"
Vaelen: "Yes. I want you to be there with me when the Mythran army hands over their demand for surrender."
Sarah: "You think the Bagrad royal family will resist?"
*Vaelen shook his head.*
Vaelen: "Their army is broken. Their guards have abandoned their posts. The city is lost."
Vaelen: "It's just...a tense moment."
Vaelen: "If not for you, I'm the only one from the Brothers of Providence. I'd like to have more friendly faces in the room. Just in case."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "Sure, I'll come along. I'll bring a handful of soldiers along, just in case."
Vaelen: "Excellent. We'll need to move soon, their army is going to be entering the throne room any moment."
*Sarah selected a handful of soldiers.*
*It wasn't much, especially not if the Mythrans would decide to cross them, but it would be enough to put up a short fight. Perhaps enough to run away.*
*Sarah had come to learn that a lot could go wrong near the end of a contract.*
*More than one lord or lady had tried to short them on their pay when it came time to pay up.*
*With her personal entourage in tow, Sarah linked up with Vaelen and together they sat off for the throne room.*
*Arriving in the throne room, Sarah could see that there was already a significant presence of Mythran soldiers.*
*Their army was larger than their mercenary company by many times, and still, it represented only a small part of the total Mythran army.*
*Mythra truly was a superpower without equals.*
*It was fortunate then for the rest of the world that Mythra was so prone to infighting, or else every living soul would have to answer to them.*
*Sarah marched slightly behind Vaelen, past the host of Mythran soldiers.*
*Near the front, she saw that the Mythran prince was already waiting.*
Mythran Prince: *Shah Mahda! Come out of your little rat hiding hole before I send in my men to drag you out like the vermin you are.*
Mythran Prince: *If you're not going to live honorably, at least you can die honorably.*
*There came no response.*
Mythran Prince: *Whatever, I don't have the patience for this. Men! Tear down the barricade and drag these rats out, alive!*
*A sound cut through all the others, as the room went silent.*
*The clattering of wood, then steel.*
*Piece by piece, the fragments that made up the barricade to the royal quarters came down, being taken apart from the inside.*
*Climbing out through the small passage, was the Shah.*
Mythran Prince: *Aah, finally. I was afraid my men would have to break a sweat getting you out of there.*
*Sarah watched the Shah walk up towards them.*
*Despite having lost, he seemed entirely unaffected. He still walked with the confidence of kings, the kind that reminded her of her own father.*
*His imperial gaze slowly drifted across the room.*
*For a moment, his eyes settled on Sarah. She could feel herself pinned to the ground.*
Shah Mahda: "I see your mercenary lapdogs are here."
*The Mythran prince laughed.*
Mythran Prince: *Aah, it speaks. I was beginning to think you'd be too scared to even come out.*
Shah Mahda: "A worm like you won't make me cower."
*Sarah could see rage flash across the face of the Mythran prince.*
Mythran Prince: *You killed my nephew. You brought all this upon yourself, remember that while you hear your family get tortured to death.*
*Sarah could see the Shah's face. It didn't move at all.*
*She leaned in to Vaelen and whispered to him.*
Sarah: "There's something wrong."
Vaelen: "What do you mean?"
Sarah: "Why...why is he out here?"
Vaelen: "To surrender, what else?"
Sarah: "Does he look like someone that is about to surrender?"
*Vaelen didn't answer her.*
*The Mythran prince moved closer towards the Shah.*
Mythran Prince: *Enough! You and the rest of your debased dynasty have been tolerated long enough.*
Mythran Prince: *Your allies have abandoned you. Your armies are shattered. Your city will soon be put to the sword. You've lost!*
Shah Mahda: "Not all my allies have abandoned my house."
*A pause lingered in the room.*
Mythran Prince: *Soldiers! Seize him, strip him and whip him till he begs for mercy! Maybe that will bring some sense back to him.*
*Sarah watched as a small cadre of soldiers began to move forward.*
*Suddenly, they stopped.*
*Turning her eyes back towards the Shah, she saw the object emerge from his robes.*
*A dagger. A handle as black as obsidian, a blade glowing in deep crimson red.*
*She watched as the Shah raised his arm high above his head.*
*The room had gone silent.*
*Though none could say why, everyone could feel the item reverberate. A thing that commanded respect, awe.*
Shah Mahda: "My family hails back centuries. Millenia."
Shah Mahda: "My allies on this side have failed me, but my allies on the other side won't!"
*With a single slash, Sarah watched the dagger cut through the air.*
*At first, she believed it had been nothing. Perhaps a final gesture from a man truly gone insane.*
*But then she could see.*
*Tracing the movement of the blade, Sarah could see the glimmer of a cut. A wound across the face of creation.*
*Rapidly expanding, the wound grew and grew, and Sarah could now see into it. A void, deeper more devoid of light than any she had ever known.*
*Then two sets of claws emerged, seizing upon the wound and tearing it open entirely.*
*Birthed from this violation of reality, a creature slithered out.*
*It's body black as ink, it slithered and moved like a snake.*
*It's brute claws pierced the stone of the old palace, and with great effort it pulled itself out from whatever dimension it called home, into Sarah's world.*
*The thing's face, as white as a mask made out of porcelain, it's only feature its pitless eyes and razor teeth like those of a shark.*
*Having looked on, first in stunned silence, a single soldier was the first to break their collective trauma.*
*A scream rang out. Then, a chorus of countless soldiers, screaming.*
*Sarah watched as the beast suddenly leapt forward with a speed that belied its enormous size.*
*The thing stood before the Mythran prince, who looked up at it.*
*So great was his fear of the thing, that even the idea of resisting his own death filled him with dread.*
*The creature's snakelike body sat half upright. Even so, it towered over the Mythran prince by at least three times.*
*Then it snapped.*
*The creature's mouth snapped around the Mythran prince's head, catching him across his shoulder and upper chest with its teeth.*
*In one fell gulp, Sarah watched the Mythran prince be swallowed, dissapearing into the creature's stomach.*
*If the prince had screamed, Sarah didn't hear it.*
*The only sound she could hear for certain among the chaos and screams, was the laughing.*
*The Shah, beyond himself, laughing hysterically at the carnage.*
Sarah: "We need to leave!"
*Sarah gripped Vaelen by the shoulder.*
*She felt his body flinch, as if she had pulled him from somewhere very far away.*
Sarah: "Now! Or that thing is gonna kill us all!"
Vaelen: "Yes...yes! Run!"
*Together, they began to run towards the only exit that the throne room had.*
*As they ran, Sarah could feel the chaos in the room growing as soldiers all around them were wildly running, many dropping their weapons, falling, tumbling over one another.*
*A shade rushed by her.*
*Sarah saw the creature, it's limbs wildly flailing as it dragged its own snake body across the throne room.*
*It was fast. So fast.*
*Before she realized, the thing had placed itself between the door and the soldiers.*
*An entire army trembled.*
*Whatever the thing was, it possessed enough intelligence to block their escape.*
*Sarah watched the thing coil its body and snap foward.*
*A soldier, too far out from the others, caught in the things teeth.*
*He screamed as the creature ripped off and swallowed his arm, the blood pooling from his wound.*
*Sarah felt her heart sink.*
*The soldier had worn armor, perhaps even better than the kind anyone in her mercenary company had, and the creature had sliced through it like it was nothing.*
*Suddenly it rushed forward.*
*As it reached the center of the soldiers, it turned around on itself, its tail striking out like a whip.*
*A group of soldiers, too slow to run away, exploded into red mist as the thing's tail slashed through them.*
*There was no time to process.*
*As it spun and whipped its tail, its claws reached out, gripping, crushing anyone it caught in its range.*
*It moved with such speed that no sooner had the soldiers turned to it, then it had already positioned itself anew.*
*Each time a group of soldiers tried to rush for the door, the creature would snap back, catching them.*
*Sarah felt the screams grow louder.*
*Soldiers were running off into every direction, but the army was trapped in the room with no escape.*
*And yet they still ran, if only so they could hope to die last.*
*Sarah watched Vaelen, knelt down, hoping to hide himself from the creature's sight.*
*Even he didn't have a plan for them to escape.*
*They were all going to die.*
*Sarah knew it as surely as she had ever known anything in her life. In her mind's eye, she could see it play out again and again.*
*Then, her heart soared.*
*The screams slowly faded around her. A different voice spoke. It to spoke to her with her own voice, yet she knew it to be different.*
Sarah: "Stay here!"
Vaelen: "What are you going to do?"
Sarah: "Just stay here and no matter what, don't try to make a run for the door."
*Sarah strode out onto the center of the throne room, drawing out her blade from its sheath.*
*Each step measured. Each step exactly as she knew it.*
*All around her, a vast space. Most soldiers had ran for the edges of the room, hiding behind pillars or any other object that might give them shelter.*
*The center was open.*
*Seizing her blade with both hands, Sarah raised her sword up besides herself.*
Sarah: "Come!"
*She screamed the word, half to challenge, half to bolster her own confidence.*
*The creature turned towards her, as if obeying her command.*
*She stared into its face and she could see, despite for lack of its eyes, the thing looked back into her.*
*Why.*
*The only thought that Sarah could ask herself, again and again.*
*And yet, as though her body moved to a different beat, she had ventured out to face the creature.*
*For a moment, the thing lingered.*
*Then, the thing's tail sprung like a coil, launching itself towards her.*
*By less than a heartbeat, Sarah stepped aside and felt the creature rush past her.*
*She felt the tremors and heard the creature's claws digging into the earth, halting its rush and allowing it to turn back to her.*
*Sarah spun and thrusted out her blade, catching the creature in its face.*
*Suddenly, the beast lunged back, surprised that anything might have hurt it.*
*Sarah could see something in the beast's movements. An uncertainty.*
*The moment passed as the thing launched itself upwards, descending upon her again, now from above.*
*Sarah rolled and swung her blade up in an arc, catching the creature by the joint of its leg.*
*A deafening scream erupted from the creature as it crashed into the stone floor, its limb flopping against the ground with a loud thud.*
*But her body moved quicker still.*
*Spinning around again, Sarah brought her blade down with a plowman's strength, hewing her sword deep into its back.*
*A black liquid spewed out, covering part of her face and armor, and the beast roared again.*
*As she pulled her blade back, she could feel the thing's flesh rip and tear.*
*Raising her sword high above her head, she brought it down again with both hands.*
*Again, she could feel the beast thrash. Its scream drowned out all other senses. More blood spewed forth, pooling on the floor.*
*Rip.*
*Tear.*
*Raising her sword above her head for yet another blow, Sarah caught a shade moving in the corner of her eyes.*
*Too late, Sarah only realized it was the creature's tail when it struck her across the head.*
*So great was the impact of the force that Sarah felt herself topple over, her entire body spinning, rolling across the floor, the clattering of metal as her armor broke her fall.*
*Hold on, she screamed in her mind, hold onto your sword.*
*When she finally stopped rolling, Sarah tried to push herself back up.*
*No sooner did she try when she saw the creature lunge for her.*
*She rolled to the side, again the creature missed her.*
*She felt it reach for her with the stump of its limb.*
*Continuing the motion of her roll, Sarah positioned herself back onto her feet.*
*This time, she caught the thing's tail in time.*
*Ducking low and raising her blade up, she felt it cut through the thing's tail as the beast swiped it into her blade. A loud thud of something falling behind her.*
*Its face rushed towards her.*
*The thing's razor sharp teeth, a mouth opening and shutting with a sickening chomp.*
*She stepped back, sweeping her blade across as she kept stepping backwards, she caught the creature across its face, holding it off, injuring each time it tried to snap her in its jaws.*
*A fury was building in the thing, she could hear its screams mix with an animalistic fury, something close to a hiss.*
*As it began to wildly swipe its claws at her, Sarah dove in under it, thrusting her blade up, she caught another of the creature's limbs.*
*For a moment, her blade remained buried in the beast flesh, but with a titan's effort, Sarah pulled out the blade, cutting away what little remained of the creature's limb.*
*Leaping back, Sarah looked upon the thing.*
*Deprived of two of its limbs, the thing stumbled upon itself, its inky belly slithering across the floor, leaving a pool of black blood as it tried to approach her.*
*It's hissing had grown deeper, more exhausted, its attacks slower.*
*As it lunged for her again, Sarah was ready, bringing her blade down across its face, splitting the thing's mask apart.*
*It screamed more loudly than it ever had before.*
*All of its body flinched and writhed around the room, thrasing violently as it sought to deal with the pain.*
*But with each wild movement, its body slowed.*
*With each scream, its voice dimmed.*
*Slowly, the thing began to drag, and eventually, ceased to move altogther.*
*Sarah walked around the thing, careful.*
*She saw the thing's body rise and fall, its breathing laboured.*
*As she moved in closer, the creature swiped for her with its claws, but by now it was so slow that it had no chance to catch her.*
*Stepping back, Sarah dodged the beast's hopeless attack, and again moved in closer.*
*Leaping forward, Sarah drove her blade deep into the creature's belly.*
*More of its black innards and blood spewed out across the floor, but now the creature was too weak even too cry out. It only grunted in deep pain.*
*Sarah pulled her blade out, raised it over her head, and with the force of both hands hewed it into the creature.*
*Rip. Tear. Pull.*
*Again. Again. Again.*
*Sarah felt her face, her hair, her armor, covered in the creature's ichor.*
*So drenched in the thing's blood, Sarah could feel even her grip on her sword's handle slip.*
*But she committed herself to her butcher's work with a zeal, strengthened her grip, and hewed the blade down again.*
*She had ceased to count, but somewhere in the slaughter, she finally regained her senses.*
*Her blade remained buried in the body of the beast, but it no longer moved. It no longer made a sound.*

*Half an hour passed before they concluded their discussion and went to confront Vaelen.*
*Arriving in Vaelen's tent, they found him already waiting for them.*
Vaelen: "Have you found me the answer I'm looking for?"
*Sarah nodded, stepping forward.*
Sarah: "Yes, we have."
*Vaelen gestured at her.*
Vaelen: "Well, out with it then."
*Sarah gathered her words carefully, then spoke.*
Sarah: "With the condition of the road going forward, our wagons will simply be inoperable."
Sarah: "The alternative would be to proceed on foot, but this would mean leaving behind the majority of our supplies."
*She paused for a moment.*
Sarah: "The only viable option would be to break the wheels on some of the wagons and re-build them with a sort of sled-like construction."
Sarah: "This will allow them to be pulled across the sand."
Sarah: "However, our horses are barely suited for the road as it is, and they won't serve us much further into the desert."
Sarah: "This means that soldiers will have to pull the converted wagons, and we don't have enough soldiers to bring all the wagons."
Sarah: "And so that will mean still having to abandon close to eighty-percent of our current wagons."
Sarah: "We will have to prioritize wagons containing water and food, so in essence...we would have to abandon nearly all war loot from Bagrad."
*Sarah decided to stop speaking, letting her words linger.*
*It was an unacceptable solution.*
*The burden that a march on foot through the desert imposed, combined with asking the soldiers to abandon their stolen goods, it would be too much to ask of them.*
Vaelen: "Very well."
Vaelen: "I'll draft the orders right away. We need to be moving before nightfall, I want us to make up for lost time."
*Sarah felt his words hit her like a punch to her stomach.*
*She turned to Gideon, trying to speak to him with her eyes.*
*He seemed as lost as he was.*
*She motioned for him to speak up.*
Gideon: "Sir, you understand that-"
Vaelen: "I do. I understand the demands I am making, and that they will not be easy."
Gideon: "Sir, this goes beyond that."
Gideon: "If we ask the men to abandon their loot..."
*Vaelen waved his hand, dismissing the concern.*
Vaelen: "I will sign the order, in my name. There won't be a soldier in the camp that will disobey such a direct order."
*Vaelen's pen flashes across a series of documents, applying his signature.*
*He grabbed the documents and held them out to them.*
Vaelen: "Go, make the preparations."
Vaelen: "Get this convoy moving. You find anyone objecting, feel free to have them whipped."
*With that, the matter was settled.*
*Sarah arrived at Gideon's tent only a moment later.*
Sarah: "This is insane. We can't go through with this."
Gideon: "I agree, but we don't have a choice. He's going to go through with this no matter what."
Sarah: "So what then? We just march our men into certain death?"
*Sarah watched as Gideon sat down, rubbing his temples.*
Gideon: "We've done all we can in terms of talking sense into him. If he won't listen, I don't know what else there is left to do."
*Sarah paced back and forth in the tent.*
*After a while, she finally stopped and turned to face Gideon again.*
Sarah: "A lot of people are going to die if we do this. Our people, the one's were supposed to responsible for."
*Gideon nodded.*
Gideon: "I'm not any happier about this than you."
Sarah: "And still we press on?"
Gideon: "We...we'll just have to trust that he has a plan. Who knows, maybe it will all work out like it always does."
*Gideon's voice trailed off as though he had failed to convince even himself.*
*For a moment longer, the two stood in silence, searching for a solution that didn't exist.*
*In the end, they did the only thing they could, and followed Vaelen's orders.*
*Passed down from commanders, to officers, down to the rank-and-file of the mercenary company, the word slowly spread.*
*All reacted with the same incredulity.*
*But as the orders were repeated, disbelief gave way to growing rage.*
*Shouting, screaming and even occasional bouts of violence.*
*Each man had become rich off their campaign in Bagrad, and each was now asked to leave their wealth behind in the sands of the desert.*
*They'd return, they were promised, but few believed so.*
*In their minds, each had spend their fortune a hundred times over, and now instead, they were given only the promise of a hollow march.*
*A violent, brutal campaign deeper into a forsaken desert.*
*On the other side, no promises of plunder or glory, only the name of a town that meant nothing to any of them.*
*The most resistant of them were punished, and before long, the men committed themselves to carrying out the work that seemed so bizarre to them.*
*There was of course the alternative, to turn around and walk back the five days to Bagrad, but such was a death sentence.*
*Behind them, certain death, ahead of them, a likelihood of death.*
*Each knew they could not truly resist, and so each yielded.*
*But Sarah could see in their eyes what most of the other officers and commanders failed to see.*
*She could see that these men and their submission, did not equal their consent.*
*She could see how each of these men who now did as he was told, added their outrage and hatred to the ledger of their soul.*
*Growing and accumulating within them, the weight of their anger.*
*They did as they were told, but a cold rage was growing in them.*
*Did Vaelen not see it, she wondered, or did he not want to see it? Did he not care?*
*Sarah wished she knew the answer to any of it. Instead, she merely excercised control over what little she could affect, and instructed the men on rebuilding the wagons.*
*The wooden wheels splintered as hammers struck them.*
*The slabs of wood were mounted underneath those carts deemed most essential, the food supplies, the water storage.*
*The rest of the wagons were left behind by the side of the road, a fortune left to nothing but the elements.*
*To the men, Sarah could see that this wealth meant much more than just the monetary value.*
*It was the thing they had risked their lives for.*
*This was how all mercenaries lived. They risked their life for wealth, and then they were afforded the chance to spend it.*
*Spending the wealth would remind them later of why they fought, motivate them to suffer the hardships of martial life.*
*That promise, of war, then comfort, had now been crudely violated by Vaelen.*
*Trial now followed war, and no promise of comfort seemed near.*
*And still they labored.*
*Shattering the wheels of the wagons and transforming their convoy to one that could withstand the brutal road ahead.*
*With great worry, Sarah overlooked them.*
*One week had passed since they had first set foot beyond the road.*
*A week since they had broken their own wagons and transformed them.*
*Upon the back of each man and woman now balanced a weight as great as they could manage.*
*The great wagons, now converted to sleds that could be pulled across the desert sand, were dragged along by great ropes.*
*Soldiers were rotated in and out from pulling the great ropes.*
*The desert, ever treacherous, continued to drag the soldiers deeper.*
*Their feet sank deep into the sand, slowing down their already reduced march to a crawl.*
*And above all, there was the merciless assault of the sun.*
*Where first the soldiers had cried out against it, hurled their insults, there was now only a brooding hatred for the thing.*
*Those who dared to say anything of the sun, the heat, were met only by angry glares.*
*Each knew of the torment of the sun. Each knew of the torment of the heat. None needed the torment of a fool speaking the obvious.*
*And so, with each passing day, they ventured further and deeper into the desert.*
*Guided by the measures of the shadows, the rising and setting of the sun, they did their best to keep their course.*
*After another hard day's march, the company set up camp and Sarah took what little rest she could find.*
*Leaning back against a rock, a rare bit of hard surface, she let the embers of the campfire glow on her face.*
*Samayra sat next to her.*
*The poor girl had been born to a life in the palace and now she had to suffer through something even Sarah struggled with.*
*Sarah could see in her face that she tried to be strong, but the trip was taking a toll on her frail body.*
*Before, Samayra had been able to ride in the wagons, but now she had to march most days, same as the rest.*
*Sarah had tried to make an exception for the girl, but there was simply no space left anywhere.*
Samayra: "Hey..."
*Her voice was soft, her eyes hollow and distant.*
*She trembled and shivered in the cold desert night.*
Sarah: "How are you holding up?"
*Sarah almost instantly felt stupid for asking the girl. Of course she'd lie.*
Samayra: "I'm...ok, I just need to catch up a bit."
*Suddenly, her back arched and she began to cough.*
*Sarah could hear a deep rattle in the poor girl's lungs.*
Sarah: "Come over here."
*Sarah opened her arms.*
*Eagerly, Samayra leaned closer, falling into Sarah's embrace.*
*The heat. The cold. The heat again. It was taking a toll on even the strong, and Samayra's body was not that.*
Sarah: "Just stay here with me, close to the fire."
*She felt Samayra nodding against her.*
Samayra: "Just for a moment..."
*Sarah stroked the girl's hair.*
Sarah: "Yes, just for a moment."
*Together, they sat near the campfire, gathering what little warmth they could manage in this desert night.*
*Staring into the fire, and feeling the poor girl's lithe frame against her own, she felt memories from long ago return to her.*
*Her brother, oddly enough.*
*More than once she'd cradled him, just as she now held Samayra.*
*Sarah had related to Samayra, a princess like herself, cast out into a cruel world, but perhaps there was also an element of her brother in the girl.*
*A soft soul, perhaps by nature unfit for what the world demanded of her.*
*It was always the kind ones that suffered the most, Sarah thought.*
Samayra: "Do you think I'm going to survive?"
*Sarah felt her heart skip a beat as the soft words of the Samayra reached her.*
Sarah: "Of course."
*Sarah lied.*
Sarah: "You're going to make it through, I'm sure of it."
*Again the girl's cough revealed just how weak she really was.*
*Sarah wanted her to live. But out here, what could she do? Each day she could see Samayra grow weaker.*
Sarah: "I'm going to find you a place to ride on one of the sleds, alright?"
*She felt Samayra shake her head.*
Samayra: "No, I want to...I want to walk...just like the others..."
*Sarah hushed her.*
Sarah: "I'm a commander; your commander. I'm ordering you to ride on one of the sleds."
*Sarah didn't hear another objection, though perhaps it was simply because the girl didn't have it in her to fight back.*
*Sarah tried to search her mind for a solution.*
*The only spaces left were the sleds used as makeshift hospice wards.*
*There the wounded, exhausted and sick were dragged along, but they offered little hope.*
*Most refused to be put on them, knowing that they meant death.*
*She had heard the wailing of those confided to the medical sleds. Thinking of putting Samayra among them, made her fearful.*
*Exhaustion alone was a great danger for the girl, but a simple infection might mean the end.*
*Then again, her body was too frail to continue the march...*
*Sarah felt a tear run past her face, unsure of what to do.*
Samayra: "If I die..."
*Sarah hushed her again.*
Sarah: "Don't talk like that. You're going to be alright."
*Sarah tried to keep the emotion from her voice.*
Samayra: "...at least I'll have seen the world."
*Sarah continued to stroke the girl's hair.*
*What a cruelty if this was all she'd ever get to see of the world.*
Sarah: "No, you'll get to see so much more."
Sarah: "Remember the snow? We can go to Rossana, and I'll show you what it looks like."
*She heard the girl softly laugh.*
Samayra: "The snow...the whole world covered in white...you're a liar..."
*Sarah hugged the girl, trying to pass her body heat to her.*
Sarah: "You'll see, I promise."
*Sarah could feel Samayra's body rise and fall, slower and slower.*
*Then, finally, her she could hear the soft snoring of the girl, now lost to sleep.*
*Sarah smiled, knowing the girl would last a bit longer.*
*Softly, she lifted her from her arms and placed her down near the campfire, placing a blanket on her and pulling it up close to her neck.*
*For a brief moment, Sarah held the girl's image in her mind.*
*It felt so ethereal, even now. Like the winds could pick up and simply blow her away.*
*She was a creature so delicate, much like Sarah's brother, that one could not help but feel a primal desire to protect.*
*But Sarah could only protect her from enemies she could swing a sword at.*
*Whatever was hacking away at the girl's lungs, racking her body, was beyond her ability to combat.*
*Sarah stood up and began to walk away, content to leave the girl by the warmth of the fire. She would make it through the night, that much she knew.*
*Whatever came next...*
*Having said still for long enough, eager to get some movement, Sarah stood up and began to walk away.*
*Walking through the camp was like a labyrinth.*

*Where once the fires had been places of celebration, where the soldiers sang and drank until the next day, they were now something very different.*
*Now they were pits of shared misery, where each sat and lingered in silence, content only to share their grudges.*
*Saying nothing, she could see that their eyes spoke volumes. Deep, dark and hollow. Their angry souls peered out through their eyes.*
*Sarah worried about what was coming over the camp.*

*She passed by Vaelen's tent.*
