Gideon: "Sure, but I promise I'm gonna win."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Sure, but this was just a warm-up round. Next time we wager on it."
Gideon: "Deal."
*Sarah waved at Gideon and turned around to leave, stumbling back towards the camp.*
*It took her a while, half drunk and lost in darkness, before Sarah finally found her way back to her bed.*
*Sleep came for her nearly instantly.*
*When the next morning came, Sarah had found Samayra still in poor condition.*
*For a brief moment, the girl had sought to fight Sarah on her decision, trying to still hide her sickness.*
Samayra: "No...I...I can still march...just for...today."
*She spoke with broken breaths.*
*Worst, Sarah could hear her lungs rattle each time she drewn in her breath.*
*It wasn't long before the girl was hunched over, exhausted merely from packing.*
Sarah: "You're going on the medical sled, that's an order."
*Sarah grabbed Samayra by her upper arm and dragged her along.*
*They only made it a few steps before the girl's legs gave out.*
*Sarah caught her only just in time.*
*Surprising herself, she pulled Samayra up and carried her in her arms.*
*Sarah could feel Samayra instinctively burying her head into Sarah's shoulder.*
Samayra: "You...you're a good friend...Sarah..."
*The girl's voice faded.*
Sarah: "Don't think about that for now. Just focus on getting better."
*But Sarah wasn't sure if the girl would get better. Very few made it back from the medical sled.*
*Sarah carried Samayra through the camp in her arms, weaving through the crowds of soldiers that each seemed more occupied with their own work.*
*When she finally arrived, Sarah's worries grew even deeper.*
*Spread out across the medical sleds were soldiers, ailing, delirous with heat, or suffering from wounds that had never managed to heal.*
*Across the crowd, Sarah could hear a few lungs rattle as Samayra's did.*
*Sarah felt Samayra's small and weak hands clutch her chest.*
Samayra: "Don't put me here...please..."
*Sarah wished there was another option.*
Sarah: "I...you're sick, Samayra..."
Samayra: "I know...but...please, if you have to...can you stay with me?"
Samayra: "I don't want to...not alone..."
*Samayra didn't finish her sentence, but Sarah understood enough.*
*She nodded.*
Sarah: "Of course, Samayra, I'll be right here with you."
*Sarah placed Samayra down on one of the sleds, a bit distanced from the others.*
*Then she seized the reins af the sled and began to pull it herself.*
*Sarah wasn't sure if she had the energy for all this. Even an ordinary march was exhausting enough, but she also knew she didn't have the heart to leave the girl.*
*Whatever else, she didn't deserve a fate that cruel, not after all she'd been through.*
*All throug the day, Sarah bore the weight of Samayra as though it was nothing to her.*
*What it costed her extra in effort, she made up for in spirit.*
*Behind her, she could hear the girl wail and ache, at times softly sobbing.*
*She wanted to be so much more, but the nature of her body and its current condition made it not a question of strength, only one of cruel biology.*
*And the truth was that the girl's build was too weak for a days hard work, and a days hard work was nothing compared to this march in the desert.*
*Even strong and powerful men were being brought low. A girl like Samayra had no chance, no matter how much she tried.*
*Sarah felt a tear run past her face, knowing she would lose the poor girl.*
*Still, Sarah carried on, dragging the sled until night fell and the camp was set up again.*
*Samayra for her part, had fought hard enough to survive yet one more day.*
*When Sarah made a campfire and placed Samayra close to it for warmth, she heard the girl speak for the first time since she had put her on the medical sled.*
Samayra: "W-w-water..."
*The word barely made it past her cracked lips.*
*Sarah brushed Samayra's face clean.*
Sarah: "Of course, I'm going to get you some water, you stay here."
*The day passed by with little to remark on.*
*Marching through the day, Sarah finally managed to get some rest when they made camp for the night.*
*Too focused on marching, she could feel her cracked lips, parched from lack of water.*
*Sarah set out to resolve the matter.*
*Walking through the camp by herself, Sarah set out to find water.*
*They had marched on longer than usual, making up time by keeping going for parts of the night.*
*As a result, the camp was buzzing with activity, soldiers working on unpacking and rigging the sleds to protect them from potential desert storms.*
*Sarah turned down the direction where the foodstuffs were usually kept, but to her surprise found only more packs of soldiers, busily working.*
*Asking around, she received five different directions, each contradicting the other.*
*Sarah sighed but kept looking for water.*
*Ask, follow, search, open up carts.*
*Everywhere she went, the water was absent.*
*By the end, Sarah had found herself near the edge of the camp, annoyed and frustrated by the chaos that seemed to have overtaken everything.*
*They had once been so organized, so efficient.*
*The collapse of morale had done more than just suppress peoples humors, it had also begun to make them lazy.*
*That was a dangerous thing in a place like this.*
*Then, just as she was ready to turn around, Sarah heard the running of water.*
*For a moment, she considered herself mad. Water didn't flow like that in the desert...*
*But her ears did not deceive her, she heard it as sure as anything else.*
Sarah: "If there isn't any water, I've surely lost my marbles..."
*Sarah mumbled to herself as she slid down the hill, towards the sound.*
*Suddenly, the earth beneath her feet turned solid and hidden under a curve in the dune, Sarah saw the entrance to a cave.*
*Unable to suppress even a hint of hesitation, Sarah walked closer towards the entrance of the cave, still following the sound.*
*Stepping into the cave, Sarah was instantly struck by the sense of relief she felt as cool air breezed past her skin.*
*More than cool, the air almost seemed to strip away all the pain and stress that had build up unknowningly.*
*The sound of flowing water continued to invite and seduce her further.*
*As the cave narrowed, Sarah pressed and contorted her body through the slimming pathways.*
*Part of her feared becoming stuck, but it was nothing compard to the eagerness to find where it all led.*
*Then, suddenly, the path opened up and Sarah stepped towards a small open space.*
*Though it was under ground, a soft glow of blueish light filled up the cave.*
*The light danced as it sprung from the water, or reflected off it, Sarah wasn't sure.*
*Entranced by the sight, Sarah walked up closer towards the pool of water, and kneeled down besides it.*
*The water was clear, but ran so deep, Sarah could not see the bottom.*
*Reflected slightly on the surface, she caught a glimpse of her own face.*
*What a mess she'd become.*
*Perhaps more than even the dirt and grime of the desert, Sarah worried about the darkened look in her eyes.*
*Had her eyes always been so angry?*
Ragged Man: *Don't worry child. What is carved in, can be carved out.*
*Sarah flinched, turning instantly towards the source of the voice.*
*Sitting in the corner of the cave, a man dressed in bandages.*
*Through the rags across his face, two gleeming eyes of black, peered out at her.*
Sarah: "Who are you!"
*The man made no motion suggesting he planned to move.*
Ragged Man: *No need to waste your time learning my name, child. I am of no import, and I am not long for this world.*
*A softness echoed through his voice. Sarah presumed he was male, but she could not be certain, so frail his body and so wrapped in gaze.*
Sarah: "I didn't come here for riddles."
*A laughter, interbroken with a choking sound from his lungs could be heard throughout the cave.*
Ragged Man: *We often find what we're not looking for.*
*He gestured around the cave.*
Ragged Man: *You sought for water, and now you have found it. And perhaps a bit more.*
*Sarah watched the man, cornered in the shadow, the light danced all around the cave but seemed to avoid him.*
Sarah: "Tell me who you are, or I'll make you tell me."
*Another broken laugh emerged from the ragged man.*
Ragged Man: *How violent you have become over the years, my child. You used to be so gentle.*
*Sarah narrowed her eyes.*
Sarah: "You don't know me."
*He nodded.*
Ragged Man: *I don't know you, but I have friends that do.*
Sarah: "And who might that be?"
Ragged Man: *Altyaehr, the Craftsman. Vaeda, the Birth-Mother. Naelyon, the Huntsman.*
Ragged Man: *My list of friends is long. Must I go on?*
*Sarah recognized the names. Names from the pantheon of gods. In total, there were more than two-hundred names, but these were the most prominent names.*
Sarah: "I think I've heard enough."
Sarah: "A madman in a cave, rambling about his divine friends."
*Emerging from behind his cloth bindings, a smile of shattered teeth.*
Ragged Man: *Not a madman, only a messenger who has been waiting here for a long time to deliver it.*
Ragged Man: *Forgive me if my manners have failed over the years.*
Sarah: "Years?"
Ragged Man: *Ooh, I can't say, but I suppose it must be close to two decades by now since I first came here.*
*Sarah only saw water here. Even with that, he couldn't have survived for that long out here.*
Sarah: "That long, without food?"
*The man gestured towards the pool of water.*
Ragged Man: *The water provides all that I might need.*
*Sarah wanted to dispute the man, but she couldn't deny that it was strange that he had survived here.*
*It had been hard to get to this point, even with an entire army behind her, bringing supplies. The idea of one man managing to survive just for a few days...*
Sarah: "How can you live off just water for two decades?"
Ragged Man: *A gift, from my friends. Or perhaps payment for my services now rendered.*
Ragged Man: *Who knows, it's been so long living in this hollow world.*
Sarah: "A gift?"
*The man smiled his broken smile again.*
Ragged Man: *Yes, it's been a long, long time since I came here.*
Ragged Man: *Back when there were still caravans travelling these parts, few as they were.*
Ragged Man: *My master, a great merchant, had a beautiful daughter, and she very much thought the same of me.*
Ragged Man: *But her father did not approve.*
Ragged Man: *Approved less when we acted upon our desires.*
*Sarah watched the man pull his hand over his scalp, as if to soothe himself.*
Ragged Man: *Drove me out of the caravan, hunted me for a little bit, but then I suppose they decided the desert could finish what they failed to do.*
Ragged Man: *I wandered the desert for a few days before I came upon this cave.*
Ragged Man: *As I entered, the water awaited me, and the voice spoke the words I needed to carry to you.*
Ragged Man: *Deep in the desert, no way out, but here I could live.*
*The man shrugged.*
Ragged Man: *Some would have chosen to die, but I suppose, I quite like being alive. And so I drink the water, and I am sustained.*
*Sarah's eyes drifted across his broken body. She wasn't sure if sustained was the right word.*
Sarah: "You want me to believe the water is magical?"
*The ragged man shook his head.*
Ragged Man: *Not magic. Divine.*
*Sarah sighed, frustrated at his obscurantism.*
Sarah: "I've had more than my fill of witchcraft and prophecies. If you have something to tell me, spit it out."
*The ragged man laughed again, his voice echoing through the cave.*
Ragged Man: *Considering all, it is but a small message. A warning.*
Sarah: "A warning?"
Ragged Man: *Yes, my friends hold you in good favor. They look upon you with kindness and wish that you return to the path.*
Sarah: "The path?"
Ragged Man: *Yes, the path.*
Sarah: "I am on a path, towards a city. How is that not a path?"
Ragged Man: *They have lost sight of you.*
Ragged Man: *You are special among special, and they fear losing you more than most.*
Sarah: "I...are you talking about breaking the edicts of the gods?"
*Sarah knew the list, murder, lies, adultery, but by now she imagined she had broken more than a few of them.*
*The man laughed, again and again.*
Ragged Man: *No, child. Their edicts do not take hold on you.*
Ragged Man: *They fear what all parents fear, to lose sight of their child. They urge you to turn away from this path to nothingness.*
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "Well, you've wasted a good deal of my time."
Sarah: "I have no idea what any of this means, nor do I have any desire to find out."
*The man shrugged.*
Ragged Man: *I was burdened with carrying the words, not their meaning.*
*The man leaned forward and pointed towards the water.*
Ragged Man: *However, there is also a gift.*
Sarah: "A gift?"
Ragged Man: *For one who needs it.*
Sarah: "The water?"
Ragged Man: *It feeds body and soul. Grants sucor to those desperate and nourishes wounds and deeper wounds.*
*Sarah looked towards the water.*
Ragged Man: *They fell me you have a friend that might have need of it...*
*Sarah's eyes went wide.*
Sarah: "How could you know that?"
Sarah: "Are you saying that this water will...heal Samayra?"
Ragged Man: *I don't know what a Samayra is, but make them drink the water and the water will drive out all foulness.*
*Sarah fell to her knees by the pool and cupped the water into her hands.*
*Carefully, she poured some of it into a flask.*
*Time...*
*Samayra was running out of time.*
Sarah: "I have to go!"
*The man waved his hands.*
Ragged Man: *We have no more words to barter. Take your gift and your warning. Do with each as you please.*
Ragged Man: *And remember, we live in a hollow world.*
*Sarah turned and ran out of the cave.*
Ragged Man: *However, there is also a gift.*
Sarah: "A gift?"
Ragged Man: *For one who needs it.*
Sarah: "The water?"
Ragged Man: *It feeds body and soul. Grants sucor to those desperate and nourishes wounds and deeper wounds.*
*Sarah looked towards the water.*
*Sarah fell to her knees by the pool and cupped the water into her hands.*
*Carefully, she poured some of it into a flask.*
*With a second helping, Sarah poured some of the water onto her face and down her throat.*
*Like a rush, she felt the stress and pain flow away from her body, her thirst quenched, appetite sated.*
*Sarah became as once aware to the comfort of the absence of pain, as only those long trapped in it can be.*
*Never had she imagined that simply feeling so much like herself, could be such a gift.*
Sarah: "I have to go."
*The man waved his hands.*
Ragged Man: *We have no more words to barter. Take your gift and your warning. Do with each as you please.*
Ragged Man: *And remember, we live in a hollow world.*
*Sarah turned and walked out of the cave.*
*Stepping out of the cave, Sarah saw the desert open back up before her.*
*Turning back around, she saw the lights of the camp just atop the hill.*
*Looking back down, she saw nothing but sand where the entrance to the cave should have been.*
Sarah: "Witchcraft..."
*Sarah muttered the word to herself as she began climbing back up the hill, trudging through the shifting sands of the dune.*
*With each step, Sarah could feel her legs sink further.*
*But with each step, she reached forward, clawing her hands, digging deep into the sand and pulling herself up along the hill.*
*A frenzy took hold of her as she continued her march, up and up the hill, faster and faster.*
*Reaching over the ledge, Sarah toppled back into the camp.*
*She crawled back onto her feet, taking barely a moment to recover herself, and ran through the camp.*
*For a moment, she ran blindly, in any direction, eager just to be me on the move, but slowly she began to recognize her direction.*
*Weaving through the small camps, Sarah finally found her way back to the campfire where she had left Samayra.*
*Rushing up, Sarah falls to her knees besides Samayra.*
*Sarah softly grabs the back of the girl's head and pulling her up.*
Samayra: "You...you're back...I...I dreamed..."
Sarah: "Don't speak, open your mouth."
*Too tired to resist, the girl spread her lips as much as she was able.*
*Sarah seized the flask from her waist and brought it up to Samayra's lips.*
*Tilting the bottle slightly, Sarah allowed the water to flow from the flask into the girl's mouth.*
*For a brief moment, Sarah feared she had been deceived. Believing the lies of a madman in the desert, but then, all changed.*
*Like a rush, Sarah could see Samayra's face shift.*
*Her hollowed out cheeks regained their youthful blush, her eyes grew back to their deep crimson red, her skin grew soft as though the sun and desert had never took hold of it.*
*Suddenly, Samayra lunged forward, out of Sarah's arms.*
Samayra: "I...what was I saying."
*Gone was the labored breathing and the exhausted broken speech. The girl was as she had always been.*
Samayra: "Did...what did you give me?"
*Sarah could feel the tears drawing near.*
Sarah: "Water...it's just water."
*Sarah could see that the girl distrusted this answer, but appeared far too eager at this turn of fate to question it much more.*
Samayra: "I...I feel great."
*Sarah laughed.*
*Laughed for so much dread that she had kept bottled up, prepared and fearing for the worst, was now released from her.*
*Sarah grabbed Samayra into a deep embrace, hugging her as she imagined she was never going to be able to.*
Sarah: "Samayra...I'm so happy you're healthy again."
Samayra: "Of course. You shouldn't have doubted me, I told you I'm stronger than I look."
*Leaning back, Sarah could see the girl smiling back at her.*
Samayra: "Besides. You promised me snow, remember?"
*With each step, Sarah could feel her legs sink further.*
*But with each step, she reached forward, clawing her hands, digging deep into the sand and pulling herself up along the hill.*
*She continued her march, up the hill.*
*Reaching over the ledge, Sarah toppled back into the camp.*
*She crawled back onto her feet, and walked through the camp.*
*Around her, all the world seemed brighter and more intense than it had appeared to her in many years.*
*A dullness had been lifted, and Sarah prayed it would remain forever banished.*
*Another week had passed since Sarah had come upon the cave and the strange man.*
*His words, the effects of the water, all of it had been hard for her to shake.*
*Samayra had by now become herself, if not more than herself.*
*Where once she trudged along, struggling through the desert, unable to keep up, she now began and ended each day with a strange serenity.*
*Exhaustion. Disease. The dirt of the desert.*
*None of it seemed to be able to take hold of her anymore.*
*Instead, she now marched along with the others, and when they put down their gear at the end of the day, nearing collapse, she simply sat down as though it meant nothing.*
*The water had driven out the sickness, but so too did it keep all other decay at bay.*
*To see the girl, so frail and lithe of body, now so resilient, Sarah could offer no rational explanation.*
*As the thoughts of the encounter continued to swirl through Sarah's mind, she had for a moment lost sight of the situation around her.*
*Only in the last few days had she managed to focus on her work again.*
*But by the time Sarah had done so, she had found the mercenary company in dire straits.*
*Food had begun to run low, forcing them to impose even stricter ration policies.*
*Water too, had begun to run low, when it was found that one of the wagons had been torn open on a jagged rock, spilling the water into the thirsty desert sand.*
*The men had grown increasingly resentful, their wealth from Bagrad now cast away into the desert.*
*Poor. Hungry. Thirsty.*
*Perhaps if they had been defeated in the battle, the men could have more easily carried their circumstance, but they had been victorious.*
*Not that long ago, they had rejoiced as conquerors, and now they lived as beggars.*
*With strict rations, even the soft reprieve of a day's march by the campfire had been cut short, robbed of drink to celebrate.*
*And so, gathered around their campfires, the men of the mercenary company had only their grievances and their hatreds for company.*
*And around the campfire, they exchanged them freely and eagerly.*
*They cursed many things, but as men are prone to do, they soon found a concensus for their hatreds.*
*Vaelen.*
*The man who had crowned them with victory, the man who had taken it away from them.*
*Like children, the men of the camp could abide the gentle hand and the firm hand, but they could not tolerate the fickle hand.*
*So, their hatreds grew.*
*It was on such a night, where Sarah could hear the men whisper among themselves, that she had been invited to Vaelen's tent.*
*Present already was Gideon, who along with Sarah was attributed most of the blame by Vaelen.*
*For most worryingly of all, more so than their lack of food and lack of water, was a more grave fact.*
*The fact that by most estimates, they should have reached the city of Nauyziri by now.*
*They could have all shouldered a great deal, knowing that their trials might soon end, but by now, nobody could be certain if they would ever end at all.*
*Sarah saluted as she entered the tent.*
Sarah: "Commander Vaelen."
*He threw her a temporary glare.*
Vaelen: "You're here, finally. Give me the status on our supplies."
*Sarah glanced over towards Gideon, his eyes fixed to the ground. Apparently he had already received his share of berating.*
Sarah: "We've handed down orders to further reduce rations, but the most recent reports seem to suggest these are not having much of an effect."
*Vaelen looked up from his desk.*
Vaelen: "How do you mean? How can the reduced rations have no effect?"
*Sarah cleared her throat.*
Sarah: "The most likely cause is a further collapse of discipline."
Sarah: "We've begun to suspect that officers are refusing to carry out accurate supply counts, handing out more rations than instructed while fabricating their reports to us."
*Vaelen slammed his fist against the table.*
Vaelen: "Then have them whipped if that's what it takes."
Vaelen: "We're in the middle of a desert. If we allow morale to break down here, it's all over."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "I understand, but that's exactly what the officers are trying to do."
*Vaelen frowned.*
Vaelen: "How do you mean?"
Sarah: "They officers work most directly with their own units. They see their own men every day."
Sarah: "They understand that morale is breaking down as a result of forced marches and increasingly strict rations."
Sarah: "They want to maintain good relations with their soldiers, so they break the rules and give out more than they should."
Sarah: "We can snap the whip on them, force them to follow the new guidelines, but this won't increase morale. It is likely to the opposite."
Sarah: "The men are already close to starving, and not only that, we are still forcing them on long daily marches that require the opposite of rations. The men should be eating more than usual."
*Vaelen rubbed his temples.*
Vaelen: "And if we give them more, and we run out, we'll all starve out here."
Sarah: "That wouldn't have been a problem if we had reached our destination by now."
*Vaelen glared at her.*
Vaelen: "You mean to suggest anything, Sarah?"
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "No, commander, but the truth is that even by the most negative estimates...we should have arrived by now."
Sarah: "Perhaps we have been marching off course....perhaps we have marched past the city...I don't know, but we should have come across it by now."
Sarah: "That city...the Mythran army there, they are our only real way out of this mess."
*Vaelen sighed.*
Vaelen: "Yes, I am aware."
Vaelen: "But the map..."
*Vaelen tapped the map on his desk.*
Vaelen: "We should reach it...soon."
Sarah: "How certain can we be?"
*Vaelen paused before answering.*
Vaelen: "It's...one...perhaps two weeks, at most."
*Gideon suddenly looked up.*
Gideon: "That's not possible, commander."
Gideon: "Our food supplies are low, but with the recent disaster on our water cart, the water supplies are even lower."
Gideon: "We have days left of water, not weeks."
*Vaelen pointed his finger angrily towards Gideon.*
Vaelen: "Your job is to solve my problems, not regurgitate them back to me."
Vaelen: "You've handed down the orders, not see to it that they are enforced. By whatever means necessary."
*Gideon saluted.*
Gideon: "Yes, commander."
*He quickly turned and left the tent.*
Sarah: "You should know that he does his best, given the circumstances."
*Vaelen was hunched over his map, not bothering to even look at her.*
Vaelen: "He's a man, if he wants to complain about how I run things, he can talk to me myself. He doesn't need you to speak for him."
*Sarah watched as Vaelen stroked his chest, the bulge just under his shirt was where he kept the stone from Bagrad.*
*Always touching it, obsessively.*
*Sarah stepped forward.*
Sarah: "You had best start paying attention to the world outside of your maps and reports."
Sarah: "This company is coming apart at the seams, and the only instruction you're able to hand down is to whip people until they do as you say."
Sarah: "You used to know what it took to lead, but ever since Bagrad you've become distracted."
*Vaelen suddenly looked up.*
Vaelen: "Are you questioning my leadership as well now?"
Vaelen: "Because there have been others before you, and there will be others after you if you continue this."
Vaelen: "This company is at the most critical moment in its existence."
Vaelen: "We either come apart here and lose everything, or we hold on, just for a moment longer, and reach the other side of this desert."
Vaelen: "And once we do, all these problems that people are making out to be so big, will fade away."
*Vaelen raised himself up.*
Vaelen: "Now, go out there, and find whatever way you need to get this company moving tomorrow, and tomorrow, until we get to our destination."
Vaelen: "Am I clear enough?"
*Sarah knew there was no reasoning with him.*
*She saluted.*
Sarah: "Yes, commander."
*Sarah turned and left the tent.*
*As soon as she left, Sarah caught Gideon from the corner of her eyes, waiting for her.*
Sarah: "Shouldn't you be doing as you were told?"
*Gideon smiled at her.*
Gideon: "About as much as you should be doing as you were told."
*Sarah smiled back at him.*
Sarah: "Treason, Gideon, treason."
Gideon: "Sure, mayba you're right. Let's go for a walk before I get the rope."
*Sarah could see he needed it. She nodded.*
Sarah: "Sure, let's walk."
*For a short while, the two walked side by side in silence as they got further and further away from the camp.*
*Before long, they found themselves far enough to be certain they were alone.*
*Standing atop one of the many rolling dunes, Sarah could see out across the desert.*
*No direction seemed to offer any hints of where their destination might lie.*
*Just endless desert, in each direction.*
*A full moon draped the world in pale light, making the dunes appear as silver.*
Gideon: "So, what do we do?"
*Sarah didn't bother to look at him.*
Sarah: "Probably what he told us to do..."
*Gideon kicked the sand.*
Gideon: "This is bullshit."
Gideon: "If I press down on my men any harder, they're going to turn on me."
*Sarah kept looking out towards the horizon, hoping something might offer her an escape. But there was none.*
Gideon: "He's lost it, don't tell me I'm the only one that sees it."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "You're not wrong, but he's still the one in charge of this company."
Gideon: "Well, maybe that should change."
*Sarah quickly turned to face him.*
Sarah: "Don't ever repeat that to anyone, do you understand?"
*Gideon shrugged.*
Gideon: "I was just talking."
Sarah: "Well, that's the kind of talk that gets you killed. And don't think he's not the kind of man to do it either."
Sarah: "There have been others over the years, too ambitious, too hungry, and they've all met the same fate."
*Gideon sighed.*
Gideon: "So what?"
Gideon: "Just keep marching till we die?"
*Sarah threw up her hands.*
Sarah: "What else do you suggest we do?"
Sarah: "Turning back now...we don't have the supplies to survive the trip back. Even if we did, we have no idea what would even be left of Bagrad."
*Sarah paused for a moment.*
Sarah: "The only chance we have is reaching Nauyziri. If there really is a Mythran outpost there...with food and water...we stand a chance."
Gideon: "And what if its all bullshit?"
Gideon: "What if nothing is out there?"
*Sarah studied the horizon again.*
Sarah: "I have to believe that there is. It's our only hope."
*Gideon laughed mirthlessly.*
Gideon: "Great."
Gideon: "So that's what it's all come down to. Hope and a prayer."
*Sarah turned back to face him.*
Sarah: "I've had worse."
*He studied her face for a while.*
Gideon: "I like to think that I have a good read on most people, but I'll be honest, I don't think I've ever figured you out."
*Sarah smiled.*
Sarah: "Maybe you're not as clever as you think."
*He laughed.*
Gideon: "That's definitely true."
Gideon: "But why are you so loyal to him?"
Sarah: "Because when I met him, I was in a very bad place."
Sarah: "And out of all the people in this world that sought to take advantage of me, he was the only that ever offered me a real chance."
*Sarah paused as in her mind she drifted back to all those years ago.*
Gideon: "I've known tough times, don't mean I'm indebted to any asshole that gives me a hand."
Sarah: "It's different for you and me."
Gideon: "How's that?"
Sarah: "I'm a woman."
Sarah: "You can say it shouldn't matter, but it does."

*It had bothered neither of them, and before the thunderous rage of their father, she had seen him smile more broadly at her than he ever had.*
*Back when life had been easy, and the road ahead seemed not just safe, but obvious.*
*Now every path before her seemed confused.*
*Sarah felt a tear run down her face.*
*She felt it linger for a moment, before it fell into the sand of the desert.*
*The sun scorched it away into nothingness.*
*This desert, much like the rest of the world, tolerated no weakness.*
*Sarah closed her eyes and emptied her mind.*
*Work. Work would be the thing that would distract her.*
*Sarah forced herself to resume her task, and she felt the day swiftly go by, an endless series of tasks and meetings.*
*She was happy for the distraction.*
*When night had finally fallen over the camp, and most of the soldiers had returned to the camp, Sarah received her invitation.*
*She, along with the rest of the command of the mercenary company, had been extended an invitation.*
*Vaelen, herself, Gideon and the others.*
*It made sense, Sarah thought to herself. She could meet with Lady Carolyn again, longer, and whatever spying eyes there were, they'd likely be aimed at Vaelen, their leader.*
*Sarah made her way towards Lady Carolyn's tent, leaving the camp and its celebrating soldiers behind her.*
*When Sarah arrived, she found Carolyn's tent already bristling with people.*
*Seated all throughout the tent, food was already being served up and drinks had been widely consumed.*
*Sarah saw Lady Carolyn, in deep discussion with Vaelen.*
*If she acknowledged her at all, it was so brief that even Sarah couldn't tell.*
*Sarah made her way towards one of the empty seats and sat down.*
*It wasn't long before a servant rushed over and placed a platter of food before her.*
*Despite being out on the edge of the world, the Mythrans had clearly no shortage of food.*
*Not only did they have the basics, but judging by the plate filled with fatty meats, fruits and rich cheeses, they clearly had an abundance of everything.*
*The servant poured her cup with wine, filling it nearly to the brim.*
*Idly, Sarah began to eat and drink while she observed the room.*
*The room was filled with familiar faces, officers, fellow commanders.*
*Mingled in the crowd were some unfamiliar faces, but judging by their regalia it was easy enough to mark them out as Mythrans.*
*There was an easy, amicable mood.*
*The kind that could be found among fellow soldiers, free from the worry of any real danger.*
*As her eyes drifted, Sarah suddeny caught the movements of the slender bodies that darted between the soldiers.*
*Small. Unnoticed. Lowered heads and lithe bodies.*
*The slaves that they had made in Bagrad.*
*Sarah felt an instant revulsion to see these people made to serve on them.*
*Her disgust at slavery was something imprinted into her from birth in Rosanna. All the union kingdoms expressly forbade the practice.*
*But here she was among Mythrans and mercenaries.*
*To the Mythrans, slavery was as natural a state of being as could be imagined.*
*To the mercenaries, they were often lowborn, eager to feel a fraction of a king's power by lording over those too weak to fight back.*
*She could see the smiling faces of the men, their wandering and chasing eyes as the servant girls passed through the room.*
*They were as much on the menu as anything they brought out on a platter.*
*Sarah hated the sight of it, but hated herself more because she knew there was nothing she could do.*
*Could do. Would do.*
*She pondered which of the two it really was.*
*Suddenly, from the corner of her eyes, she saw movement. Before she even fully realized it, she saw Gideon fall down beside her.*
Gideon: "You're in a foul mood."
*Sarah raised an eyebrow.*
Sarah: "Am I?"
Gideon: "You're scowling."
Sarah: "Maybe that's just my regular face."
*Gideon laughed.*
Gideon: "That it might just be. Still, you should be celebrating."
*He gestured towards the room full of men.*
Gideon: "Trust me, they can't wait to sing your praises."
Gideon: "Rose knight. Demon killer. Now miracle-worker too."
*Gideon laughed to himself.*
Gideon: "I'm going to have to keep a list of all your titles."
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "I'd rather you didn't."
Sarah: "Besides, how would any of them know what happened in Bagrad?"
*She saw Gideon smiling.*
Gideon: "Maybe I told them."
*Sarah sighed.*
*The last thing she needed was to become the center of attention.*
Sarah: "I'd rather you keep all of that to yourself. I don't need more trouble than I have."
*Gideon leaned back, drinking from his cup.*
Gideon: "If it had been me, I'd make sure the whole world knew."
*Choose*
*Snap at him*:
Sarah: "Well it wasn't you, now was it?"
*Sarah realized the moment she said it that her words had sounded harsher than she meant.*
*Gideon's face suddenly sunk.*
Gideon: "I'm sorry, I was only joking."
*For a moment, a pause lingered between them.*
*Let it go*:
*Sarah waved her hand, dismissing the matter.*
Sarah: "It's fine. What does it matter anyway."

*Gideon shrugged.*

*Gideon began to chuckle.*
Gideon: "If it had been any other man, I might have thought he'd be holed up there with one of the girls from Bagrad, but who knows what his appetites are."
*It wasn't often spoken of in the camp, but there had certainly been rumors about Vaelen.*
*Most mercenaries wore their desires openly. They prided themselves on living in excess.*
*They often, correctly, believed they wouldn't live very long and had best make up for their short lives by living them twice as hard.*
*But not Vaelen.*
*He consumed everything in portion. Measured. And as for desires of the flesh, he either had none or kept them well hidden.*
Sarah: "Don't start rumors."
Gideon: "You don't think it's weird?"
Sarah: "I think I don't know enough to talk one way or another, and whatever you do so, is just going to start trouble."
Sarah: "Best to keep your mouth shut."
*Gideon laughed.*
Gideon: "My life would have been a lot easier if I had just learned to do that from a young age."
*An attractive servant girl passed them by, carrying a jug of wine to fill up the cups of the commanders.*
*Sarah could see Gideon's eyes following the curves of her body as she passed them.*
*He suddenly stood up.*
Gideon: "I think I'm going to get a refill."
*Sarah watched as he quickly dissapeared into the crowd, following in the wake of the servant girl.*
*Would it be any comfort to the servant girl that the man who would take her was closer to her own age and handsome?*
*Sarah could feel a pit growing in her stomach.*
*She banished the thought.*
*Sarah continued observing the crowd from a small distance.*
*Occasionally, a Mythran officer or a familiar face would drift by, but other than that the night passed uneventfully.*
*Her eyes switched and lingered between Vaelen and Lady Carolyn.*
*Each moved about the party, smiling, nodding, performing exactly the part they were supposed to play.*
*Each seemingly naturally born to play their roles.*
*Sarah didn't know what to make of either of them.*
*As the night went on, Lady Carolyn made her way through the crowd.*
*Expertly, she appeared to favor no person above the other, moving and stopping for the occasional conversation.*
*Until she ended up in front of Sarah.*
*Casually. Gracefully. Nobody would consider anything more of it. She had after all spoken to just about everyone else in the room.*
Carolyn: "Having fun, are we?"
*Sarah forced a smile.*
Sarah: "Not really my scene I think."
*Lady Carolyn smiled back at her, seemingly genuinely entertained.*
Carolyn: "When I spotted you, I made you out right away. But the more I talk, the more I feel like you're not entirely the girl from back home."
*Sarah met her gaze.*
Sarah: "The years have changed, as they have you, I suppose."

Carolyn: "Ooh dear, I'm at home in any place. I match myself to the room."

Sarah: "Woman."
*Sarah corrected her.*
*She saw Lady Carolyn's eyes slide up and down her body.*
Carolyn: "Yes, quite."

Sarah: "You told me you would tell me about why we're here. Why you sought me out."

Sarah: "Would be me."

*Sarah spat out the words.*

Carolyn: "The horde is splintering."

*Sarah listened intently as Lady Carolyn explained.*
*Much had changed back home. She suddenly thought of herself as foolish for having allowed herself to be so ignorant.*
Carolyn: "He is growing weaker by the day. Soon, the moment will come where he will fall."
Carolyn: "My master, Gilead, would like it to be you who delivers that fatal blow."

*Sarah saw Lady Carolyn's mouth slightly curl, a predator that had set its trap and now awaited the prey.*
Sarah: "Why me?"
Sarah: "If his grip on Rosanna is fading, why not wait and let the people rise up?"
Carolyn: "Well, there is the matter of the other nations. Our neighbours of Normandi and Elarand."
*The two nations that bordered Rosanna. Rivals, allies, differing things in differing times.*
Carolyn: "Both of them are eying parts of Rosanna. For the moment, neither moves, fearing the other, but in time they will."
Carolyn: "You have a stronger claim than either of them."

Sarah: "And I would be a puppet on the throne, on behalf of some stranger I've never met, for an empire I have no sympathies for?"

*The mercenaries were loyal to Vaelen and the Mythran armies that Carolyn spoke of were even less loyal to her.*

*It was easy for Lady Carolyn to pretend that there were no strings attached to it, but Sarah knew better.*
*No empire as powerful as the Mythrans made gestures out of goodwill. She would be in debt to them, and they would collect on her.*

*Her people had languished under the rule of the tribesmen for years now.*
*Sarah knew enough about them to know that they offered only brutality to those they conquered.*
*They were her people still.*

*And what if she was too slow, and the neighbours of Rosanna conquered her lands instead?*
*Would they prove any kinder to her people?*

*Was her pride worth more than the lives of her people?*

Sarah: "What is this Gilead offering, exactly?"

*If they ever leave, Sarah thought.*
*Her only way out from under them was by hoping the Mythrans would keep their word.*
*More than a few kings and emperors had lost their lives misjudging the intentions of the Mythrans.*
*Sarah suddenly felt Lady Carolyn's hand on her wrist.*
Carolyn: "Do not worry, you are not expected to decide now."

*Rahayal, the great capital of the Mythran empire, a city supposedly without rival in all the world.*

Sarah: "I will meet with him, but no more than that."

*Choose*
*Ask Carolyn about Vaelen*:

*Say nothing*:

*She saw his face fall back into its natural state. Cold and unmoving like stone.*

Vaelen: "None of this matters."
Vaelen: "I already know how this ends."
*Sarah watched as he turned and walked away from her in broad steps.*
*She was left by herself.*
*In front of her, the now empty street where Vaelen had dissapeared.*
*Behind her, the warm glow and sounds of celebration coming from inside the tent.*
*And herself, caught between.*
*For a moment longer, Sarah stood by herself, trying to make sense of it.*
*She had never wanted his role, had always served faithfully and given her honest advice.*
*He had always valued her.*
*Always, until now.*
*Had something broken between them in Bagrad? Memories of the stone returned to Sarah.*
*The words of the spirit haunted her.*
*Feeling the chill of the night air on her skin, Sarah began to walk.*
*Away from Carolyn's tent. Away from Vaelen. Away from everyone.*
*She kept walking until she couldn't so much see or hear another soul.*
*The broken road under her feet reminded her that this was a city long faded.*
*Off to the side, she saw the ruined remnants of what had once been houses, or so she assumed.*

*Memories flashed in front of her eyes of the man who had almost attacked her in the alley.*

Sigmund: "Are you out of your damned mind, girl?"

*She saw the man rubbing his temples, frustrated.*
Sigmund: "This place is dangerous enough for just about anybody, girl."
Sigmund: "Someone like you wouldn't last a day out on the old road."
Sigmund: "I don't want to find your corpse in some ditch, your throat slashed by some bandit."
Sigmund: "Go back to the city, you'll be a lot safer there."

*Sarah forced herself to speak through the sobs.*
Sarah: "I was in that damned city!"

Sigmund: "Look, girl, I'll grant you Lethram ain't the safest place in the world, but trust me, whatever is out here is a hundred times worse."

Sarah: "So what?"
Sarah: "I go back into that city and sleep on the streets till that bastard, or someone like him, finds me?"
*She watched as the man struggled to find an answer.*
Sigmund: "I..."
Sigmund: "Look. You're still young."
Sigmund: "Whatever this is, just go back home and apologize to your parents, you don't want to be out here."

*Sarah nearly screamed the words. Who was he to make assumptions about her life?*

Sigmund: "I'm...sorry. I shouldn't have assumed."
Sigmund: "But you still can't be out here. It's too dangerous."
*Sarah planted her feet on the ground, as if expecting that he might try to physically force her back into the city.*
Sarah: "I'm not going back into that city, no matter what you try."
*The man sighed again. He seemed equally frustrated but equally unable to walk away and let her be.*
Sigmund: "Look..."
Sigmund: "I'll tell you what."

Sarah: "Alright."
Sarah: "I'll accept your offer."

Sarah: "It's not real?"

Sigmund: "It is real. I just mean you're lucky that you ran into me."
Sigmund: "Just about every other bastard on the old road would have taken you two miles up the road, robbed you and left you behind, or worse."
*Sarah felt her heart beat faster.*
Sigmund: "You're too naive for city life, hell you might be too naive for small town life."
Sigmund: "You really shouldn't be out here."
*Sarah steeled herself.*
Sarah: "Well, I ain't going anywhere else."
*The man laughed.*
Sigmund: "You got a spark to you, I'll give you that."

Sarah: "Sarah, nice to meet you."
Sigmund: "Nice to meet you too, Sarah."

*Sarah followed the man. She could see his cart from a distance.*
*Two men were sitting up against the wheels, sitting in the shade of the cart, hiding from the sun.*

Sigmund: "Right, enough pleasantries."

Sigmund: "You get up front and ride with me, Sarah."
Sigmund: "Sakar and Krip can ride on back."
*Sarah nodded and followed Sigmund's instructions, climbing onto the front of the cart.*
*Sitting atop the elevated position, Sarah could see a bit further out.*
*Next to her were the reins, connected to two large black horses that were standing ready, casually swatting away flies.*
*A large yoke bound the two animals to the wooden pulls.*
*Growing up in Rosanna as a noble woman, Sarah was not unfamiliar with horses.*
*But these were clearly different from the breeds she had grown up with.*
*The kind of horses she was most familiar with were riding horses. These horses were clearly bred for burden, large and bulky, strong enough to seemingly pull anything.*
*Around her, Sarah could see and hear that the others were busy preparing the cart for departure.*
*She felt guilty just sitting here, doing nothing, but she also didn't really know how she could possibly help them out.*
*She would probably just get in the way.*
*Sitting atop the box, Sarah's eyes trailed the winding road that led away from Lethram.*
*She couldn't see a soul.*
*After a while, Sarah felt the wagon shake.*
*Looking off to her side, she saw Sigmund step onto the box, taking his seat besides her.*
*He grabbed the reins.*
Sigmund: "Be sure to hold onto something."
*Sarah nervously gripped the edge of the cart's seat.*
Sigmund: "Hyaa!"
*With a firm yell and a snapping of the reins, Sigmund forced the horses into motion.*
*Sarah felt the cart begin to rock and was glad that she had chosen to hold onto something.*
*After a few more shocks, the horses finally found their speed.*
*The cart's violent shaking slowly became more something like the motions of a ship, a constant back and forth.*
*As the horses pulled the cart along the road, Sarah watched the few buildings that remained quickly fade away.*
*Before long, there was nothing but an empty road that stretched out ahead of her.*
*Off to the sides of the road, there was nothing more than open fields, stretching out in every direction.*
*Sarah struggled to get used to it. Only a few miles out from Lethram, and nature seemed to have taken over entirely.*
Sarah: "It's so peaceful..."
*Sigmuned laughed.*
Sigmund: "Yeah, we're still close to Lethram, but the further we get out from the city, the bolder the bandits tend to get."
Sigmund: "Up till Gallow's Creek nobody will mess with a cart like ours, but further up along the old road, there is no telling what can happen."
*Sarah looked at Sigmund.*
*His face was rugged and a stern expression didn't do him many favors.*
*But there was something in his face that Sarah seemed to recognize, though she couldn't quite put her finger on it.*

Sigmund: "You're not from Lethram, are you?"
*Sarah shook her head.*

*Sarah had studied enough geography growing up in Rosanna that she knew Lethram and Rahayal were on the same side of the continent, so a land route had seemed obvious to her.*
*Back in Rosanna, all the union kingdoms were intertwined, and land trade made up most of the economy.*
Sarah: "Why is it called the old road?"
Sigmund: "It's a long story, but it used to be simply called the imperial road."
Sigmund: "But after the wars of the central kingdoms, it became too dangerous for most merchants too keep using it."
Sigmund: "Seeking a safer passage, most merchants began to rely on sea routes, and Lethram given its location was more than happy to encourage that."
Sigmund: "And now...I think it's been more than a century since this road has seen any real trade."
Sigmund: "Now people just call it the old road."
*Sarah listend quietly.*
*She thought she had been well educated, and compared to most she had been, but there was still so much of the world beyond her home country that was new and strange to her.*
Sarah: "If it's so dangerous...why do you take it? Why not just take a ship like everybody else."
*Sigmund laughed.*
Sigmund: "You would be right, except we make our money transporting Pyrrite."
Sarah: "Pyrrite?"
*He nodded.*
Sigmund: "It's a mineral used as a catalyst in certain alchemical reactions."

Sigmund: "The only problem is that pyrrite has a strong chemical reaction when it comes into contact with water."

Sigmund: "It explodes."
Sigmund: "Anything more than a few drops of water and pyrrite blow apart."
Sigmund: "If it's just a small crystal, the stuff isn't that dangerous, but if you're hauling a cart full of the stuff like we are, then the crystals an set off a chain-reaction."

*Sarah could feel hersel grow more tense with every word.*
*Before Sigmund had started talking, she thought the cart was filled with generic trading goods.*
*Now she realized she was in fact sitting atop a bomb on wheels.*
*Each time the cart shook, Sarah felt her heart freeze.*
Sarah: "But that's...insane."
Sarah: "What if it starts raining?"
*Sigmund shrugged.*
Sigmund: "The crates are sealed tight and the pyrrite is wrapped in three layers of coating, so long as it's just a bit of water we're safe."
Sigmund: "Besides, there are worse ways to die than in a pyritte explose."
Sigmund: "It would be so fast, you'd probably not even realize it."
*Sigmund started to laugh as if the idea was entertaining to him.*
*Sarah could only feel herself grow more tense.*
*She wasn't exactly eager to die in a firey chemical explosion.*
Sarah: "And so you take these crystals by land, all the way to Rahayal?"
*Sigmund nodded as the cart continued to roll along.*
Sigmund: "No matter how much you pay a sailor, they ain't gonna take a crate of pyrrite on board."
Sigmund: "And because the demand for the stuff in Mythra is so great, the price you can fetch for a cart like this is worth the trip."

*Sigmund looked up to the sky, as if to help himself do the math in his head.*
Sigmund: "About...a house."
Sarah: "A house?"
Sigmund: "Yeah. With the profits off this cart alone, you could probably pay for an entire house in Rahayal or Lethram."
*That they could make so much money off just one cart seemed absurd to Sarah.*
*Then again, Sarah thought, she didn't really know much of anything about money. Money had never been a problem for her family growing up.*
Sigmund: "But don't go thinking we're all that rich."
Sigmund: "Trip like this can take a good while. Biggest chunk of the profits go to the bastards that own the cargo."
Sigmund: "We're just the idiots that are crazy enough to transport it."
Sigmund: "And after we're done transporting, we still need to split whatever money is left three-ways."
Sigmund: "All in all, the money isn't really worth it."

*He might have lived a rough life, but he clearly also knew a lot about the world. The way the world really worked for those that weren't born to a castle like herself.*
Sarah: "How often have you made the trip?"
*She saw Sigmund frown his brown, as if deep in thought.*
Sigmund: "You know...I don't think I really remember."
Sigmund: "I tried to keep track of it all, the first few times, but you keep going up and down this road, at some point, the trips just start to blur together."
*As the minutes turned to hours and Sarah continued speaking with Sigmund, she slowly saw the open fields roll past her.*
*Each hill didn't look all that much different from the next.*
*The only real difference came hours later, when Sarah watched the last few beams of light fade beyond the horizon as the sun finally set.*
*Sigmund ignited a small lamp above the cart, casting a small bit of light out ahead of them.*
*The stars above them were the only real source of light.*
Sigmund: "Alright, we'll pack up and set camp on the side of the road here."
*Sarah felt the wagon shake as it pulled away from the road, into the ditch.*
*Slowly, the horses came to a stop and the wagon ceased to move.*
*Sigmund leapt from the box back onto the ground in a single, practiced leap.*
Sigmund: "Sakar, Krip, let's go. I want a fire up before it's full dark."

Sigmund: "I can't guarantee your safety if you're alone with them. Do you understand?"

*She knew that the men were violent, they simply oozed violence.*

Sigmund: "Thank you. That's all I wanted to hear."
Sigmund: "We'll be in Gallow's Creek by tomorrow. After that, you won't have to worry about any of them, I promise."
*Sarah sat down against the wheel of the cart.*

*Why was every corner of this world so filled with danger?*
*Sitting in silence, she looked out across the road which simply stretched on each direction.*
*And there she was trapped in the middle of nowhere.*

*They seemed to somehow burn brighter here than anywhere else.*

Sakar: "Well, this should be plenty of wood."

*Like it was nothing, he had made them a campfire.*

Sakar: "That's alright, I was only offering."

*Make the eggs and bacon.*:

Sarah: "I'll make the eggs."

*Make a stew*:
*Sarah thought about it for a moment.*

Sigmund: "Sakar!"

Xanthippe: "Save her? What do you suggest I do, step out and snap my fingers, turn him to ash?"
Sarah: "You could!"
Xanthippe: "Yes, and then what?"
Xanthippe: "Then the entire square of these degenerates wakes up and attacks me."
*Sarah looked into Xan's eyes, trying to see what might move him.*
Sarah: "Then you kill all of them! Don't tell me you're not strong enough."
*Xan rubbed his temples.*
Xanthippe: "Think, Sarah. Suppose I survive the square, then what? They sound the alarm and soon the entire city garrison will descend on me."
Xanthippe: "And for what?"
Xanthippe: "So I can save her?"
Xanthippe: "What about the others, do I save them too? Do I save the entire city?"
Sarah: "As many as you can!"
Xanthippe: "You're still lost in the girl you were, Sarah. Becoming a mage is more than learning magic. It's also about adopting a greater view of the world."
Xanthippe: "Do you think what's happening here is unique?"
Xanthippe: "I've lived a long time, Sarah. I've watched countless cities and nations rise and fall."
*Xan waved his hand at the view.*
Xanthippe: "Every tragedy you see here has played out countless times before, and it will again. It's just human nature."
Xanthippe: "I can't stop every tragedy."
Sarah: "But you can stop this one!"
Xanthippe: "And why would I stop this one, and not the one before or the one after? What makes these people more special, more deserving of being saved than all the other victims of history?"
*A pause.*
Sarah: "Because they're my people..."
*Xan shook his head.*
Xanthippe: "They're not anymore, Sarah. They might have been once, but you're not their princess anymore."
Xanthippe: "You're going to become so much more. You will rise above this world and see it from the high point. You can't continue to pretend that you're also a part of it."
Xanthippe: "If you don't learn that, you'll burn out. You'll try to fix every injustice in the world, and it won't be long before you find yourself outmatched."
*Xan seized her by the shoulders.*
Xanthippe: "We operate on the scope of the whole world, Sarah. We measure not the years but the centuries. Our duty is towards the whole of the human race."
Xanthippe: "We cannot allow ourselves to fail in that greatest of duty, and throw it away because of some random girl, however tragic her circumstance might be."
*Sarah could see tears form in his eyes.*
Xanthippe: "It pains me, same it does you. You might not believe it, but I'm human too."
Xanthippe: "But we have a great obligation, and we cannot stray from that. We must keep our eyes on the great mission."
Sarah: "What is that? What is so important that we let this girl suffer?"
*Xan released her.*
Xanthippe: "It will come. One day, when you're ready, I will tell you. For now, I only ask that you trust me."
*But Sarah had no choice.*
*Xan would not intercede, this she now knew, and she wasn't yet powerful enough to do anything.*
*And so the girl suffered her fate, and Sarah turned her eyes away from it.*
*The image would remain seared in her mind.*
*She never would learn what became of the girl, but her tragedy became a part of Sarah.*
*The two returned via the door they came, back to the house in Lethram.*
*Neither spoke, and each retreated to their rooms, to contemplate in silence.*
*Months passed and seasons turned.*
*Sarah had lost all relation to time, perhaps even the world outside of the wizard's house.*
*There was only the study, and her endless lessons.*
*Ever since she had seen her home country again, she had become posessed with a purpose.*
*Many nights even Xan would retire to bed earlier than her.*
*Before, she had engaged with her lessons as if they had simply been classes, the kind she had been taught growing up in Castle Reinmeer.*
*Now, she understood them for what they were. The path towards power, towards mastery of magic.*
*The thing that would allow her to change the world.*
*Sarah raised up her hand. Guiding the tempo of her movement now came natural to her, no longer forced.*
*A muscle long unused but now trained was flexed.*
*The feeling of the energy around her, within her, she had learned to guide it without becoming distracted by it.*
*Then, all things faded.*
*There was no more room. No air around her. No noise.*
*Only the perfection of her form, the gathering static of her power, and then the utterance of her words.*
*The passed from her lips as if nearly silent, but in her mind, their meaning screamed and roared as she imprinted her will onto the magical energies.*
*By her will alone, she crushed, broke, reshaped and forged the magical energies into the shape that she needed...demanded.*
*As wind to a hurricane. As water to a tsunami. As a spark to a blaze.*
*The seperate energies forged together became more than their parts. Sarah extended her palm, and manifested her will.*
*From her extended palm, an orb of near pure light erupted, firing off towards Xan.*
*Splitting across the room, the orb crashed into Xan's barrier. Had he not been ready for it, even the mighty mage would have paid dearly.*
*Sparks scattered across the room as the orb sliced and spun, its force splintering fragments of Xan's magical shield.*
*Sarah looked on, and continued to impress her will upon her creation, pushing the orb deeper into Xan's defenses.*
*Suddenly, she watched as Xan began to move his hand, performing movements and speaking words she had never seen before.*
*No sooner did she notice, did the orb's energy dissipate, sparing what was left of the mage's shield.*
Sarah: "Not fair. You're using new spells."
*Xan laughed.*
Xanthippe: "Sorry, but I wasn't about to let my head get taken off for a practice lesson."
Sarah: "You mean I was close."
*He nodded.*
Xanthippe: "My barrier would not have held much longer."
*Sarah eyed Xan. She might have nearly shattered his barrier, but he did not appear to be in much distress about it.*
Sarah: "So I almost defeated you?"
Xanthippe: "Maybe, if I had kept up the barrier and done nothing else."
Xanthippe: "But you'll have to understand that in a fight, a real fight, no magic user would just stand and absorb your hits like that."
Xanthippe: "In a real fight."
*The mage was gone.*
*Sarah felt his hand slapping the back of her head.*
Xanthippe: "A real mage would have been moving."
*Sarah spun around.*
*There was nobody behind her.*
Xanthippe: "And you're far from ready for that."
*Sarah turned back around to face Xan.*
Sarah: "How did you..."
Xanthippe: "Magic. That much should be obvious by now."
*Sarah rolled her eyes.*
Sarah: "That's always your answer to everything."
Xanthippe: "And it's almost always true."

*Xan considered his answer for a moment.*
Xanthippe: "For most, I would say years, but for you Sarah, I don't know. Maybe months, maybe only weeks..."
Xanthippe: "You're progressing so much faster than even I could have even dared to hope."
*Sarah smiled at his compliment.*
*She knew she was progressing fast. Even when the mage had said nothing of it, she could see in his face, his stunned surprise by how fast she now mastered certain arts.*
Sarah: "A prodigy, huh?."
*Xan nodded.*
Xanthippe: "A natural aptitude, but such is no replacement for commitment. That's what's changed."

Xanthippe: "Maybe you were, but not like you've been working for the last few months."
*Sarah knew he was right.*
*Having seen what became of her country, her people...*
*But worse than the carnage was knowing she could do nothing for her people. That she had to stand by and let it all happen.*
*She would never let herself be that weak again.*
Sarah: "I think it just took some time to click for me, you know?"
*Sarah could see Xan studying her. Trying to unravel her inner thoughts.*
*Could he see, she wondered, what was in her mind?*
Xanthippe: "Magic comes to each in their own speed. For you perhaps faster than most, but still, you should not push yourself too much. There is plenty of time."
Sarah: "Plenty of time?"
*Xan paused for a moment.*
Xanthippe: "Of course. You have a lifetime to master it."
*Sarah wasn't a fool. She knew that wasn't what he had meant to say. Still, it was pointless to press him.*
*Xan had habit of going his own pace. Only revealing what he wanted to, and never a fraction more. She decided to drop it.*
Sarah: "So, now that I've mastered that spell, what comes next?"
*Xan laughed.*
Xanthippe: "I hardly doubt you've mastered it."
Sarah: "Fine, whatever, I can do it just fine. I want to know what comes next."
Xanthippe: "Didn't I just say you shouldn't rush?"
*Sarah shrugged.*
Sarah: "I've barely broken a sweat. I can keep going."
Xanthippe: "You, maybe, but I'm not as young as I may appear. Holding off those attacks takes a lot out of me."
*She watched Xan shuffle across the room, dropping down into his chair.*
*There were other things she could do. Train by herself. Study even more. But something kept her here.*
*Had it been what he said earlier?*
Sarah: "What comes after this?"
Xanthippe: "The next spell? Ooh, I'll have to see, I'm thinking your first transubstantion spell, that should prove a challenge."
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "No, I'm not talking about the next spell, or the spell after that."
Sarah: "I'm asking where this road leads to? In the long term."
*Xan rubbed his temples.*
Xanthippe: "You'll be my apprentice for a few years more, until I decide you've learned enough."
Xanthippe: "Then you'll be introduced to the masters in the citadel, who can decide whether you're ready."
Xanthippe: "If they allow it, you will be included into our order as a mage of the first tower."
Xanthippe: "From there, you will continue your studies. Every few years you will advance, if you learn enough, to the ranks tower."
Xanthippe: "When you're a mage of the fifth tower, you will be allowed to take on an apprentice."
Xanthippe: "Then you will teach them as I taught you."
Xanthippe: "Maybe one day, centuries from now, you can retire to the elder circle, guide our order, and so on."
*Sarah listened as Xan painted a picture of her life.*
*Choose*
*That sounds nice.*:
Sarah: "That sounds nice."
Xanthippe: "Exactly. This life of ours, studying magic, it can be very orderly. Very measured."
Xanthippe: "You'll always know where you stand."
*It did sound nice to Sarah. Clean, orderly, decisive. No more doubt.*
*That sounds horrible.*:
Sarah: "That sounds horrible."
Xanthippe: "What do you mean?"
Sarah: "To be locked away in some citadel? Studying for centuries, all to what end? So I can watch the world turn by?"
Xanthippe: "The opposite. From that vantage point, you will see the world."
Xanthippe: "Rather than be trapped inside of it, you can watch the turning of human society."

Xanthippe: "Exactly."

Xanthippe: "What about me?"

*Xan laughed.*
Xanthippe: "I get out, don't worry. Endless doors and rooms lead to ever corner of the world."
Xanthippe: "Before I ran into you, I was quite busy."
*Sarah looked at Xan, trying to gain a measure of him.*
Sarah: "Doing what?"

*Xan rapped his knuckles across the desk.*
Xanthippe: "You're right, it's not."
Xanthippe: "We spoke of it, months ago when I took you to visit Rosanna."
*Memories flooded Sarah's mind. Memories she hoped would stay buried.*

Xanthippe: "The council has plans, designs, that it hopes can come about."
Xanthippe: "The council believes that with the proper guidance, we can steer this world towards peace, towards a future where the horrors of war, famine and all other tragedies can be done away with."
Xanthippe: "A future where every soul, be it a king or a peasant, will be valued and safeguarded."
*Sarah listened intently as Xan spoke.*
Sarah: "It sounds like a fantasy."

Xanthippe: "The world is brutal, but it used to be much more so."

Xanthippe: "And that's how the council likes it."

*Xan shook his head.*
Xanthippe: "You don't, because they mean nothing to you, and Rosanna still means everything to you."
Xanthippe: "But that is a flaw in your perspective, a flaw that you will learn to overcome in the years that follow."
*Sarah listened to what Xan told her.*
*Sarah watched the mage retire to his room and sat by herself as night set in.*
*Maybe he was right. But the thought alone scared her.*
*Could she ever become like him? Stand idly by and watch innocents suffer, because some great design demands it?*
*Would she even want to be that cold?*
*She wanted power, enough to reshape the world, but what if following this path would change her?*
*What if she gained the power to change the world, but in the process lost the will to change it?*

*Months turned to years as Sarah followed her studies under Xan.*
*Her mastery of magic continued to grow as she devoured the endless libraries of the world.*
*The world.*
*She had come to see so much of it by now.*
*Sarah walked with Xan across every continent and every nation.*

*Promises were made, influence was peddled, bribes were handed out.*
*Sarah could see they were working towards something, yet she did not know what, nor did Xan ever tell her much of it.*
*There was a loneliness in that house, made worse by how Xan kept her at a distance.*
*Perhaps it was this fact that drove Sarah into the arms of the spirit.*
*She feared the spirit too much to visit it more than every few months, but sooner or later, her urges would overtake her better judgement, and she would meet with the spirit.*
*An unusual friend in an otherwise lonely place.*
*The spirit, Razaphel, continued to be an odd presence. It whispered as she passed it, but she ignored the creature as best she could.*
*Even now, she did not know what to make of the creature.*
*It was under this same set of unclear circumstances that Sarah now found herself in the great palace of the city of Bagrad.*
*Bagrad had once been a great city. Seated at the heart of a great empire, the city grew so impressive that for centuries after all other cities appeared only poor imitations.*
*But that had been centuries ago.*
*Today, Bagrad was the last vestige of that old empire. A city that once housed millions; now barely a hundred-thousand remained.*
*And yet, the city still stood. Its vast monuments immune to the forces of nature and decay, testament to a place that once meant something.*
*The people of Bagrad, and it's royal family, were much like their city.*
*Though time had changed, their perception of themselves seemed immutable. Even now they considered themselves far above the rest of the world, even as the world had all but forgotten about them.*
*It was this arrogance that had brought Sarah and Xan to the city.*
*The head of the royal family, the Shah Mahda, had hosted some festivities several months ago.*
*During the festivities, a young Mythran prince too drunk on wine, spoke too truthfully of what had become of Bagrad and its people.*
*The Shah Mahda, too arrogant to let this slight pass, killed the young Mythran prince.*
*The Shah had failed to understand that Bagrad survived by virtue of being too unimportant to conquer, but with the spilling of important blood he had given a cause for war that weighed heavier than strategy.*
*A few miles outside of the city walls, a Mythran army led by the uncle of the slain prince was camped. Soon they would begin their assault.*
*In desperation, the Shah had reached out to any potential ally who might save him, but a scarce few had answered.*
*That was, until Xan told Sarah that they were going to offer the city their protection.*
*It was not unheard of for mages to step unto a battlefield, but Sarah could not help wonder why this battle was worth their intervention.*
Sarah: "I doubt they're going to survive for very long."
*Xan stood off to the side, his neck craned, seemingly trying to find someone or something.*
Xanthippe: "Maybe."
*He seemed distracted.*
Xanthippe: "We'll just need to make sure they make it through today."
Xanthippe: "A Mythran host is no joke, but the Bagrad army should be able to keep them off for a while. We're mostly here just to protect the palace from anyone that sneaks past the main battle."
*Sarah observed Xan. He was always so different when they left the house. Out here in the real world.*
*Anxious, seemingly always on edge.*
Sarah: "I'm glad my years of magical training can be put to use as a bodyguard."

Xanthippe: "Yes, it's not the most glorious task, but sometimes even these base things need to be done."

Xanthippe: "We didn't press the issue because we imagined we had more time, but after he made a mess of it, we're now suddenly very short on time."

Servant: *All rise!*

Xanthippe: "Honourable Shah, it is with humility that we received your invitation and with eagerness that we have answered it."
*Xan always struck Sarah as a man of many faces.*

*Sarah could see the Shah observing them.*
*But she also realized that Xan had understood the Shah.*

Shah Mahda: "You may stay, for now..."

Shah Mahda: "Do you see, Samayra? I told you to count your fingers when you're around these creatures."
*Suddenly, Sarah noticed someone standing off to the side of the Shah, hidden away in the shadow of his throne.*
Samayra: "Yes, father."
*Her voice carried softly through the room.*
*She kept her head down, eyes fixed to the floor. There was something about her, quiet in both voice and presence.*
*Sarah studied the girl. She was close to herself in age but she gave off a quiet and reserved energy that made her seem so much younger.*
*Or perhaps, Sarah considered, it was she herself who had become older than her age over these last few years.*
*The Shah had spoken to his daugther, but paid her little heed after, turning his attention back to Xan.*
Shah Mahda: "My war council will soon gather to discuss our strategy in defending the city. I insist that you join us."

*With the wave of his hand, the Shah dismissed the both of them. Advisors flocked to his seat, hoping to spare a moment with him, but Sarah could see he was distracted.*
*Sarah tried to imagine if Thomas had been like this...*
*When the tribesmen invaded, and he had been left all alone to defend Rosanna, did he have these quiet moments of fear?*
*Sarah shook her head to clear it, as she walked along with Xan to the far side of the room.*
*Thinking about her brother was too painful, and yet, even years later she still found herself thinking about him.*
*One part of her wanted to numb the pain, the other wanted it to linger forever like a poorly healed wound so that she might never forget him.*
Xanthippe: "Well, that went better than I thought it would."
Sarah: "You weren't surprised that he was angry that it's just you and me?"
*Xan shrugged.*
Xanthippe: "I know the council played coy with their promises, but I also knew he had no choice but to accept our help."
Sarah: "Will the two of us be enough to make a difference?"
*Xan stared into the distance.*
Xanthippe: "Maybe, it depends on how the fighting plays out. But it doesn't matter."
Sarah: "It doesn't?"
Xanthippe: "No, we're not here to save Bagrad. Whether it survives or falls is irrelevant. The vault remains the first priority."
Sarah: "But if Bagrad falls and the palace is overrun with soldiers and mercenaries, I imagine finding the vault would prove difficult."
*Xan nodded.*
Xanthippe: "Correct, so we should at least try to keep them out for a few days. Enough time for the Shah to let us into the vault, or otherwise find a way in."
