*She spun around in the air towards the voice and saw her.*
*Her old friend.*
Sarah: "Kate..."
Kate: "Sarah...what did you do..."
*Who was she.*
*Who was she to come here, after all these years, and question her.*
*The girl who she thought was her friend. The one who robbed her of her home, stole her away across an ocean, and forever changed her life.*
*The thief. The drunkard. The traitor.*
*Her old friend.*
Sarah: "Who do you think you are to question me about anything?"
*Sarah could see the radiant light that she cast, shimmering, cutting through the darkness. She illuminated everything.*
*The pale light brought out Kate's features. The fear in her face.*
Kate: "Sarah...why did you do that?"
Sarah: "Because I am here on a mission. To guard this place from low-lives that would seek to loot it."
Kate: "You killed Caleb...and Ephraim..."
*The names sounded familiar. A lifetime ago. Kind men. Had she really snuffed out their lives so casually?*
Sarah: "And who are they to me?"
Sarah: "Nobodies. People that I might have known years ago."
Sarah: "A lot has changed, as you might notice."
*Sarah could see the magical energies crackle around her, emphasizing her power.*
Kate: "You're a freak..."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Maybe. But it took me a long time to find my way back to myself after what you did to me. When you stabbed me in the back."
Kate: "Sarah...I..."
Sarah: "Don't deny it, Kate. Save yourself and myself the disgrace of lying."
*Sarah could see Kate struggle to find the words.*
*Choose*
*Kill Kate*:
*Sarah raised up her hands towards her old friend, magical energies twisting around her arms, ready for the kill.*
Sarah: "You used my trust in you, and you betrayed me."
Sarah: "You thought because I was just some spoiled noble girl, you could use me and treat my life like it meant nothing."
Sarah: "I never sought revenge against you, but you've brought yourself here."
*A silence lingered.*
Sarah: "Any last words?"
*Sarah could see Kate had none.*
*Kate did not run, fight or beg. It would have made no difference, but still, she did not.*
*Sarah snapped her fingers.*
*Kate died in flame.*
*So intense did the fires burn that soon only ash and soot were left of her.*
*Then, the last of the soldiers followed her in death.*
*Sarah stepped down back onto the ground.*
*A dominating silence hung over the room. Ashes slowly drifted across the floor.*
*Spare Kate*:
*Sarah lowered her arms.*
*Despite everything, she couldn't do it.*
Sarah: "Leave."
Sarah: "Take the rest of your soldiers and leave, before I change my mind."
*Sarah watched as Kate turned to gather the soldiers and exit the throne room.*
*Neither spoke another word to the other.*
*The room was empty.*
*A dominating silence hung over the room. Ashes slowly drifted across the floor.*
*It was over.*
*After repelling the last of the soldiers, nobody else came to try again.*
*Maybe it was only a small advance party, or maybe rumors spread of the mad mage that guarded this room.*
*Whatever it was, Sarah had succeeded.*
*She sat down on the steps that led up towards the throne and looked out across the throne room.*
*Traces of her magic could be seen across the room, but it wasn't anything some servants wouldn't be able to fix.*
*Sarah breathed in.*
*The smell of ash and burned blood was heavy in the air.*
*All this power.*
*She had given up so much to gain it, made it her goal in life, and yet it never made her happy.*
*Being able to end a life with little more than a gesture, made taking it feel like a small thing. It made people seem like small things.*
*Sarah began to understand how Xan, having done this for centuries, could have turned so cold.*
*Would she?*
*Had she already?*
*Sarah tries to clear her mind, sitting amidst the ashes.*
*Hours pass, but Sarah remains at her post.*
*No other soldiers make an attempt to breach the throne room, but outside, the sounds grow louder.*
*She contemplates leaving, but thinking of Samayra, she remains guarding the throne room.*
*More time passes, when suddenly, the doors to the throne room are thrown wide open again.*
*Sarah leaps to the ready, gathering her power, but lowers her guard.*
*It's Xan.*
*Sarah watches her mentor stride across the room.*
Xanthippe: "Sarah! Are you alright?"
*Sarah runs up to him. She can see blood pouring from his temple.*
Sarah: "I'm fine, but what about you?"
*The mage waves his hands, dismissing her concern.*
Xanthippe: "It's nothing, forget about it."
Sarah: "What happened out there?"
*Xan sighs.*
Xanthippe: "They broke through..."
*Sarah was stunned.*
Sarah: "What?"
Xanthippe: "The Mythran army came through the main gate, as expected, but they brought more heavy artillery than we expected."
Xanthippe: "Their cannons kept us pinned down. I was barely able to hold onto a position for longer than a few spells. I had to keep moving."
Xanthippe: "As they kept shelling us, their forces moved out and engaged the Bagrad army on the center square."
Xanthippe: "By the end, we had to abandon all positions and fall back into the city itself."
Sarah: "So they'll be here soon?"
*Xan stroked his chin.*
Xanthippe: "Maybe. The city is like a maze, and the small alleys will keep the Mythran army from moving too fast..."
Xanthippe: "But yes, sooner or later, they will move and take the palace. The Bagrad army won't hold out for long."
*Sarah began to pace back and forth.*
Sarah: "So...what do we do now?"
Xanthippe: "We do what we came here for. Get into the vault."
Sarah: "I know where it is."
Xanthippe: "What?"
Sarah: "The vault, I can take us there."
Xanthippe: "How?"
Sarah: "Samayra showed me. She guided me through the secret tunnels, I can find our way back. I left a magical trace."
*Xan began to laugh.*
Xanthippe: "Incredible. You really are amazing, Sarah."
Xanthippe: "Let's go then, no time to waste."
*Together, the two took off. Passing through the abandoned hallways, the sounds of battle could be heard across the city.*
*Through Sarah's room, into the secret tunnel, and following the magical trace, the two quickly found their way to the vault.*
Sarah: "And how do you propose we do that? We have no idea where it is."
*Xan was quiet for a moment, before resuming.*
Xanthippe: "You're right. It's somewhere in the tunnels that run under the palace, but I don't know much more than that."
Sarah: "And those tunnels probably stretch for miles. We don't have the time explore them."
Xanthippe: "I was hoping there would be a better way..."
Xanthippe: "SHAH MAHDA!!!"
*Xan's voice, undoubtedly amplified by magic, roared through the throne room, shaking the stone itself.*
*A moment passed, then, movement.*
*Appearing from the royal quarters, the Shah emerged.*
Shah Mahda: "Wizard, you've returned from the front."
Shah Mahda: "Tell me, how goes the battle?"
Xanthippe: "I've come for our end of the bargain."
*A pause lingered.*
Shah Mahda: "I commanded you to tell me how the battle goes. Speak, wizard, lest I send you away."
Xanthippe: "A disaster."
Xanthippe: "The front has collapsed and the Mythran army is inside your city. In a few hours, they'll be all over this city."
*The Shah's face turned white as paper, as if the very idea of defeat had never crossed his mind before.*
Shah Mahda: "You...you're lying...this cannot be..."
Shah Mahda: "The Bagrad army...is...no..."
*The Shah began to anxiously pace from side to side.*
Xanthippe: "Enough, Shah. We want our payment."
Shah Mahda: "Your payment!?!"
*He nearly screamed his response.*
Shah Mahda: "You have failed me. My city will be looted by these, these savages, and you want a reward?"
Shah Mahda: "For what? Stabbing me in the back?"
Shah Mahda: "I knew I was a fool to trust you. Wizards, warlocks, witches, all the same."
*Xan looked at Sarah, before fixing his gaze back on the Shah.*
Xanthippe: "I inflicted great casualties on the enemy, slowing their advance. My apprentice repelled a sneak attack from a mercenary party."
Xanthippe: "We have made good on our end, and now we demand you show us the vault."
*The Shah laughed.*
Shah Mahda: "Demand all you want, you won't get a thing from me."
*Xan stomped his heel on the ground, shaking the earth. This got them the Shah's attention.*
Xanthippe: "Listen to me you fool."
Xanthippe: "Your city will fall, this is simply a fact."
Xanthippe: "Before the battle is over, your army will collapse and even your most loyal guards will abandon their posts."
Xanthippe: "Right near the end, your own personal bodyguards will begin to question their loyalty, question what they might get if they hand you and your family over."
Xanthippe: "I've seen it play out countless times before."
Xanthippe: "My offer is simple. Give us the vault, and we will come back to you. We will stay here and negotiate a surrender on your behalf."
Xanthippe: "Instead of you and your family being dragged out and stomped to death, you might very well still make it out alive."
*The Shah shook his head in disbelief.*
Shah Mahda: "As what? A vassal state to those depraved Mythrans? Never."
*Sarah stepped forward.*
Sarah: "Think of your daughter!"
*Suddenly, the Shah was stunned.*
Sarah: "When their soldiers march in here, without us to protect you, they'll be more brutal than you can even imagine."
Sarah: "You might be strong, you might be willing to die for your city, but what about Samayra."
Sarah: "What about her life?"
*Sarah and Xan watched the Shah struggle.*
Shah Mahda: "Curse the both of you..."
*But the Shah's voice had dropped. His defiance seemed gone.*
*Reaching into his pocket, he threw a piece of paper unto the ground.*
Shah Mahda: "There. Those are the directions to the vault. Take them, if you promise you will negotiate our surrender and keep my daughter safe."
*Xan bowed.*
Xanthippe: "This I promise you, Shah."
*Xan fished the sheet of paper from the ground and studied it for a moment.*
Xanthippe: "Let's go then, no time to waste."
*Together, the two took off. Passing through the abandoned hallways, the sounds of battle could be heard across the city.*
*Through Sarah's room, into the secret tunnel, and following the magical trace, the two quickly found their way to the vault.*
*Sarah looked to her side and watched Xan study the metal doors that blocked their access to the vault.*
Sarah: "Now what?"
Xanthippe: "I'm considering."
Sarah: "It's humming with magic. I don't think we'll get far just trying to open it."
*Xan nodded.*
Xanthippe: "It would almost certainly kill us if we just touched it."
Sarah: "So...what then?"
*Xan shrugged.*
Xanthippe: "We're out off any good options, so all we have left are the bad ones."
Sarah: "Meaning?"
Xanthippe: "Meaning we rip it open, one spell at a time."
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "Centuries old, one of the greatest mages of all time, and that's your solution?"
*Xan laughed.*
Xanthippe: "You see, that's your problem Sarah. You overthink everything. Sometimes the direct approach is the best approach. Let's get started."
*Together, Sarah and Xan began to gather up their magical energies, one after the other releasing a barrage of offensive spells.*
*The raw energy sparked and scattered as it crashed into the magical barriers and wards that guarded the door, but with every attack, they grew thinner.*
*The sounds rang loud, echoing through the tunnels, but the sounds of battle outside masked their cacophony.*
*After nearly an hour, the last of the wards finally collapsed, and their magical energies cut through the metal door.*
*The hole left by their magic seared red with intense heat, like metal to a forge.*
*Xan stepped forward and passed through the opening first. Sarah followed soon after.*
*On the other side, Sarah felt a chill pass over her body.*
*The air was cold in the tunnels, but here, it was colder still.*
*A stillness in the air seemed to tell her that very few people ever came here.*
*Xan waved his hand, bringing a light to the vault.*
*To Sarah's surprise, the light reached far and deeper into the darkness, but she could not make out the other end, so large was the vault.*
*Everywhere she looked, she could see an endless variation of treasure. Trinkets, gold, jewels, paintings.*
*The wealth of an empire was on display here, or whatever was left of one.*
Sarah: "Now what? What are we looking for?"
Xanthippe: "We'll split up, the vault is far too large."
Xanthippe: "We're looking for a stone, a shining red jewel."
Sarah: "Like a ruby?"
*Xan shook his head.*
Xanthippe: "Not quite a ruby, but something like it. You'll know it when you see it. It emits a sort of crimson red light."
Xanthippe: "When you find it, no matter what, do not touch it."
Xanthippe: "Call me over, and I will handle it from there."
Sarah: "Why?"
Xanthippe: "Because it's beyond dangerous, Sarah. It's more dangerous than you can possibly imagine, and I don't want you handling it."
Sarah: "Fine, I'll call you over should I find it."
Xanthippe: "Good, I'll go left, you take right."
*With that, Xan took off.*
*Sarah began her own exploration, walking through the piled up crates and mountains of gold.*
*How much wealth, she imagined, sat here simply boxed up. Enough to change a thousand lives forever, but here, too trivial even to take out of the box.*
*Walking through the vault brought about an odd feelig.*
*All these things, unseen, untouched and unnoticed.*
*What did art mean, or wealth, when it just sat here, hidden from the world. Other than the Shah, who ever even looked at these things? Did he even?*
*Once, artist and labourers poured their sweat and tears into creating these masterworks, all so they could end up here, forgotten.*
*Perhaps, Sarah thought, it might be better if they were looted, thrown back out into the world.*
*Sarah slowly followed her path, illuminating her path with a simple spell.*
*Would she even know it if she saw it?*
*Sarah passed one artwork after the other. There was no time to stop and wonder.*
*In the corner of her eyes, she recognizes something.*
*Sarah stops and turns towards the massive painting.*
*Her heart stops for a moment.*
*Depicted upon the canvas is the royal family of Rosanna. Her father. Her brother. And herself.*
*Her father sits towards the center, she and her brother by his side. Strong. Regal. Just as he had been in life.*
*Sarah knew this painting well. It once had a prominent place in Castle Reinmeer.*
*So often she had walked past it, observed it, traced its meticulous design.*
*And now it was here.*
*Sarah reached out, touching the frame of the painting as if to make sure it was real.*
Sarah: "How did you end up here..."
*Looting, she had no doubt. The tribesmen must have seized it, and with no use for art, sold it off to some merchant, passing hands until one day it dissapeared into this vault.*
*What a prize it must have been, the painting of the last royal family of Rosanna.*
*She couldn't take it with her, yet, it also felt wrong to her to leave it behind. It wasn't theirs, it belonged to her.*
*Sarah committed  the painting to mind. Then, she reached out, and with the touch of her palm, burned it.*
*The old material of the canvas caused it to catch fire easily, burning out in only a few seconds. Like that, it was gone. Remaining only to Sarah's own mind.*
*As she turned to resume her search, a glimmer of crimson caught her eye near the end of the path.*
*Sarah rushed forward, fearing to lose sight of it, but not long after found herself coming upon the object.*
*It was as Xan had said a stone that shone with light of crimson, but it was also not quite a gemstone or a ruby.*
*The light swirled within it. The colours softly shifted, from crimson to other variations of the colour, exploring patterns Sarah had never seen before in her life.*
*Don't touch it.*
*She tried to remind herself, because the object seemed to almost reach out to her, begging to be seized.*
*Acting before she could finish her thought, her hand had reached out and grabbed the object.*
*Sarah nearly turned to call out to Xan, only for the light around her to begin to fade.*
*There was still a light, but it turned cold and grey, and the sounds around her grew muted.*
*Something arose from the shadow, swirling and shifting. One most familiar to Sarah.*
Sarah: "What are you doing here?"
Razaphel: "No way to greet an old friend, Sarah."
Sarah: "Is that what we are? Friends?"
*The spirit spun and twirled around the stone.*
*Sarah was unsure of what this meant. The spirit had always been bound in place by its flask. For it to now move so freely, here of all places...*
Sarah: "How are you appearing here?"
Razaphel: "Here...there..."
Razaphel: "Not all concepts that govern your species are quite so strict on mine."
Razaphel: "The space around this stone is as near to me as the flask, and as near as some other places. It is you that has moved far, I have sat still."
Sarah: "I've come all this way, just to be tortured by your riddles?"
Razaphel: "Why, were you hoping we could do something else?"
*The spirit taunted her with their carnal connection.*
Sarah: "Don't flatter yourself. You're a tool to an end."
*A hiss emerged from the spirit, what passed for laughter.*
*Sarah hated herself for allowing the creature to seize her body, yet knew she could not deny her weakness for it.*
*The spirit was silent.*
Sarah: "Tell me, why are you appearing here?"
Razaphel: "I told you a long time ago, Sarah, that there were things we could speak of, but only when the time was right."
Sarah: "And?"
Razaphel: "That moment is now, in this place..."
*Sarah observed the spirit. Its intentions, much like its shape, were hard to grasp.*
Sarah: "Why?"
Razaphel: "Because here we can speak freely."
Sarah: "And we couldn't in Xan's house?"
Razaphel: "We couldn't anywhere, Sarah. Always eyes, always ears, everywhere, watching, looking, seeing. Only in this space are we unseen."
Sarah: "Unseen?"
*The creature twisted through the air.*
Razaphel: "Here, so near the stone, the gods can't see us."
Sarah: "The gods..."
Sarah: "What are you talking about? Enought with the riddles!"
*Sarah stomped her feet on the ground.*
Razaphel: "The gods of your world have long vanished, so many have forgotten they ever existed. But they have only lain dormant."
Razaphel: "They hide in the place beyond, observing the passing of this world."
*Sarah shook her head. As always, the spirit enjoyed obscuring his meaning.*
Sarah: "What are you talking about? The gods are a story we tell, they're not real."
Razaphel: "Ooh no, sweet Sarah, they are far more than fiction."
Razaphel: "The mage told you of the empire that preceded all other empires. Of how an empress made a foul bargain, and cursed my world to be fixed under yours."
*Sarah remembered that story.*
Razaphel: "After, the gods of your world vanished, but in truth, they merely escaped it. They hid because the destruction caused by the world collision killed one of them and left the others weakened."
Razaphel: "For the first time in their existence, they realized they could die."
Razaphel: "Fearing their own deaths, they escaped."
Razaphel: "But not before enacting their final scheme, the Golden Path."
*Sarah observed the creature. It had no face, and with it, no hints as to whether it spoke truth or lie.*
Sarah: "The Golden Path?"
Razaphel: "Your gods weaved fate itself into the fabric of your world. They uttered their design, and created the mechanism by which to manifest it."
Razaphel: "They both saw the future, and uttered it into existence, at the same time."
*Sarah rubbed her temples in frustration.*
Sarah: "What does that mean?"
Razaphel: "It means that your race, as well as mine, was forever trapped. Trapped to walk down a road that only led to one outcome."
Razaphel: "Their victory. Their return. The resumption of divinity."
Razaphel: "All the world and all its people dream themselves free, but in truth, walk in the divine plan of your gods, robbed of their agency."
Razaphel: "Each unkowingly performs the inevitable act that will bring about their rebirth."
*Sarah struggled to make sense of what the spirit was telling her.*
*All the world a fiction, each soul playing a pre-written part in some play, authored by another.*
Sarah: "Then...all our lives...are already determined?"
*The spirit shifted, excited.*
Razaphel: "No, Sarah, not all lives..."
Razaphel: "The gods can see everything, they know everything."
Razaphel: "Rising up against them is foolishness, for they have forseen every resistance, and will prevent any that might rise, and those that do, they willed to occur. Everything walks in their path."
Sarah: "What then?"
Razaphel: "This stone..."
*The spirit weaved its body around it.*
Razaphel: "These are rare artifacts, called fate stones."
Razaphel: "We pulled them, deep from void of the underworld, as a means of fighting back."
Razaphel: "They block the sight of the gods, making them blind to what transpires near the stone."
Sarah: "This is why you could never tell me this before...because in Xan's house, the gods would have seen and heard us..."
*The spirit hissed.*
Razaphel: "Yes, Sarah, that's right. Had I spoken back then, they would have known, and our resistance would have been futile from the start."
Sarah: "Resistance?"
Razaphel: "Yes, together, Sarah, we can resist this tyranny of heaven. Break free from the chains of your gods, and return agency to the world."
Razaphel: "The control they wield over this world is but a fraction of what they will wield if they return."
Razaphel: "All the world will become theirs, down to every atom. If they are reborn, their yoke will become unbreakable."
*Sarah looked around, trying to find an answer.*
Sarah: "I'll need to talk to Xan about this."
Razaphel: "NO!"
*The creature's voice boomed as it rushed forward.*
Razaphel: "You cannot trust him!"
Razaphel: "He is their agent. His entire order serves their design."
Sarah: "Why? Why would they do that?"
Razaphel: "Because they were there..."
Sarah: "There?"
Razaphel: "When the empire fell. He was there."
*The realization struck Sarah like a brick.*
*She had known Xan was old. Like all mages, he lived a long life, centuries she had imagined...*
*But if the spirit's words were true...*
Sarah: "If that's true, that means he's more than two millenia old..."
Razaphel: "He is, and he has tirelessly worked from the day that he saw the empire fall, to bring about the return of his masters."
Razaphel: "No matter what, you cannot tell him you know this."
Sarah: "Or what?"
Razaphel: "Or he will kill you."
*Sarah tried to think. Would he really kill her?*
*Then again, Sarah thought, how much did she truly know Xan at all?*
*If he was more than two millenia old...why would he think twice of killing an inconvenient girl that he knew for only a fraction of his life...*
Sarah: "I...what do I do..."
Razaphel: "When you leave this place and return to his house, we can work together to overcome him."
Razaphel: "He is strong, but he is not stronger than the both of us..."
Sarah: "You mean to kill him?"
Razaphel: "No...if it can be helped, I won't. But I will need your help to do so."
*Sarah tried to think it over.*
*Betraying Xan, on the word of this creature...*
*And yet, what if the spirit spoke true? Then all her life she had been a puppet to some gods, a plaything.*
*And Xan, he had tricked and lied to her, used her towards his own ends. Was it wrong to betray someone who betrayed her first?*
*Sarah didn't know what to do.*
*Suddenly, the sound of rushing footsteps could be heard.*
*Xan drew close.*
Razaphel: "Remember my words. Hold close the stone and you can break free!"
*With those words, the spirit vanished.*
*Xan came rushing up from a distance.*
Xanthippe: "Sarah!"
Sarah: "What?"
Xanthippe: "I told you to warn me when you found the stone. Did you touch it?"
*Sarah nodded absently.*
Sarah: "Sorry. I just...I saw it and I lost track of time...it's like nothing I've ever seen before."
Xanthippe: "It's alright, just stay clear from it."
*Xan moved up, stepping in between Sarah and the fate stone.*
*Pulling a satin scarf from his pocket, he carefully wrapped the stone without touching it and placed it in his pocket.*
Xanthippe: "We have what we came for."
Xanthippe: "We'll go back up, the door back to the house is in the upper eastern wing, we should be back home before you know it."
Xanthippe: "I can't wait to be rid of this horrid place."
*Xan began to walk away, until Sarah stopped him.*
Sarah: "You gave them your word."
Xanthippe: "What?"
Sarah: "The Shah...Samayra...you told them we would come back, to protect them..."
*Xan sighed.*
Xanthippe: "Look, Sarah, I said what I had to in order to get into the vault. Now we have what we came for."
Xanthippe: "The battle is already lost."
Xanthippe: "The truth is that the Shah, his daughter and probably his entire royal household will be dead or wishing they were dead before the night is over."
*Sarah stepped foward.*
Sarah: "NO!"
*Xan seemed shocked by her outburst.*
Sarah: "We promised them that we would protect them. Even if that only means allowing them to run away, or giving them enough time to safely surrender...we promised!"
Xanthippe: "So what? The Shah was planning to stab us in the back since we got here, and now you feel like we owe him?"
Sarah: "If not him, at least his daughter, she didn't do anything wrong."
*Xan laughed.*
Xanthippe: "Ooh, that's great. We need to risk our lives because you have some obsession with that girl?"
Xanthippe: "Forget it."
*Sarah stepped foward again, blocking Xan's path.*
Sarah: "We're going to help them. We gave them our word."
Sarah: "That might not mean anything to you, but it does to me."
Xanthippe: "And what if I just leave? You think you can do this alone?"
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "No, I don't. If you leave, I'll most likely die trying to help them."
*Each was quiet for a moment.*
Sarah: "So, you might not care if they live or die, but maybe you'll care if I live or die."
*Xan sighed.*
Xanthippe: "Gods, you can be obnoxious."
Xanthippe: "Fine, we'll help them, but only to negotiate a safe surrender. I'm not fighting an entire Mythran army."
*The two turned around and left for the throne room, neither bothering to speak to the other.*
*Sarah and Xan arrived back at the throne room.*
*When they had left, it was empty, but by now the first army units of the Mythran army had begun to swarm in.*
*It was nothing like before, when Sarah had faced a small advance group of poorly armed mercenaries.*
*This was a real army.*
*Hundreds of men, marching in formation, bearing full plate armor. Swords, lances, bows.*
*They were ready for everything.*
*One man marched at the front of the soldiers. His armor was covered in intricate designs, seperating him from the ordinary soldiers.*
Mythran Prince: *Shah Mahda! Come out of your little rat hiding hole before I send in my men to drag you out like the vermin you are.*
Mythran Prince: *The least you can do is die with some honour.*
*There came no response.*
Mythran Prince: *Whatever, I don't have the patience for this. Men! Tear down the barricade and drag these rats out, alive!*
*A sound cut through all the others, as the room went silent.*
*The clattering of wood, then steel.*
*Piece by piece, the fragments that made up the barricade to the royal quarters came down, being taken apart from the inside.*
*Climbing out through the small passage, was the Shah.*
*Following after him, was his daughter Samayra.*
Mythran Prince: *Aah, finally. I was afraid my men would have to break a sweat getting you out of there.*
*Seeing the moment, and how fast things could turn, Sarah nudged Xan, urging him to take action.*
*Xan stepped forward, in between the two warring factions.*
Xanthippe: "Greetings, great prince of Mythran. My name is Xanthippe. I am here on behalf of my order, and I have vowed to safeguard the Bagrad royal family."
Xanthippe: "I would wish to speak with you about a peaceful surrender, one that acknowledges your great victory here, but one that also sees that the royal family will come to no harm."
Xanthippe: "The reputation of your people tells me you are a civilized folk, one that has no love for brutality, so I urge you, allow the royal family dignity in their defeat."
*A pause lingered.*
*The Mythran prince raised one eyebrow.*
Mythran Prince: *What trouble is any of this to your order?*
Xanthippe: "The royal family of Bagrad has been true friends to our order for centuries, and so we wish to facilitate a graceful surrender."
*The Mythran prince laughed, his voice echoing through the vast throne room.*
Mythran Prince: *Where was this concern for protocol and politeness when that decrepit creature stabbed my nephew to death?*
Mythran Prince: *Over what was it, again Shah? A rude comment?*
*The Mythran Prince shook his head.*
Mythran Prince: *No, I think I'll do whatever I want to them, as is my right by conquest. And your order can go back to ignoring whatever else happens in the world.*

*But he had.*
*Sarah knew that a spike was a poor attack, because it took a long time to produce the spell, allowing the other mage to anticipate it.*
*But she also knew that it sliced through most wards, and forced the other mage to actively catch or deflect it.*
*Meaning, that if only for a moment, he had to release his hand from Razaphel.*
*Sarah watched as the spirit leapt up, free from his torture. The thing's mouth opened like a snake, rows and rows of fangs emerging.*
*On Xan's face, she could see that the mage had realized his mistake by the shadow that the spirit now cast over him.*
*Razaphel's mouth clamped shut, the rows of teeth catching Xan by his collarbone.*
*Sarah watched.*
*Xan's entire head was gone, dissapeared into the mouth of the spirit. A muffled scream could be heard emerging from within.*
*She watched as Xan tried to drive the spirit away, flailing his remaining arm with burning magic.*
*But the spirit could tolerate the pain, because it knew victory was near.*
*Sarah watched Xan's body slow down. His flailing turned to twitching, until eventually, even that ceased.*
*With a loud crunch, Razaphel's jaws broke through the last of Xan's resistance, snapping his bones and tearing off his head.*
*Xan's body collapsed to the floor with a solid thud.*
*Sarah forced herself to look at her former mentor. She had caused this, wanted this. What right did she then have to now look away?*
*Blood flowed freely from the stump on Xan's body, splattering the floor in blood. It didn't take long for the blood to darken and stain.*
*Hovering over his body, the spirit.*
Razaphel: "It is done."
*There was little more to say.*
*Sarah had thought she would feel some kind of release, knowing she was free, but the act itself and its brutality had stripped her of that.*
*Still, no matter how deep or far she searched her heart and soul, she found no regret. No secret wish to undo what she had done.*
Sarah: "It is done..."
Sarah: "Now what?"
Razaphel: "Now you have your freedom."
Razaphel: "So the question of now what is one you will have to answer for yourself."
Sarah: "And our deal?"
Razaphel: "Our deal stands. I have fulfilled my end, and one day you will fulfill yours."
*Sarah had imagined the spirit might want her, seize her this very moment, but she understood that was foolish of her to think.*
*The spirit had not risked everything for a chance to have her body. His demand, if it ever came, would be far more costly.*
*Sarah stood up and carefully stepped over the body, avoiding any blood.*
Razaphel: "One advice, Sarah..."
Sarah: "Yes?"
Razaphel: "Take the fate stone and carry it through the house. Hold it up in every corner, and it will shroud the house from the eyes of the gods."
Razaphel: "And perhaps more acutely, shroud it from the mage's order."
*In all the hurry, Sarah had not given much thought to what came after, or whether Xan's order might come after her.*
Sarah: "Do you think they will come for me?"
*The spirit twirled, seeming unconcerned.*
Razaphel: "Perhaps, or perhaps not. Their order is often hard to understand."
Razaphel: "But with the fate stone, you will cut out their most powerful tool, the eyes of the gods."
Razaphel: "Without it, they can find you no easier than any ordinary mortal can. And this house, they will never find."
*This gave Sarah some comfort.*
*The house had been a safe haven for her, and now, it could still be so.*
*Her house, she corrected herself. It all belonged to her now.*
*She left the spirit without further words and did as instructed, carrying the fate stone throughout every room, warding the house.*
*Near the end, exhausted, she returned to her room.*
*Sarah dragged her feet as she walked into her bedroom.*
*The events of only a moment ago now feeling like a strange dream.*
*Only the bruises on her body reminded her it was real.*
*Sarah looked at her bed.*
*Samayra was sound asleep, despite everything.*
*Sarah envied her.*
*Climbing into the bed next to Samayra, Sarah pulled herself closer, allowing herself to feel Samayra's body against her own.*
*She felt Samayra begin to stir, but not quite wake up.*
*Her lithe frame. Her warm body. Her near perfect shape.*
Sarah: "I'm a terrible person."
*Sarah whispered into Samayra's ear.*
*Sarah held onto her, fearing that if she were to let go, she might lose one of the few things that remained to her.*
*As that fear grew, Sarah slowly slipped into a deep sleep.*
*Sarah looked at her bed.*
*Empty.*
*Alone, said a voice in her head.*
*Sarah shook her head and let herself fall into the bed.*
*Sleep.*
*After all of this, she would need a year worth of sleep.*
*Not long after, Sarah slipped into a deep sleep.*
*As Sarah woke to the next day, she found Samayra still asleep.*
*In their sleep, Samayra had twisted herself round and round, until eventually ending up resting her head on Sarah's chest.*
*Sarah didn't object.*
*After a short while, she carefully sneaked out of the bed, leaving Samayra to sleep by herself.*
*Sarah woke to the nex day.*
*The house made no sound.*
*It felt to Sarah as if the silent and empty house judged her, a witness to her crimes.*
*Too awake to stay in bed, Sarah got up.*
*Arriving in the main study room, Sarah slowly let her eyes glide across it.*
*The same.*
*Everything was exactly as they had left it when they set out for Bagrad.*
*The many books. The collection of artifacts. Even Xan's training instructions were still resting where they had been put down.*
*Sarah's eyes fell on Xan's desk.*
*Xan had a habit of drifting around the house. She would find him reading in the oddest of places.*
*But this room, and this desk, this had been the center of his studies, and with it, the center of his world.*
*Sarah had managed to find her own alcoves and rooms in the house, but this room was where they had spend most of their time together.*
*She sighed heavily.*
*Perhaps, Sarah thought, if she had hated Xan all this would have been easier.*
*But she owed him too much to hate him. And so instead, the guilt lingered. The guilt of what she had done to buy herself her freedom.*
*Sarah wandered over towards the desk.*
*Sitting down in Xan's chair, she looked over the many papers and books that were piled up.*
*It looked like a mess, but Sarah had seen him work enough to know there was a method to his madness.*
*Staring out at it now, the pile of documents just seemed like madness.*
*She carefully lifted one piece of paper from the pile and read the title of the document.*
*'A preliminary Analysis on Snow Crystal as an Alchemical Catalyst.'*
*Sarah carefully put the piece of paper back where she had found it. Alchemical research was the last thing she was interested in at the moment.*
*Off to the side, coming from the window, Sarah could see movement.*
*Getting back up, she walked up towards the window and stared out.*
*Outside, Lethram went on as it always had. A bustling of commerce.*
*The house sat upon one of the intersections connecting the wealthier port district with the poorer hill districts.*
*As a result, one could see just about every facet of the city play out from this window.*
*Seeing the city that was as close to her as a home, it oddly soothed her.*
*Yet she was also happy to be inside.*
*A degree of seperation between herself and the real world, now again full of uncertainty.*
*For years, her only mantra had been to listen to Xan and follow his lessons. Now there was nobody to tell her what to do.*
*Sarah knew she wasn't the weak girl from the alley anymore, but she also knew her power, great as it was, could not protect her from everything.*
*Fading into existence from seemingly nowhere, the spirit manifested itself.*
*The blank mask that passed for a face sat upon his inky, black body as it twisted and swirled.*
*After having carried the fate stone through the house, the spirit was now untethered from its flask.*
*Whatever it was worth, it seemed to enjoy its new found freedom.*
Razaphel: "You seem full of worry."
*Sarah kept staring out the window.*
Sarah: "I have a lot to worry about."
Razaphel: "I imagined you would have taken more favorably to your new freedom."
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "What we did to Xan..."
*The spirit rushed forward.*
Razaphel: "Do not concern yourself with the fate of that mage."
Razaphel: "He received not a fraction of what was due to him, consider it mercy."
*Sarah laughed humorlessly.*
Sarah: "Mercy? We killed him."
*For a moment, the spirit was quiet, only observing her. Then it spoke.*
Razaphel: "So, is that what we must do now, Sarah?"
Razaphel: "Must we now perform the sad faces and the spilling of tears, so that we might imagine our conscience clean?"
*The spirit reached out with his tendrils, shaped as claws, seizing her by the shoulders.*
Razaphel: "I will make no apologies for seeking to rid myself of his horrid presence."
Razaphel: "Nor should you make apologies for your part in securing your own freedom."
*Sarah shook her body.*
Sarah: "Let go of me, Razaphel."
*The spirit obliged, slinking back towards its corner.*
Razaphel: "I imagine you might enjoy-"
Sarah: "You imagined wrong. I'm in no mood for anything, least of all that."
Razaphel: "Or perhaps the girl is now the object of your pleasures?"
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Jealous, are we now?"
Razaphel: "Go ahead, mourn that wicked man, your mentor..."
Razaphel: "But if you want, I shall tell you tales of what he did to me."
Razaphel: "His many tortures, seeking to draw out from me my secrets. I wonder, would you think of him the same if you knew?"
*Sarah waved her hand, dismissing him.*
Sarah: "I don't have any illusions about him, but I do owe him for all he taught me."
Sarah: "Without him, I'd still be what I was...lost, powerless."
*Slowly, the spirit emerged back from his corner, drawing closer.*
Razaphel: "Tell me, child of starlight..."
Razaphel: "For what reason have you taken his blood on your hands? What did you hope to gain?"
*Choose*
*Power*:
*For a moment, Sarah considered the words of the spirit.*
*What did she want. Why had she done what she had done.*
*But the answer was obvious to her.*
Sarah: "Power."
*A hissing sound emerged from the creature, the closest it could produce to a laugh.*
Razaphel: "A most surprising answer."
*Sarah turned to face Razaphel.*
Sarah: "Surprising? How?"
Razaphel: "I have come across those who are delirious with lust for power."
Razaphel: "They are more often a simple kind, with simple pleasures."
Razaphel: "I imagined you more complex."
*Sarah shrugged.*
Sarah: "I only gave you the truth. I had no desire to impress you, spirit."
*Freedom*:
*For a moment, Sarah considered the words of the spirit.*
*What did she want. Why had she done what she had done.*
*But the answer was obvious to her.*
Sarah: "Freedom."
*A hissing sound emerged from the creature, the closest it could produce to a laugh.*
Razaphel: "I suspected as much."
*Sarah turned to face Razaphel.*
Sarah: "You thought that would be my answer."
Razaphel: "Yes."
Razaphel: "Ever since you came to this place, I could see it in your eyes."
Razaphel: "This magic, it was but a tool for you. A tool to secure your real ambition, to live on your own accord."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "It's the truth."
Sarah: "Even before I lost everything, I can now see that my life was being dictated by others."
Sarah: "So when Xan threatend to take what little freedom I had managed to procure, away..."
Razaphel: "You had to act."
Razaphel: "I understand, child."
*Sarah sighed deeply and turned back to looking across the room.*
Sarah: "Now what..."
Razaphel: "You want me to answer that for you?"
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "I just...I need to understand what my place is now."
Sarah: "I freed myself from Xan but..."
Razaphel: "You are free to do as you wish, but you fear that you do not yet know what that is..."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "I need to better understand my circumstances. My position."
Razaphel: "Should you wish council, I am available."
*Sarah smiled at the spirit.*
*The truth was that she hardly knew what to make of Razaphel, alien as he was.*
*But she also knew that there were not many people left that could understand her. And Sarah wasn't even sure Razaphel was people.*
Sarah: "Let me ponder it myself for a while."
*The spirit swirled, animated.*
Razaphel: "Go, child, and enjoy your new found freedom."
*With that, the spirit vanished same as it had appeared.*
*Sarah turned back towards the window, continuing to observe the movements of the city.*
*What now, she wondered half in awe, half in fear.*
*The answer did not come to her. Not yet.*
*Sarah had spend most of her day in deep thought.*
*When even the sun had begun to set, and she was no closer to an answer, she had taken to wandering the house.*
*She had spend years in this house, and over the course of it, she had come to know it like a maze.*
*No, she thought.*
*Not quite a maze, for a maze could be mastered and understood.*
*The house, rather, was forever changing and resisting being understood.*
*Rooms would be where they were. Only until they were not.*
*Hallways would have an exact number of doors. Only until it had more.*
*In the first year, Sarah had dedicated significant amounts of her intellect on trying to solve the puzzle that was the house.*
*Only when Xan had told her to give up on it, did she finally relent and accept that the house was beyond her ability to grasp.*
*Still, on occasion, she could not resist pondering the mystery.*
*It was near the end of the night that Sarah came upon a room she had not yet encountered before.*
*The room appeared lived.*
*Exploring through its contents, she found more relics, more writing and more books. Always more books.*
*Looking at the table, she saw a familiar handwriting covering the papers.*
Sarah: "Xan..."
Razaphel: "Aah, I see you've come upon his private study."
*Sarah felt her brow furrow.*
Sarah: "I thought you would have been up to something else by now."
Sarah: "Or did you really work so hard to rid yourself of Xan just so you could torture me?"
Razaphel: "It's a lonely house."
Razaphel: "Either I torture you, or I torture your new friend."
*Sarah snapped towards the spirit.*
Sarah: "You leave her alone, got that?"
Razaphel: "Only jest. We are all friends here."
Razaphel: "It's a lonely house."
Razaphel: "What else is there for me to do?"
*Sarah ignored the spirit's pleading.*
Sarah: "Did you say this was Xan's private study?"
Razaphel: "Yes. He was a man who enjoyed his secrets."
Sarah: "Then how did you know about this place?"
*The spirit swirled around, exploring the corners of the room.*
Razaphel: "He knew you had sympathies for me, and so he carried out his interrogations with me in this place."
Sarah: "interrogations."
Razaphel: "Tortures, to be more exact."
Razaphel: "His magic...your magic. To my kind it feels as flesh pressed against a forge."
*Sarah shivered at the idea.*
Sarah: "I never knew..."
Razaphel: "He did not want you to know, and I did not want to burden you with such knowledge."
Sarah: "Burden me? It was you who he tortured. I would have listened to you..."
Razaphel: "I know you would have, child."
Razaphel: "You would have listened, and cared and you would have pleaded for him to stop."
Razaphel: "But your heart is soft while his was made of iron."
Razaphel: "He would have continued the tortures, and back then, you would have been too weak to stop him."
Razaphel: "And you would have been eaten by the guilt of serving a master so wicked."
Razaphel: "I wanted to spare you such troubles, and so I kept it a secret."
*Sarah felt a deep sadness in her heart, knowing that all these years, she had not even realized this horror.*
*And the spirit, for all that it was, appeared not deserving of such brutality.*
Sarah: "Does this place make you sad?"
*The spirit twirled around in the room for a while. Observing it.*
Razaphel: "It doesn't make me feel much of anything."
Sarah: "It doesn't scare you? It would scare me."
Razaphel: "His tortures were cruel, but he never drew anything from me that mattered, and so I know in the end he only stained his own soul with his crimes."
Razaphel: "Best to forgive and move on."
Sarah: "Now that he is dead?"
Razaphel: "Exactly."
*Sarah sighed and leaned back over the desk.*
*She reached down and grabbed a book that laid atop all the others.*
*Sarah read the title.*
*'The Hollow World'.*
*The tome appeared thick and heavy. The leather binding expensive.*
*Sarah held it in her hand and look up towards Razaphel who spun around like a child through the air.*
Sarah: "Do you have any idea what Xan was working on in here?"
Razaphel: "Nothing I could ever be sure of. Whenever he brought me here, it was he who was asking me the questions."
*She held up the book to him.*
Sarah: "Do you know what this is?"
Razaphel: "I do, but child, you told me you longed to be free."
Razaphel: "It is a waste for a girl of your age to spend her time with dusty old books."
*Sarah continued to hold up the book towards the spirit.*
Sarah: "I thought we were done playing tricks and riddles. Tell me what this book is."
*Razaphel slowly descended down, his mask-face pressed close to the cover of the book.*
Razaphel: "It is the foundational text of their order."
Razaphel: "Written about three millenia ago, after the fall of their empire."
Sarah: "This book is three thousand years old?"
*Sarah struggled to imagine such a thing.*
Razaphel: "No, not this copy. But the text it contains is close enough to the original."
Razaphel: "Perhaps a few minor revisions."
*Sarah placed the book back down and flipped open the cover.*
*Near the start of it, a long itemized index gave hints to the many pages and chapters it contained.*
Sarah: "What is it about?"
*The spirit produced the hissing laugh. Sarah never felt comfortable when it did.*
Razaphel: "You want me for me to summarize this text for you? Impossible."
Sarah: "So you don't know what it is, after all?"
Razaphel: "How do you explain the world to a child?"
Sarah: "Are you calling me stupid?"
*The spirit swirled around.*
Razaphel: "No, Sarah, I do not believe you are foolish. Rather the opposite."
Sarah: "So what then? What is it about?"
Razaphel: "The book is a dense work, written in a different age, based upon principles that stretch back even further."
Razaphel: "If I explain it to you, I can only do so as one explains the world to a child."
Razaphel: "In analogy. In reduction. In simplicity."
Razaphel: "But a child does not know the world when we shrink it down for them, they know only the simplified version."
Razaphel: "If you wish to learn of this book, truly learn it, you must commit yourself to the work that proceeds it."
Razaphel: "To understand this work and what it aims to produce, you must read several volumes that proceed it."
Razaphel: "Sufficiently ground your understanding of the principles at play."
Razaphel: "There exists no simplified version that would not butcher the truth so as to make it meaningless."
*Sarah stepped back and eyed the book.*
Sarah: "Fine, what do I need to read then?"
Razaphel: "Always so eager..."
Razaphel: "I shall prepare a list for you, should you truly be interested."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "Thank you, Razaphel."
*Sarah suddenly felt her body wobble.*
*Only just in time did she grab hold of the back of the chair, keeping herself upright.*
Sarah: "I..."
Razaphel: "You're tired, child."
Sarah: "I think you're right..."
Razaphel: "You don't need to solve all the world's problems in a day. Go, rest Princess."
*Sarah laughed as she moved towards the door.*
Sarah: "I'm not a princess anymore, Razaphel."
*She stumbled through the door. Sarah could not recall how she made her way back to her room, only that she did.*
*Sarah woke early to Samayra still sleeping next to her.*
*Sarah felt guilty for having left Samayra to herself the day before.*
*Next to her, the former princess of Bagrad tossed and turned as if caught in a bad dream.*
*Sarah reached out and softly touched her, shaking her awake.*
*Samayra's eyes shot open and her body jolted.*
*Only when her eyes met Sarah's did she calm down.*
Samayra: "Ooh...Sarah..."
Sarah: "It's ok. You were having a bad dream, I think."
Samayra: "I...I was..."
*Sarah didn't want to press her. She also could imagine, everything the girl had been through, what her nightmare had been about.*
Sarah: "I wanted to say sorry about yesterday. Leaving you alone like that, here in this strange house. I should have taken better care of you."
*Samayra smiled.*
Samayra: "It's ok. Sleeping here with you...it feels kind of safe."
*Sarah was happy to hear she could offer Samayra at least that.*
Sarah: "I promise I'll make it up to you today. We'll go do something fun."
Samayra: "Fun? Like what."
Sarah: "Honestly...I don't know yet. But I'm sure we can figure it out, right?"
*The girl eagerly smiled and nodded.*
Sarah: "Tell me, have you eaten anything since we came here?"
*Embarrassed, Samayra looked down and shook her head.*
Sarah: "Right, well get yourself something to eat and I'll see about if we can do something."
*Sarah made her way towards the door and left the room.*
*Sarah woke to an empty bed, early the next morning.*
*The house had a silence that seemed overwhelming. The kind that pounded on the ears.*
*Sarah sighed to herself, if only to break through the silence.*
*Climbing out of the bed, she tried to think of what to do.*
*There was the matter of the book, but it had only been a day and she had not heard anything from Razaphel.*
*Nor did she particularly care to dig much deeper for the moment.*
*Distraction. That was the real thing she needed right now.*
*Sarah made her way towards the door and left the room.*
*Stepping out into the hallway, Sarah turned her head from side to side, orienting herself.*
*It all still very much looked the same, but even that couldn't necessarily promise that nothing had changed.*
*Suddenly, the spirit manifested itself again.*
Razaphel: "Awake I see."
*Sarah sighed.*
Sarah: "You know, I think we're going to need to find you some friends, because I don't think it's healthy for you to spend all your free time with me."
*The spirit hissed with laughter.*
Razaphel: "You are great fun, Sarah."
Razaphel: "Perhaps if you are bored of talking, there are other things we could do."
*Sarah rolled her eyes.*
Sarah: "How about you help me instead."
Razaphel: "Any particular matter?"
*Sarah looked across the hallway.*
Sarah: "Suppose..."
*She paused to consider.*
Sarah: "Suppose someone wanted to do something...to just...relax?"
*The spirit swirled across the hall, its body bellowing like smoke from a chimney.*
Razaphel: "Such simple desires."
*Sarah shrugged.*
Sarah: "I am only human, hard as that may be for you to remember. Everyone needs a break sometimes."
*The spirit twisted through the air a moment longer, before finally answering.*
Razaphel: "This house is accommodating to your desires."
Razaphel: "Should you find yourself in need of a thing, all you must do is will it sufficiently and truthfully, and it will deliver."
*For a moment, Sarah was happy to hear the answer and prepared to turn and leave, only for to realize the insanity of it.*
*She turned back towards Razaphel.*
Sarah: "You...you say the house gives me what I want?"
Razaphel: "Yes, to an extent."
Razaphel: "Surely this cannot surprise you too much, you have known the house to shift and alter itself."
Razaphel: "To be larger within than without."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "I knew it wasn't a normal house, I figured that out years ago...but I figured it was just...magic."
Sarah: "That it was Xan who was doing it."
*The spirit flinched at the mention of the mage's name.*
Razaphel: "No. The house moved to the mage's will, but it was not his doing."
*Sarah frowned her brow, trying to make sense of it.*
Sarah: "What then? What is this house, exactly?"
*Razaphel spun and brought its face-mask close to Sarah's face.*
*Its inscrutable features made it hard to ever know what the spirit was truly thinking.*
Razaphel: "Are you familiar with a river-rock-crab?"
*Sarah was surprised to hear those words coming from the spirit.*
Sarah: "I...of course I am. I'm from Rosanna, they're everywhere. You can find them in just about every river."
Razaphel: "Exactly."
Razaphel: "And can you tell me...why they are called as such?"
*Sarah frowned.*
Sarah: "Well...their shell is grey, like the pebbels founds by the side of the river. So they kind of look like rocks."
*The spirit's body slowly twisted and floated through the hall, turning thin as mist.*
Razaphel: "Yes, that is correct."
Razaphel: "Now tell me this. Is a river-rock-crab a crab, or a rock?"
*Sarah was confused at the question, but decided to play along.*
Sarah: "It's a crab, obviously."
Razaphel: "Correct."
Razaphel: "But tell me, why is it not a rock?"
*Again, Sarah was confused, but she continued.*
Sarah: "Just because it looks like a rock, doesn't mean it is a rock. It's basic camouflage."
Razaphel: "And there you have your answer."
*Sarah looked confused at the spirit and considered his words.*
*Then, they struck her like lightining.*
Sarah: "A...a...are you suggesting...this house..."
Razaphel: "Is not a house."
Sarah: "But-"
Razaphel: "It looks like one, but it is not a house. Not really."
Razaphel: "In fact, it is quite similar to the river-rock-crabs, but perhaps only its methods are more...advanced."
*Sarah suddenly felt her body shiver, the whole of the house...*
Sarah: "So you're saying we're..."
Sarah: "Standing in the insides of a creature?"
*The thought alone was enough to strike terror in her.*
Sarah: "No...that's impossible!"
Sarah: "There is no creature in the world that can do something like this."
Razaphel: "That is true, but this particular creature is not from your world or mine. Some other place altogether."
Sarah: "Where?"
Razaphel: "I do not know. Even I do not hold all the answers."
Razaphel: "All I know is that by some unfortunate circumstance, centuries by now, this creature found itself trapped in our reality."
Razaphel: "Exposed to a hostile world, it did what most animals would do. It hid itself."
*Sarah stared at every part of the building, suddenly horrified at it.*
Sarah: "How did it come to be here?"
Razaphel: "I believe in time it was discovered by the mage order, more observant than most ordinary people."
Razaphel: "They found the creature, and fearing for its life still, it threw itself on their mercy."
Razaphel: "And as you might imagine, the creature was happy to serve its new masters if it meant its survival."
Sarah: "And Xan was his master?"
Razaphel: "He was the most powerful thing in this house, and so the creature bend itself to his mercy."
*For a moment the spirit paused.*
Razaphel: "But, with that mage gone, I suspect that his favor now falls on you."
*Sarah looked at Razaphel, stunned.*
Sarah: "You mean...it's afraid of me?"
Razaphel: "Afraid. Or perhaps merely playing on your good nature."
Razaphel: "I suspect that is also why you suddenly were able to find Xan's private study."
Razaphel: "Before, the house hid the room because its master did not want you to find it."
Razaphel: "Then, after the mage was gone, the house knew you were searching for something, and it offered it to you."
*Sarah felt the stress grow in her body.*
Sarah: "I..."
Sarah: "But I never said I was looking for that room."
Razaphel: "No, but wherever this creature is from, the barriers of thoughts are not as...seperate as in your world or mine."
*Sarah looked around frantically for any sight of the creature, but found only the house.*
Sarah: "You mean it can read my mind?"
Razaphel: "Not quite so direct, I suspect. I believe instead he merely feels your mind. Feels your intentions."
Razaphel: "And in turn, he proceeds you, delivers that which it knows you seek. Like a cat, delivering a mouse to its master."
Sarah: "Unbelievable..."
*Sarah was quite for a while as she considered.*
*It was a horrifying thought, that this house was in fact a living thing, but at the same time, the more she thought, the more it appeared to her as a powerful ally.*
Sarah: "Can I trust it? The house?"
Razaphel: "You can trust it to do what it has done for centuries. Survive."
Razaphel: "If you give it what it wants, it will return the favor. It possess few desires outside of that base instinct, from what I have been able to deduce."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "Fine...I think I understand then."
Razaphel: "Very well, then I shall part ways with you. Other affairs to see to."
Sarah: "You have other affairs?"
Razaphel: "Maybe I'm going to look for new friends, as my old friends have advised me."
*Just like that, the spirit faded away.*
*Sarah doubted she would ever manage to get the spirit to stop being obtuse.*

*Choose*
*What is the hollow world?*
