*Sarah only breathed heavily, recovering from the beast's urges and desires.*
*A swift strike across her face, her ears ringing from the blow.*
*Sarah could feel tears building in her eyes.*
Master: *I will not keep teaching you forever. Address me as you must, or you will suffer far worse.*
*Sarah swallowed her pride.*
Sarah: "Yes...Master..."
*Sarah felt the creature's claws weaving through her hair.*
*Forcefully, and yet with seemingly no effort at all, the creature pulled her up to her feet.*
*He threw her forward, and Sarah stumbled.*
*As the creature neared her again, Sarah threw up her hands.*
*Without effort, he swatted them away.*
*Its claw clenching down around her throat again, it produced a metal ring with its other hand.*
*Before she could manage, the circlet was placed around her throat.*
*Running tight around her neck, Sarah could feel the iron of it press against her throat with every breath.*
Master: *You are new to this world.*
Master: *In time, you will learn. This is why I am so kind to you for now.*
Master: *But when you defy my, you offer no real resistance. You only invite my punishment. Do you understand, slave?*
*Sarah tried to speak through her choked throat.*
Sarah: "Yes...Master..."
*The creature released her.*
*It grinned.*
Master: *Good, you are learning.*
*It moved past her, along the sharp rocks of the alien world.*
Master: *Follow me, do not tread slowly or you will bear the whip for that too.*
*Burning heat searing her body. Pain still ringing inside of her.*
*Despite it all, Sarah forced herself to walk after the creature.*
*Master. The word alone made her shiver.*
*The rocks cut into the soles of her feet with every step. A reminder of this new and wicked place.*
*For now, this is where the story ends.*
*Ignore the voice*:
Sarah: "Get away from me!"
Sarah: "Whatever you are, get away!"
*Sarah nearly screamed the words.*
*The voice went silent, and a moment later, she saw Metis emerge.*
Metis: "Sarah!!!"
*A panicked expression on his face.*
Sarah: "I...was that...who was that?"
Metis: "What are you talking about? I just...you dissapeared, I was searching for you, but you vanished!"
Sarah: "A voice...a voice reached out to me and it..."
Metis: "Ooh Gods, tell me you didn't follow it."
*Sarah shook her head.*
Sarah: "No, I didn't."
Metis: "Gods, you have no idea how lucky you got."
Metis: "Some creature was haunting you, searching you out. If you had followed that voice...I don't even want to imagine."
*Sarah felt a shiver move past her spine.*
*A thing...preying on her. A thing she could not even conceive of. A thing from a different world.*
*Daemonology was truly a dangerous Art.*
Metis: "Well, you managed to avoid it. Good. Remember that. Do not let their voices seduce you, no matter what they promise."
*Sarah shivered, her body still transfixed in the Trance.*
*All around her, she could feel the faintest vibrations. What caused them. Were they creatures like the one that had spoken to her?*
*She suddenly felt Metis' hand on her shoulder.*
Metis: "Don't worry, Sarah."
Metis: "This Art is dangerous, but you are gifted. The rewards will be worth it in the end."
Metis: "Stay focussed. Do not waver. You can do this."
*Sarah looked into his eyes. His concern for her seemed genuine, and for whatever else, Sarah found herself calming down.*
*She nodded.*
Sarah: "Thank you, Metis."
Metis: "Alright, let's keep moving. You don't want to remain in this Trance any longer than you need to."
Metis: "The longer you stay here, the more...things can notice you."
Metis: "Bring you mind back to Laitha."
*Sarah repeated the name in her word over and over again and slowly found herself return to that place.*
*Below her, the lush jungles, sprawling with life.*
Sarah: "I can see it...the world..."
Metis: "Good."
Metis: "Now we will need to see if you can pull something into our world."
Sarah: "Won't that be...dangerous?"
Metis: "Depending on what you drag over, yes. Intelligent creatures are the most dangerous, because they can reach back int you."
Metis: "Large, monsterous creatures are also dangerous, because you never know if you lose control over them when you draw them in."
Metis: "But there are also creatures that are more...amicable to control."
Sarah: "Such as?"
*Metis pointed with his finger.*
*Looking in the direction, Sarah saw a large horde of creatures she had never seen before in her life.*
*They stood, all together, on a massive field of grass, more like an ocean.*
*Chewing. Eating. Playing.*
*If ever there seemed to be a simple, harmless creature, this must surely have been it.*
Metis: "Those are herbivores, won't harm a fly. And they're none too bright, so not very dangerous at all."
*Sarah studied them a moment longer.*
Sarah: "What...do I do?"
*Metis looked at her.*
Metis: "Well, Sarah, not so different from what the other creature tried to do when it spoke to you."
Metis: "Speak, make it listen, and draw it in."
Sarah: "Speak? But how? I can't speak its language. I barely know what it is."
Metis: "Do you need to know a dog's language to communicate with it? No. Same goes for this creature."
Metis: "Reach out and speak to it in a way that it might understand, and lure it."
*Sarah studied the herd, and finally picked out a target.*
*Small enough that it appeared even more harmless.*
*Drawing from within, she began to speak to the creature.*
*At first, it was as if nothing happened at all.*
*The creature, along with the rest of its herd, grazed from the grass, uncaring.*
*Again and again, Sarah repeated the words. All to the same result.*
*But slowly, memories of her youth came over her.*
*The cats that wandered Castle Reinmeer, especially near the kitchen.*
*How she had begged her father for one, only to be rebuked each time.*
*How she had slowly learned to lure the cats to herself, not with words so much as sounds.*
*She began to imitate her younger self.*
*Making a high-pitched sound with her tongue, she found the creature suddenly reacting to her.*
*The only one among the herd now not grazing.*
*The creature looked around to a sound only it had heard.*
*Sarah repeated the sound. Again. Again.*
*Slowly, the creature began to walk, moving, reacting to her. It wandered a small distance from the herd.*
Metis: "Now, reach out and seize on it."
*On some level, Sarah had no idea what Metis meant by seizing on 'it', and yet, on another level, she knew exactly what he meant.*
*Sarah could feel a bond with the creature.*
*Her attention on it. Its attention on her.*
*In her mind, she took hold of the bond as though it were a rope, and with one strong pull, she yanked the creature towards her.*
*Her eyes suddenly shooting open, Sarah realized she was standing in the middle of the room.*
*The room she had never left.*
*In front of her, Metis, but perhaps more importantly...the creature.*
*Seen only in her Trance, she now saw the creature in full.*
*Bigger than she had at first imagined. Its smell. The sounds. Every facet of the thing was suddenly real.*
*The creature, equally confused, seemed to stare around the room for a moment, disbelieving its situation.*
Metis: "Be very calm now or..."
*Sarah reached out with one hand.*
*The creature stormed off.*
*Trapped in the room, the creature could not escape, but trapped in emotion, it could neither calm down.*
*Instead, it raged and stormed through the room.*
*Its herbivore nature meant that attacking either of them was unthinkable, yet a few times it nearly slammed into them in panic.*
Sarah: "Hey! Calm down!"
*Words meant little to the creature.*
*Metis only chuckled, seemingly amused by the chaos.*
Metis: "You're gonna have to wrestle it."
Sarah: "What? Are you crazy?"
Metis: "Well, that or let it rage till its tired, but Gods know what it's going to knock over. Or if it manages to break through a door."
*Sarah sighed.*
*When the creature made another lap through the room, passing close to Sarah and Metis, she made her move.*
*Leaping forward, Sarah jumped on the creature.*
*Her body weight alone was enough to slow the creature down significantly.*
*Wrapping her arms around its belly, she slowly managed to grind the creature down.*
Sarah: "Hey! We're not gonna hurt you!"
*Sarah kept repeating it, and over time, the creature seemed to even begin to believe her.*
*Its rage and panic subsided as it realized it was caught in Sarah's grip, but suffered no wounds.*
*Eventually, Sarah found herself sitting on the ground, the animal in her grip.*
*By now, she no longer felt it struggle, only its belly rising and falling with every breath.*
*Sarah slowly began to pat the creature's slimy back.*
Sarah: "There, there."
*She looked up at Metis.*
Sarah: "Now what?"
*Metis shrugged.*
Metis: "Official Order regulation says trans-dimensional creatures should be exterminated after study."
*Sarah felt her eyes go wide with shock.*
*Metis waved his hands.*
Metis: "Don't worry, I don't much care for rules like that. You can keep it if you like. They're not really dangerous."
*Sarah continued to pet the creature, which seemed increasingly comfortable.*
Metis: "Xan is a little different about such things, but I guess you'll have to fight that out with him."
*Sarah nodded absently.*
Sarah: "Yeah..."
Metis: "Anyway, you take care of all this. I left some more books for you to study up on on the table over there."
*Metis vaguely gestured towards the other side of the room.*
Sarah: "What? You're leaving me here with this thing?"
*Metis chuckled.*
Metis: "Well, it's yours isn't it?"
*Sarah watched as Metis walked away, still laughing at his own remark.*
*She turned her attention back to the creature.*
Sarah: "What am I gonna end up calling you, huh?"
*She saw the creature shake, demanding her to continue patting it.*
*Sarah did as the creature wanted.*
Sarah: "You got any ideas on a name?"
*The creature just looked back at her, confused.*
Sarah: "Nice talking to you."
*She patted the creature's back, and it seemed to excitedly nestle itself into her.*
*Sarah realized she wasn't getting away any time soon.*
*It was would be at least several hours before she finally managed to get out from under the creature and find it a place to live.*
*As always, the house had provided.*
*Sarah walked back to her room, books under her arm, beyond exhausted.*
*Sarah had woken early the next day.*
*She had quietly sneaked out of bed, leaving Samayra to get a few extra hours of sleep.*
*The girl needed it, she had seemed exhausted these last few weeks.*
*She sat behind her desk, looking out over the pile of work that she had somehow managed to attract.*
*Books from Metis. Books from Razaphel. Books for her own study. Practicing magic.*
*When she added it all up in her head, it seemed like a mountain.*
*And yet, climbing a mountain required a first step, and so Sarah found herself pressing herself to the work.*
*Like a blade to a whetstone, she could feel herself sharpening.*
*She hadn't long begun when she suddenly heard a noise.*
*Metis entered the room.*
*Sarah could see something was different about him. It took her a moment to realize the packed bags near his feet.*
Sarah: "You're leaving?"
*Sarah was surprised at the fact that she found herself shocked.*
*It wasn't that long ago that she would have gladly pushed him out onto the street.*
*Metis nodded.*
Metis: "Yeah, the ship I chartered came in a few weeks early."
Metis: "I know I promised to train you for longer, but the truth is I have my own work to see to."
Metis: "Now with the ship coming in early, it means I can get where I need to go faster."
*Sarah looked at him from across the desk.*
Sarah: "And where is that?"
*Metis chuckled.*
Metis: "Keep asking questions, I like that about you."
*A reply, but not an answer.*
Metis: "Tell you what, if I get back we can pick up on the lessons. In between, keep studying and practice. But don't go pushing yourself."
*Sarah noticed he was quickly changing the subject from where he was going, back to her lessons.*
*She could press him, but she also knew there was a reason he wasn't answering.*
*Also, she doubted he'd be tripped up by her asking him more questions.*
Sarah: "Well, I think I'll be sad to see you leave."
Sarah: "And I don't think I'll be the only one. Samayra was happy for the company."
*Metis chuckled.*
Metis: "She's a good kid. I think she's lucky to have you for a friend."
*He looked around to see if there was anyone else around.*
Metis: "I heard she had a surprise for you."
Sarah: "A surprise?"
Metis: "Please, don't pull it out of me. I vowed to keep quiet about it. She made me swear on the Gods and everything."
*Sarah frowned. She wasn't much for surprises.*
Metis: "Tell her I said goodbye, I regret not being able to do it properly."
*Sarah nodded.*
Sarah: "I'll tell her."
*Metis sighed and picked up his bags.*
Metis: "Well, I'm sad to see our encounter cut so short, but I'm sure we will meet again."
*Sarah looked at him intently. Had he ever discovered or suspected anything related to Xan?*
*If he had, he still gave no hint of it.*
Metis: "Tell me, if you ever see that weird little spirit, can you tell him I said hello?"
Sarah: "Razaphel never came to see you?"
*Metis shrugged.*
Metis: "Who is to speculate on the mind of such a creature. I only worry myself about the questions that can actually be answered."
*Metis chuckled again, amused with himself.*
*He made a motion for the door before suddenly stopping.*
Metis: "Aah, I almost forgot!"
Metis: "Honestly, it's like my husband always says, if my head wasn't attached to me I'd lose it."
*Sarah frowned. Husband?*
*Metis closed the distance between them, standing on the opposite side of the desk.*
*He reached into his pocket and produced a letter.*
*Casually, he threw it onto the desk.*
Metis: "When Xan comes back, can you give him that?"
Metis: "I had hoped to speak with him directly, but now with the ship and all that...it's too much trouble and I'd rather it didn't wait."
Metis: "Just hand him that and I guess that will have to do. I've written it all down in there."
*Sarah held the letter in her hand. A wax seal sat atop it, keeping it closed.*
Sarah: "Is this going to explode if it accidentally opens up?"
*Metis raised one eyebrow.*
Metis: "It's just a letter Sarah. Not everything is magic."
*He turned and walked towards the door, turning just before leaving.*
Metis: "Stay safe, Sarah. Dangerous times out there."
*Sarah looked at him, unsure of what to make of his remark.*
*She nodded.*
Sarah: "You stay safe as well. And you're always welcome here."
*Metis smiled, but said nothing.*
*He gave her one last short wave and then stepped out through the door.*
*Sarah watched through the window has he made his way to the harbor.*
*Towards his ship that would take him...wherever it was.*
*Sarah considered the man for a moment longer.*
*Appearing out of nowhere. Acting too familiar.*
*On the other hand, he seemed friendly enough and even decided to teach her.*
*Was he send here to spy? Just an accidental visit?*
*Sarah sighed. She was no closer to an answer than when she had first met him.*
*Whatever else it was, he was gone now.*
*That gave her time. Space. To think.*
*Sitting in the chair, Sarah felt her eyes slowly glide towards the desk.*
*Towards the letter on top of everything else.*
*A green wax seal covered the front.*
*She held it in her hand, passing it from one to the other, as if hoping to divine the content by weight.*
*A letter of Xan, from Metis. Explaining what he had come here to tell him in the first place...*
*She had to open it. To know...to understand...*
*Still, a part of her was hesitant. It was an ordinary letter, she felt no magical energy coming from it.*
*And still some part of her was always like that...hestitant.*
*She threw the letter back on top of the desk.*
*Whatever it was, it could wait. At least until she was sure Metis was on his ship and heading out the city.*
*She had only just thrown the letter back when she heard a noise.*
*Soft, like a mouse.*
Sarah: "I can hear you."
*Samayra stuck her head around the corner, smiling.*
Samayra: "You caught me."
*Samayra stepped into the room properly and frowned.*
Samayra: "How do you manage to hear me anway? Servants used to be scared of me because they didn't hear me walk up on them."
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "The sneaking monster of Bagrad, Samayra-the-terrible."
Sarah: "But honestly, I just had a lot of practice. Thomas used to be like you. Always walking so softly."
Sarah: "You spend years keeping your ears out for it, I guess you develop a talent."
*Samayra walked further into the room, leaning across the desk.*
Samayra: "Have you seen Metis?"
Sarah: "He just left actually. Only a few minutes ago."
*Samayra frowned.*
Samayra: "Really? He didn't even say goodbye...he was supposed to help me."
Sarah: "He asked me to tell you that he said goodbye."
*Sarah frowned.*
Sarah: "And help you with what...exactly?"
*Samayra's face turned into a wide grin.*
Samayra: "I got a surprise for you!"
Sarah: "Have I ever told you I hate surprises?"
*Samayra rolled her eyes.*
Samayra: "Ugh, don't be so dour. I practiced really hard on this!"
*Sarah looked at the girl, confused.*
Sarah: "Practiced what?"
Samayra: "Just look!"
*Samayra jumped back into the center of the room.*
*She held out her hand.*
*Sarah leaned forward, looking intently.*
*She felt it before she saw it.*
*A shift in the magical energy.*
*The energy in the room condensed into the palm of Samayra's hand.*
*Forming out of nothingness, a small pale blue flame emerged.*
*Slowly, the flame grew, wrapping itself harmlessly around the girl's hands.*
*The magical fire cast a blue-ish hue over the room.*
*And above all.*
*The girl was crowned in starlight.*
*Sarah was stunned at the sight.*
*Samayra was doing magic, however simplistic...she was doing it.*
Sarah: "How...how are you...doing this..."
*She saw past the fire, Samayra's wide smile.*
Samayra: "Awesome, isn't it?!"
Samayra: "I mean, you thought that I might be able to do it, so...I mean I asked Metis!"
Samayra: "You were so busy that you didn't always have time for me, so I thought Metis could help me out."
Samayra: "And he did!"
Samayra: "He showed me all the basics, and at first I thought I was terrible at it, I could not do it at all!"
Samayra: "I was just waving my hands like I was silly, but then it just clicked!"
Samayra: "And now..."
*Samayra moved her hand, the flame following along.*
Samayra: "See! I can actually do it!"
Samayra: "I'm a mage, like you!"
*Sarah saw the girl's face twist into embarrassment.*
Samayra: "I mean...well...not like you, of course, you're way better, but you know..."
*Sarah jumped up from her chair.*
Sarah: "Samayra! This is amazing!"
*She saw Samayra's face turn back into that beaming smile.*
Samayra: "Really? You really think so?"
*Sarah nodded. She meant every word of it.*
Sarah: "Yeah...you learned this so fast!"
*Samayra was turning red from the praise.*
Samayra: "I mean...without Metis I wouldn't have managed...but..."
*Sarah snuffed out the flame from Samayra's palm, a trivial effort for her.*
*Then she rushed forward and caught the girl in an embrace.*
*Sarah was far from the strongest, but even to her, lifting Samayra off the ground and spinning her proved hardly difficult.*
*Samayra shrieked as Sarah spun her around, before finally putting her back down.*
Sarah: "Wow...we're going to do amazing things together. I just know it."
*Samayra smiled at her. Her piercing eyes cutting into Sarah's.*
Samayra: "So..."
Samayra: "If Metis left...I guess I don't have a teacher anymore."
*The girl slightly paused before asking the question Sarah was expecting.*
Samayra: "Would you want to be my teacher?"
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Of course, you don't even have to ask."
*For the rest of the day, Sarah spend it with Samayra.*
*The girl told her how she had followed her lessons in secret.*
*How Metis had taken her through all the basics steps, how she had struggled, and how she had finally managed it.*
*Her magic wasn't much, but it was a spark, and that was all that was needed to grow.*
*So lost in this surprise, Sarah all but forgot about the letter for most of that day.*
*Instead, she looked on in awe at what Samayra was. What she was becoming.*
*Sarah decided to distract herself with the one thing that always worked. Work.*
*Late at night, Sarah returned to her desk.*
*The letter sat where it had been left behind.*
*She had not been able to put off opening it much longer.*
*Her hand trembled as she fished it off the table.*
*She held it in her hands as if even a slight touch could ruin it.*
*Sarah gathered her strength and then finally ripped open the letter.*
*As expected, there were only a few pages inside, nothing more.*
*Scrawled out across the surface, Metis' handwriting.*
*Sarah began to read.*
Metis: "Dear Xan, I write you this letter because I fear that our paths did not cross."
Metis: "When you are reading this, I will already be well on my way towards the Isles of Karpath."
Metis: "I still remember the days we had spend on that beach, the ruins."
Metis: "You were guarded of me back then, but I must return there now."
Metis: "Not merely for the memories."
Metis: "I wish that I could speak more to you, but I find these days that most everyone in the Order has become a gossip."
Metis: "Perhaps they were always like that."
Metis: "Regardless, I can speak more on the matter when we meet. Truly meet."
Metis: "The reason for leaving you this letter however, has nothing to do with my travel plans."
Metis: "Rather, there is a matter that I had been hoping to look into further, but I find myself struggling for time."
Metis: "Included with this letter you will find a report submitted by an acolyte from the Order."
Metis: "She analyzed magical paterns from one of our measuring stations deep in the Mythran heartland."
Metis: "It describes an anomaly, produced by rhythmic magical pulses, eminating from the further North."
Metis: "This station lies close to the Mythran border with the jungles of Nephatim."
Metis: "As you are well aware, more than most even, this leaves few real potential sources for the origin of this signal."
Metis: "Varany. The oldest city."
Metis: "The Order has left the city to its ruins, and rightly so. For millenia it was silent."
Metis: "But you have perhaps infected me with your paranoia, and I cannot help but wander...what if."
Metis: "Our Order holds a near singular grip on magic in the world."
Metis: "The jungle Tribes have shown no aptitude or interest in it."
Metis: "So what then?"
Metis: "I fear I have no more of an answer to that question than you likely do."
Metis: "However, you do possess a singular advantage. The House."
Metis: "It was my intention to discuss with you an expedition to Varany, even though I am well aware of your position."
Metis: "For the time being, I would ask that you consider the matter."
Metis: "When next we meet, I hope we can continue this discussion."
Metis: "I look forward to your opinion on the matter, as always."
Metis: "Your loyal student and more, Metis."
*Sarah placed the letter back down on the desk.*
*She tried processing its contents.*
*Even now, she had no idea what to make of Metis...was this all trap? Had he left her the letter on purpose, knowing her curiosity would get to her?*
*No, thought Sarah.*
*He was a poweful mage in his own right. If he suspected anything, why would he have need of tricks?*
*So what then...*
*She kept turning the letter about in her hand.*
*Varany. The oldest city. The first city of Men, before the world had collapsed by the incursion of the world beyond.*
*Where the Empress had forged two worlds into one...*
*Xan had told her stories from that place. And if she could believe it, he had even walked that city at its peak.*
*And now the mysterious letter, speaking of unexplained phenomena...*
*Sarah knew what she had to, despite the danger of it.*
*Metis' arrival had reminded her of one fact. The world, even if she might ignore it, would still be out there.*
*She could not hide away in this place forever.*
*Sarah began to pack swiftly, but in truth, she travelled light.*
*In only a few hours, she stood ready to depart.*
*Samayra came to see her off.*
Samayra: "So...I guess you're leaving again."
*Sarah nodded.*
Samayra: "I'll...miss you."
*Sarah turned her head.*
Sarah: "Why is that?"
Samayra: "Well...I don't know when you'll be back."
Sarah: "So?"
*A brief pause.*
Sarah: "You're coming with me, aren't you?"
*Sarah saw Samayra's face go wide.*
*Then the girl leapt forward and hugged her.*
Samayra: "Sarah! Really! Can I come?"
*Sarah laughed as she tried to hold Samayra off.*
Sarah: "Well, I mean...you know some magic right?"
Sarah: "I can use all the help that I can."
Samayra: "Ooh! Sarah, I promise I won't be a burden, I promise!"
*Sarah smiled as she handed Samayra a bag of her own.*
*In her heart, she worried.*
*Was the girl really ready for this? It would be safer to keep her here...*
*But Sarah knew that this was impossible.*
*She could not keep Samayra locked up in this house forever.*
*And even when she had kept her here, Metis had made his way into the house.*
*The truth was that Samayra was only truly safe besides Sarah.*
Sarah: "Well...I'll be strict on you! Just as my teacher was!"
*Samayra nodded, smiling.*
Samayra: "And I'll be strong...just like you are!"
*Sarah laughed.*
Sarah: "Okay, well, rule number one, don't be a kiss-ass."
*Samayra stuck out her tongue as she flung the bag across her back.*
*Sarah saw that they were ready.*
*She had the benefit of the House.*
Sarah: "I require a portal to Varany!"
*Sarah declared it as loudly and as firmly as she could.*
*Then she pulled upon a door.*
*Before them, the swirling magical energies revealed the jungles of the Oldest City.*
*With trembling hands, Sarah forced herself to be brave.*
*Then she felt Samayra's hand on hers.*
*She looked into the smiling face of the girl, and her heart steadied.*
Sarah: "Together."
Samayra: "Together."
*They each took one step and crossed a million.*
*Sarah began to pack swiftly, but in truth, she travelled light.*
*In only a few hours, she stood ready to depart.*
*She had the benefit of the House.*
Sarah: "I require a portal to Varany!"
*Sarah declared it as loudly and as firmly as she could.*
*Then she pulled upon a door.*
*Before her, the swirling magical energies revealed the jungles of the Oldest City.*
*With trembling hands, Sarah forced herself to be brave.*
*She took one step and crossed a million.*
